title: Titanium limbs: Life-changing engineering meets anatomy
summary:
Like a bolt out of the blue, Mark Jonkers’ life was shattered, the last thing he remembers was being parked at a 4-way stop in Somerset West. He woke to a shattered pelvis and in excruciating pain which never went away for the next 18 months, he was trapped in a wheelchair and at the age of 37 was told he would never walk again. But thanks to the incredible combined skills of mechanical engineer Dr George Vicatos and orthopaedic surgeon Dr Andre Olivier the pain is gone and Mark is walking and dedicating his life to changing kids’ lives. Mark's previous surgeon spent months sending his scans to many different international prosthesis manufacturers and every solution they came up with was too risky, then he was referred to Dr Andre Olivier and four weeks later he had a new pelvis and hip. Today he is walking and the pain has gone, along with the 22 screws that were holding him together after the initial emergency surgery. The complex thing about a pelvis is because it is the weight-bearing centre of our bodies to which our limbs are anchored, you can’t just add modular pieces, it has to be a solid structure that mirrors your exact pelvis. Technological advancements in computer design and 3D manufacturing with advanced medical scans all married together with highly skilled surgeons, has put South Africa on the world stage of medical science.

Engineering meets anatomy when you say Dr George Vicatos - his state-of-the-art limb designs are changing lives and his international claim to fame is that he made the largest ever implant worldwide. Every person’s pelvis is a unique design and shape and when you need a replacement you can't pick a modular pelvis designed off the shelf. George designs precision replicas of your unique bone structure which is 3D printed with medical titanium in a state-of-the-art unit in Bloemfontein Technicon at the Centre of Rapid Prototyping and Manufacturing (CRPM). It’s a good news story with top South African surgeons working closely with the designers and academics making life-changing surgery available to South Africans at one third of the price and in half the manufacturing time, and Vicatos ensures he attends every surgery.. The day before the surgery he sits with the doctor and a nylon replica of the implant making any last-minute adjustments. Vicatos really takes to heart the enormity of the life-changing surgery for every patients. The best news is that the Medical Aids are on board.

title: Rhino IVF
oneLiner: Cutting edge science to save a species on the brink of extinction
summary:
Experience and research show rhinos in captivity often develop menopause or premature reproductive problems; and siblings or groups of similar age don't stimulate each other. This means rescued orphan rhinos don't naturally reproduce. At Thaba Manzi, there is a group of 5 orphans that failed to conceive for 3 years. Enter Dr de la Rey. He's performed procedures on these rhinos including hormone stimulation, removal of cysts and follicles - and helped all of them conceive. Today, some of their babies are falling pregnant, showing promise for population growth. This is just the beginning. Last year, De la Rey's team performed the world's first progesterone synchronised artificial insemination. On farms, rhino can be regularly herded up and scanned to check where in their natural cycle they are, then injected with semen. But in the wild, this is more difficult and it’s desirable to be able to fertilize all the females at the same time. So they insert a progesterone device to bring the females onto their cycle. They can then be injected with the semen at a time when pregnancy will be likely. This allows genetic variation to be injected into a wild population without the stress, risk and cost of bringing a bull into a population with no guarantee of success. De la Rey can also scan for pregnancy, telling the foetus's age more accurately than lab progesterone tests. This is essential because pregnant females are transported to help repopulate reserves, but if pregnancy is too advanced they abort or give birth prematurely. With this method, transport is cheaper, kinder and more successful. The next step is IVF. De la Rey estimates he will have the first southern white rhino IVF babies by November this year.

The team that brought us Africa's first cloned animal in 2003 is bringing cutting edge fertility science to bear on the problem of wildlife populations under threat. Dr Morne de la Rey of Embryo Plus was also the first to bring an IVF buffalo into the world in 2016. Since 2017 he has been focusing his efforts on rhino, which do not breed successfully in captivity and are under lethal pressure in the wild. Using hormone stimulation, artificial insemination and even IVF, Dr de la Rey is hoping to help captive species of rhino breed at a rate that can combat the losses in the wild. He has already had considerable success.

title: SAP: DIRTY MONEY
oneLiner: We all blame the Guptas for the mess we're left with, but what about the lives they ruined - we speak exclusively to a man who stood between them and 100 million in alleged kickbacks.
summary:
In SAPs world, commission agreements are not unusual. Except in this case Transnet was already a client of SAP and the commission agreement with CAD House made it clear SAP was not so much as a sales agent to market a product to Transnet as a fixer to clinch the deal. IN EARLY 2016 SAP’S INTERNAL MEMOS ACKNOWLEDGED THAT ITS GLOBAL PRACTICE OF PAYING “BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT PARTNERS” TO SECURE DEALS - WAS FRAUGHT WITH RISK OF CORRUPTION. CAD House’s “main purpose”, it specified, “is to assist [SAP] in obtaining Customer consent to the Customer Contract and Customer’s requisite signatures to such agreement”. In the audio interview with SAP they say: “We were doing a proof of concept and CAD house was an existing vendor at Transnet and we were looking at doing 3D models for these guys to show them the value and the benefit of using our solution… The deal…" But what makes SAPs claims more awkward is the fact that Transnet deny it had any relationship with CAD house whatsoever. AND CADhouse says they never made 3d models of traing, and if they had, at most it would have been R50,000 job. Not 100 million rand. He will also tell us how despite SAP claiming due diligence was done, it wasn't. They never even met him. SAPs initial due diligence report never mentioned the Guptas - which is strange considering a simple consumer search would have shown their ownership - and a google search would have been peppered with words like “corruption.” However, no red flags were raised. The first Transnet contract SAP was awarded was R114 million… of which R17 million was paid into CAD house’s account… that money was then moved into a Gupta entity.

When you look at our State Owned Enterprises today, after several years of ‘Gupta Capture,’ you realize they were Ground Zero for brothers Ajay, Atul and Rajesh who leveraged their close proximity to then-President Jacob Zuma in order to extract unprecedented tenders. IT’S UNKNOWN HOW MANY BILLIONS STATE CAPTURE HAS COST SOUTH AFRICA’S ECONOMY. BUT THIS STORY IS NOT JUST A GUPTA ONE, IT’S ABOUT INTERNATIONAL COMPANIES USING THE GUPTA SERVICE TO PROFIT, AND THEN STAYING “WILFULLY BLIND” AFTER THE FACT. AND IT’S ALSO A NEW STORY SHOWING HOW AN UNSUSPECTING SMALL COMPANY WAS CAUGHT IN THE MIDDLE - USED AND THEN LEFT WITH NOTHING. Enter German Software Multinational SAP; They trade on the New York Stock Exchange, have offices in America and London and made R450 billion last year. BUT WHEN SAP WAS HAVING PROBLEMS CLOSING BIG DEALS WITH OUR SOE’S ON ITS OWN, DOCUMENTS SHOWED THEY TURNED TO THE BROTHERS FOR THEIR POLITICAL INFLUENCE. A SMALL GUPTA OWNED 3D PRINTING COMPANY WAS USED AS A FRONT TO BOTH DISTANCE ITSELF FROM TRANSACTIONS, HIDING THE GUPTA CONNECTION, BUT ALSO TO LAUNDER THE PROCEEDS OF SUCCESSFULLY ACQUIRED CONTRACTS FOR SAP TO THEMSELVES.THAT front company was CAD house, whose owner Bernhard Voigt is speaking out for the first time publicly. Voigt describes himself as an idealist, who had grand ideas to grow his business, which in 2015 had moderate earnings of R12 million. So he listed it as a Transnet preferred partner - and that’s where his story starts. CAD house was a 3d printing company and the Gupta’s approached him to partner. On paper, cad house became co-owned by gupta lieutenant - Santash Choubey - employed by Sahara Systems – but was managed as a subsidiary of the sahara group - indicating that beneficial ownership rested with the guptas themselves.SAP then entered the picture via the Guptas connection. Bernhard will explain how in August 2015 – SAP and CAD house signed a commission agreement which said: IF THE GUPTA COMPANY WERE THE “EFFECTIVE CAUSE” OF SAP LANDING A TRANSNET CONTRACT WORTH R100 MILLION OR MORE, IT WOULD GET A 10% COMMISSION FEE. NOW SALES COMMISSION AGREEMENTS AREN’T UNUSUAL AT 1 OR 2% BUT AT 10%, TO SOME, IT MAY SOUND SUSPICIOUSLY LIKE A EUPHEMISM FOR KICKBACK. AmaBhugane Journalist Susan Comrie believes so. And as a Gupta Leaks troller, she broke this story in mid 2017. In her audio recorded interview with them they claimed CAD House was no different than any other sales agent SAP uses. AmaB recorded their interview with SAPs Chief Financial Officer Deena Pillay who explained why CAD house was chosen to be SAPs strategic business partner.“They’re small guys who would go out there, identify business and come to SAP with that opportunity. It’s a lever available to SAP to sell its software… We’ve got a sales force that we employ, so these are the agents on the ground…"They are an extension of the sales force.” But if you speak to Bernard he says they never had experience marketing or selling SAP software- they're just a 3d printing company.

title: Locked Up for Good
oneLiner: We go inside what's been described as the world's most humane prison and ask what lessons for a South African system apparently focused on retribution over rehabilitation.
summary:
Norway is hardly a crime hot-spot. Its economy is strong and it has in place a generous social welfare system. So, comparisons with South Africa should be drawn with caution. But, like many societies (even the most flourishing) there are those who turn their backs on the benefits of being a law-abiding citizen and turn to a life of crime instead. And, for years, Norway believed the best way to deal with them was to exact retribution. Trouble is, the consequence of that approach - as it has been in America, South Africa and a myriad other countries - was to release back into society former inmates as unreformed and unrepentant as they had been when first sentenced. And that was measured in the numbers of those released from jail who went on to commit further crimes. But a change in approach, one that emphasised rehabilitation and the notion that separation from society was punishment enough, achieved remarkable results. Norway now enjoys one of the lowest re-offending rates in the world and its prisons are regarded as among the world's most humane - with Halden the shining light. What's more, the maximum sentence in Norway - for even the most heinous of crimes - is just 21 years (although, with a caveat that allows for maximum sentences to be subject to 5 year increments in the event of a prisoner not being rehabilitated).

Halden prison has opened its reinforced steel doors to Carte Blanche for a first-hand glimpse of Norway's approach to long-term incarceration. It's a maximum security facility but, in comparison to our own over-crowded, gang-ridden jails, it has the feel of a holiday camp. Prisoners are offered vocational training, yoga, lots of exercise and counseling services. Halden's governor insists that his staff are called "prison officials" rather than guards; an insight into an approach as far removed from the South African system as you're likely to get. An insight, too, into why Norway's re-offending rate among released inmates is just 20%. In South Africa, that rate is closer to 70%. We'll discover the secret to their success from the people who matter: the governor, the officials, and the prisoners.

The first-ever Springbok Test series against a touring British team was played in 1891. Newlands used to be regarded as one of the best rugby grounds in the world, combining intimate seating, a beautiful view of Table Mountain, and a great atmosphere. But it’s history is not entirely rosy. During Apartheid the Coloured fans were squashed into what used to be known as the Malay stands, later the South stand, squashed behind the goal posts. SACOS boycotted Newlands stadium for many years only returning after 1994. Newlands stadium doesn’t meet the fire and safety standards of modern stadiums, the stands, field and scoreboard all need upgrading and to the WPRU just does not have the finances to upgrade the grand old lady. The WPRU has been in dire financial straits for many years now- current debt could be as high R53-million after interest payments were not settled with Remgro.

It’s the end of an era for Western Province Rugby fans and players alike- the grand old lady will be retired- after three years of negotiations Western Province Rugby Union has finally announced they are moving to Cape Town Stadium as the anchor tenant with 99 year lease. The first Super Rugby series to be played there in 2021. 2020 will be DHL Stormers last year at Newlands Stadium. That’s the end of a 128 years of fine rugby. The City of Cape Town will retain responsibility for repairs and maintenance and the operational costs of Cape Town Stadium. It will remain a multipurpose entity, with Western Province Rugby leasing the Cape Town Stadium for matches

title: No Rape Kits
oneLiner: Although our FCS units have some of the most exemplary officers in the country, there is little they can do when they don't have the basics - like rape kits.
summary:
Monique Strydom: the woman who survived being taken hostage in 2000 in the Philippines. Her NGO Matla A Bana: which means “a voice against child abuse.” It began when she was asked to chair a task team that investigated child rape in South Africa. Their aim is to address the grey areas in the child protection system in South Africa. She says that Sexual offences kit and Buccal kit (swab in mouth kit that links DNA to different cases…) are not currently available. There’s been a long history of the tenders being cancelled for various reasons – Minister Cele has said they cancelled them because there was a problem with the bidding process, but many FCS offices around the country are out of kits. One is in CAPE TOWN. I have a cape town insider FCS officer, and I have a prosecutor – both need to be hidden but can talk about the under resourcing and appalling mismanagement. I mean they re already 50 per cent short in terms of special investigating officers, but now take away the only thing they did have which was these testing kits then they can’t so their jobs. According to the last crime stats as of sept 2018 110 rapes on average per day (over 40,000 rapes, of the more than 50,000 sexual offences reported). ( according to some…1 in 4 are reported, 14% are convicted… AFRICA CHECK)

As of February this year we were leaked the rape kit stats from the various provinces, and it's appalling. Only 19.8% of SA police stations had at least 1 rape kit for adults (meaning just over 80% of stations do not even have 1 rape kit), Only 17.8% of SA police stations had at least 1 rape kit for children (meaning just over 82% of stations do not even have 1 rape kit)...The whole of the Eastern Cape had only 22 rape kits for children (only 2 stations has these 22 rape kits). This means not even 1% of the stations has rape kits for children. BUT THAT WAS BACK THEN. NOW, it's now 4 months later, and some province's don't have any - like the Northern Cape, and some areas in johannesburg and cape town. There is a history of this happening going back to the early 2000s. And it's a two fold problem - one, the tender is national and often there are issues with the numbers ordered, and two, the problem is that the police have a lack of funding and often run out of funds during the year, and then have to use expired kits. We have an FCS officer in Cape Town who will tell us about why this is such a catastrophe - they will show us both buccal and rape kits. Buccal kits are used to link a potential rapist's DNA to other kits. We also have an NGO called Matla A Bana, which is headed by Monique Strydom, this organization works closely with police to address the problems within child protection - like a lack of rape kits. She alerted us to it the issue. She has a prosecutor in the cape who will assist us, and will give us information about what's happening at the courts. We also have court cases where the victims have not got justice because of this issue.

title: Destiny Holidays
summary:
Destiny Holidays, run by Marelise and Vincent de Bruyn, seemed like a legitimate Travel Agency. It had good reviews and many happy clients. They were polite and efficient and employed five agents. Their website carried the Asata (Association of South African Travel Agencies) logo, which Asata CEO Otto de Vries assured viewers in an earlier Carte Blanche story, should give travellers confidence that they were legitimate. The De Bruyns had several companies registered bearing ID numbers and addresses. They worked from an office in a shopping centre in Durbanville. But then in November last year the cracks began to show and bad reviews started popping up on Hello Peter. By May 2019 they filed for voluntary liquidation and 55 people have had their holiday dreams stolen and are R2.2-million out of pocket. There are 20 cases of fraud and theft laid against the De Bruyns across the country. But now the wheels have come off and the 55 people have formed a Whatsapp group. They have uncovered a web of lies. The De Bruyns have done this before. Vincent de Bruyn filed for bankruptcy in 2014. Then Marelise registered a franchise with Harvey World Travel in Menlyn, Pretoria, in 2015 from which both Vincent and Marelise operated. But complaints of unpaid bills prompted Harvey Travel to withdraw their franchise. So like most scam artists when the heat is on, they move town. They moved to the Cape at the end of 2015 and Marelise registered a new company, Destiny Holidays, employing her cousin’s husband, Riaan Earle, as an agent. In 2018 Marelise opened Travel Twist, a software package for travel agencies - a booking app.

For most people life is a grind of sitting in the traffic and slogging away to pay the bills: we dream of escaping with our families on that once in a lifetime holiday. Paul Peens dreamt of taking his new bride to the Maldives, to snorkel and dive in azure waters and walk along pristine beaches. He planned for months and on the afternoon of his wedding, as he was getting dressed he received an SMS assuring him all was in order and he should enjoy his wedding day. That was the last time he believed Destiny Holidays - he is yet to recover the R64 000 he paid to them

title: Zuma at the Zondo Commission
oneLiner: This week, former president Jacob Zuma takes the stand at the Zondo Commission on state capture, the latest attempt to have him answer a litany of corruption allegations.
summary:
Under the watch of President Zuma, the tentacles of state capture spread throughout the South African state apparatus and aligned businesses. His particular methods of supervision of the state led to the promotion of now distrusted personnel and ministers, those with more loyalty to private entities that could fill their pockets, than to the ethos of public service. After his presidency, Zuma still surrounds himself with characters tarnished by the reputation of greed. The head of his legal team for the hearings is Daniel Mantsha. The name of Mantsha was discredited in his time as chairperson of Denel, mainly because of the Denel Asia project‚ a joint venture between Denel and Gupta-owned companies. Furthermore, Mantsha has in the past been struck of the roll. At the end of the week, beyond sub-standard supervision of the state, what can Zuma be held accountable for at the Zondo Commission? After all, he has repeatedly pleaded his innocence of direct involvement in state capture machinations. Furthermore, he has resisted compliance with any investigative body that he deems not to be an independent platform. Already, he refused to answer direct questions from public protector Thuli Madonsela concerning his relationship with his son Duduzane and to the Gupta family – both parties deeply entrenched in the South African state capture saga. If Zuma co-operates with the leaders of evidence, we will cover his version of events, and weigh them up against the allegations. If he decides to work against the system then we will represent him with the empty chair scenario... in his place at the commission, an empty chair... and discuss the witness’s allegations further. Interviews with the likes of political analyst Professor William Gumede and commentator Songezo Zibi, will endeavour to pinpoint the impact of Zuma’s testimony within the broad remit of the commission.

The week of 15th to 19th of July 2019 is scheduled to be the first time Former President Jacob Zuma will appear in front of the Zondo Commission, to answer to the many accusations concerning his alleged pivotal role in state capture. Speculation is already rife on whether or not he will fully co-operate, but in any case, it is one of the most anticipated events in South African democratic history. Deputy Chief Justice Raymond Zondo’s judicial commission of inquiry has been tasked to investigate widespread allegations of state capture. Their challenge is to piece together the ‘true extent of state capture and how certain individuals and businesses’ benefited from the state financially. Will the pointing fingers aimed at Zuma, so far during the inquiry, amount to anything more than a TRC-like release from guilt by the perpetrators of wrong-doings... without any repercussions? Will we actually hear the full low-down from Zuma? Or will we have to just wait for him to write his book? With the collaboration of political analysts, we will provide the context to this historic week. The Commission, with its team of evidence leaders... The accusers of Zuma... The appearance of Zuma with the support of his legal team and rallying citizens... Former president Jacob Zuma, himself, will most likely determine the core narrative of his week at the Zondo Commission.

title: AltMed Investigation
oneLiner: Desperate to find a cure for his cancer and save his leg, young Kyle Nhlapo, turns to expensive alternative treatments. Funds are raised but in the end it all went horribly wrong..
summary:
RIGVIR is a Latvia-invented injectable cancer drug. It is a virotherapy medication approved in 2004, by the State Agency of Medicines of the Republic of Latvia. However in march 2019 the distribution in Latvia was stopped by the State Agency of Medicines after laboratory tests found that the amount of ECHO-7 virus was in much smaller amounts than claimed. The licence was suspended and RIGVIR removed from sale. Oncologist Dr David Gorski wrote " There are many mysterious aspects to the RIGVIR story that strongly suggests that RIGVIR is cancer quackery. The Latvian State Agency of Medicines sent a sample to a laboratory in the UK. the found it to have very little ECHO-7 virus. ZVA's laboratory director described it " its like expecting lemon juice and getting lemon flavoured water." RIGVIR is no stranger to controversy, with questions asked repeatedly about the validity of its clinical claims, methods of marketing itself to cancer patients across the world.

Desperate to find a cure for his cancer 20 year old Kyle Nhlapo hoped that an alternative cancer treatment called RIGVIR would save his leg and cure his Osteocarcoma. Kyle was referred to the Charlotte Maxeke hospital in 2018 where he was admitted and diagnosed with Osteosarcome. He started chemo therapy in March 2018. He became extremely ill from the treatment and his mother Beulah started looking for alternatives. They found a treatment called RIGVIR administered by a clinic called ALTMED. The treatment came at a huge cost and Kyle and Beulah contacted Hot FM (HotCares) to assist them in raising the funds. HotCares and a private donor raised almost R500 000 for the treatment. First Kyle was told that a body cleansing had to be done. He was put on a Vitamin C IV drip costing R32 168.00. After a month's cleansing they were told that RIGVIr was the best option. The clinic explained that the treatment was very costly and hoped that they had the funds. The clinic recommended treatment for three months. They gave a breakdown of the cost of the treatment. R180 000 for the first month. After receiving 4 injections there was no sign of the promised cure and no shrinkage of the tumour.. Beulah then wrote to Latvia where RIGVIR is developed asking about the treatment. She was told that they had no data of treating Osteosarcoma. Beulah and Kyle approached Altmed and informed them that they were terminating the treatment. By then , Kyle needed an amputation. Kyle and Beulah then requested a refund of the donated money. This was declined. Altmed did refund enough for the amputation but the balance of almost R80 000.00 was not refunded claiming that it was administration costs.

title: Gill Nets: Plundering our Dams and Rivers
oneLiner: Unabated poaching in our rivers and dams is threatening our freshwater biodiversity...
summary:
Belinda Joubert lives on the banks of the Crocodile river in Broederstroom. For the past 5 years she has witnessed gill nets in the river on a daily basis. The nets are deployed in the evening and then taken out in the early morning. The fish, she says, are sold at a nearby market on the side of a busy road. Of particular concern is the large number of by-catch. She has photos of lizards and various birds being entangled int he nets -- even a kudu. But this is not an isolated incident. Many of our rivers and dams are being plundered in this way. Just this week a 3km net was taken out at a dam just outside Rust de Winter and dams like Renosterkop, on the border between Gauteng and Mpumalanga are riddled with gill nets on a daily basis. The NGO Eco-Care Trust, reports that sometimes large trucks are seen on the edges of dams, ready to take the fish away. By catch, or fish that are too injured for consumption are simply left to rot in the rams and rivers. The Eco-Care Trust was established in 1995 to conserve our freshwater aquatic ecosystems. They have a vast network of volunteers that keep an eye on our rivers and dams and report and remove illegal nets. Eco-Care Trust will take us to a dam and show us the illegal nets and we will be part of the operation to remove the illegal nets. New legislation tabled for comment will potentially make all this gillnetting legal, which could have dire consequences for our freshwater biodiversity. The Government wants to make "traditional" fishing legal, giving indigent communities access to a valuable source of food, but without the necessary management and policing this could end up being disastrous. A pilot project in conjunction with Rhodes University in the VanderKloof dam in the Northern Cape wanted to pave the way for small scale commercial fishing operations, but the effect on the endangered largemouth yellowfish was devastating and the project was halted after much resistance from the conservation and angling community.

South Africa has comprehensive environmental legislation but when it comes to enforcing the law we fall short. Our freshwater fish and aquatic biodiversity in our rivers and dams are being decimated by relentless gill net poaching and even though it is illegal to even own a gill net, you find hundreds of kilometers of nets in our provincial dams and rivers. The nets are not selective and every fish in the river will end up in the net, and often other biodiversity will also become intangled in the nets. Foreigners are mostly blamed for the practice, coming in from neighbouring countries and seeing our freshwater systems as easy pickings. Nets are even regularly reported in the Vaal river, Orange river up to Richtersveld, and as far as the Crocodile River and the Zambezi -- The problem is far-reaching

title: Samantha Hudspeth
oneLiner: Samantha Hudspeth was shot through her face and neck by her abusive boyfriend and left for dead. A series of heroic acts ensued and gave her a new lease on life.
summary:
Samantha was shot by her former fiancé Mitchell Osborne in broad daylight outside the entrance to Fourways life hospital in Sandton on the morning of 19 April 2019. He sped away from the scene and shot himself dead shortly afterwards when apprehended by the SAP. She was saved by by the Fourways Life Paramedics who took 6 minutes to get her out of her car and into the emergency, where later she was operated on by Dr Mati, a brilliant surgeon who saved her life. She was shot with hollow point bullets and one was still lodged just millimeters from her spine. Once she started recovery, she was left homeless and without work, as her boyfriend was so controlling he had made her give up her job. She moved in with her 26 year old son and barely out of surgery started looking for work as a car sales person. Mercedes who she had worked for before, knew of her ordeal and gave her a job, knowing that it will take her some time to recover fully. Carte Blanche tells the story of the amazing acts of heroism and kindness that saved Samantha’s life as well as helped her get back on her feat. We also confront the state and the police as to why no action was taken to apprehend Mitchell Osbourne the night before when he threatened to kill her because she was leaving.

Every day three women die at the hands of their intimate partner in South Africa (July 2018 – South African Human Rights Commission). This too could have been the fate of Samantha Hudspeth, when her boyfriend of two years shot her early in the morning of the 19th of April, in traffic while she was driving. He had stalked her, walked up to her car and shot her through the face and neck and left her for dead. She was driving to finish off her statement of assault and abuse at the Douglasdale police station, which she had laid the night before, after he attacked her and her friend in their apartment. Quick response by Fourways Life paramedics, and life saving surgery has given her the opportunity to start over. Although still in recovery, she is back at work as she has no other means of surviving. She is a hope of glimmer for women who have been through similar ordeals and need to find a way to pick up their lives and start again.

title: Stock Theft / Slicing
oneLiner: Brutal scenes of animals slaughtered alive on farms and sold for their meat has left farmers in a state of shock. Carte Blanche investigates.
summary:
As farmers increased their security and branding of their stock, perpetrators have turned to a different modus operandi of stock theft to avoid tracing and tracking of animals. The method involves moving onto the farms at night with groups of men known as “kappers.” Armed with sticks and pangas they work swiftly hacking off the animals’ back Achilles tendons so the cattle can’t walk. The animal is then sliced alive taking only the shoulder and hindquarter. At the scene pregnant cows lie butchered with the unborn fetus next to the carcass and in some instances calves are standing next to the cow waiting to be fed. With sheep and goats, they are chased into a corner and then tied by the feet before they are beheaded. An informer has described how the gangs operate: A taxi will drop off the “Kappers” at the target farm where they will be picked up again when the job is done. A second vehicle will collect the meat. This is often a minibus or taxi with the seats removed. Meat is placed on order for big events like funerals or weddings and raids happen mostly before a weekend. Tracing the meat is virtually impossible as the perpetrators leave the body parts like the eartags behind that contain farmer’s identification.

Stock theft cost South Africa billions of rand every year. In 2018, 29 000 cases of stock theft was registered. Every day 178 cattle, 249 sheep and 115 goats are stolen in the country. In the Freestate alone the farming communities have suffered losses on average of ten million rand per month. But it goes beyond the financial loss to the traumatic impact on the farmer when faced with the carnage left behind after the slaughtering. Some farmers have described it as senseless killing, maiming animals for their body parts and leaving them to die.

Besides the orders being fake, if an arrest is made, a police man has to be present. I have no doubt that the centres know about this man and we will need to confront them as well.

An ex so called reformed drug addict has an intervention squad, and is using fake arrest or rehabilitation committal orders to haul off addicts to treatment centre, by passing the courts..and fleecing desperate parents of addicts who don't know the law. He has been doing this for some time now and despite the police knowing about this man, they have not arrested him.

title: The end of sex?
oneLiner: Scientists may soon be able to create human sperm and eggs using ordinary cells
summary:
Scientists may soon be able to create human sperm and eggs using ordinary cells – a boon for those with fertility problems that raises troubling ethical questions Forty years ago, couples suffering from infertility were given hope by the birth of Louise Brown, the first “test-tube baby”. But although millions of babies have now been born by IVF, the technique can offer no help to couples eager to have a child that is genetically theirs but who lack the eggs or sperm to make it: men whose testes produce no sperm, say, or women who have undergone surgery for ovarian cancer. Some opt for donor eggs or sperm, but an alternative may be on the way. Scientists are making steady progress towards creating human eggs and sperm – the so-called gametes that combine in fertilisation – artificially in a petri dish.

title: Post Elections - What Now?
oneLiner: The people of South Africa have spoken, heralding the brand new dawn with Cyril Ramaphosa at the helm of the ANC. Is it time for action or just more of the same?
summary:
South Africa has had its 6th free election, 25 years on from 1994. The African National Congress winning 57.5% of the vote, but showing dwindling support for the party, amidst a backdrop of a failing economy, corruption and record breaking unemployment rates. Experts tout Ramaphoria as a key factor to the ANC retaining its majority. But is Cyril Ramaphosa the man for the job, and how telling will be the internal politics within the ANC when it comes to choosing his cabinet. Will he be reigned in by internal forces or will he declare war and risk losing support within his own party? Can Cyril Ramaphosa change the perception of the ANC and put measures in place that will improve the lives of South Africans? Is he able to turn the economy around in time for South Africa to avoid another downgrade to junk status? Political and economic analysts dissect the issues and warn about the challenges, but we get an inside track on Ramaphosa the man by Ronnie Kasrils who has seen him in action going back to the Bisho Massacre in 1992 and has seen him in action within the ANC. In the announcement of his presidency in 2018, Ramaphosa announce his New Dawn, setting key objectives and goals for the country: tackling joblessness and corruption head-on, accelerating the pace of land redistribution and driving up investment in South Africa. Ramaphosa’s central pledge of the 2019 election is to build an inclusive economy that will address the big five crises facing ordinary South Africans: corruption, the lack of basic service delivery, unemployment, inequality and poverty. We go directly to Luthuli House and ask how he plans on furthering those objectives in the “Brand New Dawn” and what would be his immediate challenges and tasks. Carte Blanche takes a critical look at South Africa’s deepening social and political divides and the man tasked to make the changes that South Africans have been waiting 25 years for.

The Brand New Dawn is upon us with Cyril Ramaphosa at the helm of the ruling party, the ANC. The ANC has lost 12% of the share of the vote since the 2004 elections, showing dwindling support and belief in the party by South African citizens. Many attribute the ANC’s win to the man himself Cyril Ramaphosa. Disgruntled citizens together with a divided ANC... how can one man bring unity to a party that is factionalised and put into action promises that have been made to the electorate? Is Cyril Ramaphosa really the man of the hour, and can he last long enough in office to implement his vision? Carte Blanche speaks to insiders and analysts who consider whether the President can shine light on the fortunes of ordinary South Africans or if competing ANC factionalism will snuff out hope.

title: Funnest schools in the World: Education Lessons from Finland
oneLiner: The “Funnest” Schools in the World
summary:
Who would ever use “school” and “fun” in the same sentence? We see how well kids learn in some of the world’s most joyful classrooms. Increasing amounts of information, longer hours, more exams, extra classes, earlier lessons, less play and more work – that is the recipe most education systems are following around the world. In Finland... they do exactly the opposite. And Finnish kids and teachers thrive more than in most schools worldwide. We experience a day in the life of a Finnish family and see what it is like to attend school where the highest priority seems to be children’s happiness and not test results.

Imagine a school where the children’s happiness is the teachers’ main concern, where kids are encouraged to explore and be themselves, where play is the basis for learning and where your class and teacher becomes like your family. In Finland that would be any ordinary school.

title: Chaos the Cancer Lion
oneLiner: A lion undergoes radiation treatment for cancer at Meulmed hospital to save his life.
summary:
Chaos is a 16 year old male tawny lion who has grown up in Midrand’s Lory Park Zoo. Weighing in at close to 300kg, this massive specimen came to the zoo in 2002 when he was a few weeks old. Back then there was no lion bone trade or lion pet industry – or the problems we currently have of a massive lion population in captivity in South Africa – which results in many going into the canned hunting industry. Lory park is a private zoo, that began when it’s owners Matty and Eddy van Eck wanted to share his private collection of animals - mostly birds with the public for educational purposes. They are a facility that brings in veterinary training students from overseas, and school students wanting to learn about animals up close and personal. They do not breed their animals now, but keep the females on contraception and the males are given vasectomy’s because this is better for the animal rather than outright neutering. This keeps the animals healthier – so they don’t gain excessive weight, and allows them to keep their natural tendency’s rather than just neutering them because it makes it easier for them to be handled. (Kara: "The reason that we use vasectomy is it is much less invasive and unfortunately the contraceptive implant has many negative affects on female cats. It also ensures that hormone levels aren’t affected.") Lory park was originally a bird park, based on the Lorikeet parrot – but it has grown to incorporate many other animals ranging from big cats, apes, reptiles and birds. Matty doesn’t see the animals as pets but as ambassadors for their kind and naturally has a deep love and respect for them - they have many conservation projects and work with Onderstepoort.

We will have this story exclusively. They are sick of the other media - they all just pitched up at the hospital and forced their way into theatre. It was very chaotic, but they are willing to let us tell the entire story from A TO Z. In a South Africa first, possibly a world first, an adult lion is being treated at a hospital for cancer. Chaos was quite a ladies man, until he met Tequila, who is almost 2 years older than him – the only female he has ever mated with and they have been inseparable since introduced. He is very protective of her, and when she does come into heat he will not let anyone near their housing. They did have three littres, Amber - the one female is still at the zoo, and the other cubs went to the Sao Paulo zoo in Brazil, after that there have been no other littre’s. They want to keep his sperm on file so that there is a mixture of different lion sperm available, although Matty says there is no lion breeding program in South Africa like there is with Cheetah’s and Leopards. (From Kara: "Its not that there isn’t a breeding programme, the problem is that even if DNA is banked at bio labs, there is still no proof needed to export cats such as with Cheetahs. There is not enough effort being put into the conservation of these majestic cats. We have not bio banked any of Chaos’ sperm yet.") Chaos and Teuqila are currently retired animals – who live in a lovely large cage at the back of the zoo where the public are not allowed. When animals become older and no longer enjoy the public – this is where they are brought to. Wild male lions usually only live to 10-12 years, while in captivity they can live from 20-24 years old.

title: Proteas at the Cricket World Cup
oneLiner: We look back at the South Africa's history at the Cricket World Cup
summary:
South African cricket had been isolated from the world because of Apartheid for a period of 22 years. Then with the release of Nelson Mandela, South African Cricket was welcomed back into the fold and (at the last minute) invited to participate in the 1992 Cricket World Cup in Australia. So began South Africa's quest to capture the greatest prize in cricket and over the next 27 years, the team would scale the highest of highs and plumb the lowest of lows in trying to bring the cup home. In this episode of Carte Blanche we look back at the Proteas' history at the Cricket World Cup, reliving the moments of triumph and the depths of despair through the eyes of the players that were there. From beating Australia in their very first game, Jonty Rhodes' announcing himself spectacularly on the world stage, to rain denying South Africa a place in the final to Lance Kluseners' remarkable exploits at the 1999 World Cup to the epic semi-final against Australia or most recently, South Africa's painful exit against New Zealand in the last World Cup, South Africa's relationship with the World Cup has always been fraught with drama. We will speak to Proteas' legends like Gary Kirsten, Lance Klusener, Shaun Pollock, Herschelle Gibbs, Makhaya Ntini & Graeme Smith to interrogate what makes the World Cup so special and why winning it remains the Holy Grail for South African Cricket.

For the majority of South Africans, winning the Cricket World Cup remains the Holy Grail for the Proteas. Since participating in their first world cup back in 1992, the team has come so close, yet remained so far from attaining this treasured goal. We look back at the highlights and heartbreaks over the course of 7 previous campaigns as they embark on their latest campaign at the 2019 Cricket World Cup in England in hopes of breaking a 27-year drought and claim their maiden World Cup.

title: Chef Jan
oneLiner: South Africa's first Michelin star chef, Jan Hendrik van der Westhuizen, talks to us about his rise to fame in gastronomy's heartland and his planned homecoming.
summary:
France is the culinary centre of the Universe, Nice is the jewel on the Cote D'Azur around which much of it revolves. That Jan Hendrik, fresh off a millionaire's yacht in nearby Monaco, chose to open a restaurant there was always likely to be calamitous. Except, it wasn't. A flair for taste, design and creativity unleashed on an unsuspecting French palate such delights as rusks, chakalaka and pap. And they loved it. Within three short years of opening he was awarded a Michelin star, the culinary world's Nobel prize or Oscar. He is a creative force of nature, a wonderful cook and immensely proud of his roots. In short, an amazing story of a South African who made good.

Chef Jan is about to embark on the next phase of an already extraordinary life: a much heralded return to his country of birth. He's due to open a fin-dining restaurant in the heart of the Kalahari as well as an innovative test-kitchen in Cape Town. We get to spend two days with him at his acclaimed restaurant in Nice, France to talk about his vision of the future and past successes.

title: SANDF horses
oneLiner: should horses be entrusted into the care of the SANDF?
summary:
There is a natural narrative - and the overriding theme is the care and protection of animals whether they are in service or our pets. We expect the state to set an example. The SANDF's treatment of these horses is nothing short of a scandalous. Two charges against the SANDF speaks volumes. Our story line should send shivers down the spine of our viewers and it is hoped that there will be such an outcry that radical attitude changes will result at the SANDF.

In Aug 2018 the Nspca were horrified to discover that horses in the care of the SANDF at their equine base called SAASIC in Potchestroom army base were starving to death. Over 200 hundred horses had been purchased by the army for the new SAASIC unit - these horses were to be trained for border patrol. There is a long history with regard to horses in the SANDF, going back to their use in border patrol in the 1970's and 1980"s. The unit had been disbanded and the police took over the care of horses for their use. Then SAASIC was formed in 2014. Most of the horses that were bought were not tame. and the NSPCA offered help to the army. to help train the horses. This was turned down. They heard reports of the animals being mistreated and went to investigate. many of the horses were not being fed...and some were in such bad condition that 25 had to be put down immediately., Whilst the NCPCA were there they saw army riding horses in a cruel way, and they filmed this. 2 charges were laid for animal cruelty. They also got a court order preventing the riders from riding these horses. The NSPCA did a deal with the Army and took over the care of 76 horses which they re-homed. In a matter of months these untame horses became tame. A vet did an experiment on the horses back at the base. The vet showed different uniforms to the horses that had been abused..the only uniform that the horses reacted badly to was sandf uniforms. The SANDF insisted on keeping some horses at their base but against the advice of the NSPCA, the SANDF sent 60 to an army base called Rooiwal, better conditions. They were warned about this because of the high incidence of equine sickness in the area. The army insisted. 20 horses died with the year from equine sickness and many broke their legs because if then rough terrain. Its been a year since charges were laid but the progress of the investigation has been hampered by lack of SANDF o-operation. A commission of enquiry was held apparently by the army into the starving horses but the results of this enquiry were not released. There is a rumour that the SANDF paid top dollar for trained horses but instead they received untrained horses.,

title: Online Loan Scams
summary:
The court summons is for roughly R1770 and the threat is that you will have to pay legal costs over and above the initial amount. The summons doesn't have a number but people don't understand it has to be delivered by a sheriff of the court. Lifestyle Legal - the company that sends the threats of black listing and court summons are not even a legal firm or registered debt collectors. The more sites you look to see what loans are out there the more stop orders you rack up. The Stellenbosch law Clinic have taken on the case and are going to fight a class action to stop Damian Malander and similar loan scamsters. We have had loads of submissions on our website from desperate people. its a consumer story and a public interst story to expose this man. I have a PI who will track his number and movements to see that he is in the country and we will write a letter requesting a sit down interview and if that is not successful we will door stop him

With 13 loan websites Damian Malander is making a killing. His website looks like they offering loans but infact they are not credit providers and instead they are passing you on to get loans and sometimes they don't even do that. What they are selling you is legal advice you didn't ask for like how to get a divorcee or fill out a will- anything but the loan you so desperately need. What you do get is even more debt than when you started. When you aply for the loan you have to click the terms and conditions to advance to the next page and in doing that deep in the small print you have agreed to have a stop order on your account for the next 12 months. THe first amont is R399 and then R99 for the next 11 months. If you try and call and cancel in the first 7 days you cant get through and they don't answer your emails. If you try an cancel they charge you a cancellation fee and you still end up paying about R800 for nothing. If you successfully stop the debit order then the court summons and threats of black listing arrive from Lifestyle Legal which is not a law firm or a registered debt collector. If you manage to stop one stop order they just change one digit and it slips past the next month and you are back at the bank asking for help. Some banks like Capitec just reverse it but others like Nedbank make you contact the company. Its nightmare that goes on for years.

title: Shakespeare for the Homeless
summary: In between taxis, and hawkers and piles of rubbish, squeezed in between decaying buildings, there’s a sign – easy to miss- that announces the Hillbrow Theatre…then down the stairs you go until to the basement and here amongst the broken chairs… England’s most famous playwright; William Shakespeare’s words are being given new life and meaning. Around 15 men of various ages are sitting in a semi- circle. Playing to this audience is 31 year old Michael Mazibuko. He’s reciting Hamlet’s soliloquy ‘ To Be or Not To Be’. Director, Michael Maxwell is giving Mazibuko voice direction and explaining the meanings of some of these very olde English words – while he is doing this you could hear a pin drop, everyone’s attention is focused on Michaels every word. Called Johannesburg Awakening ( Jam), this is brain child of Dorothy Anne Gould, one of South Africa’s most celebrated and respected actresses, Dorothy has starred in over 180 productions and been awarded several of South Africa’s top accolades. Dorothy’s own life was changed as teenager when she discovered the power of the spoken word. "I fell in love with the stories and poetry of a man called William Shakespeare. These made a profound shift in my immature consciousness to a more spiritual level of understanding of my world and of humanity; they made me aware that performance in a story is a sacred art and can transform both performer and audience and that this is achieved through the use of breath, through the power of the spoken word and through the act of sublimating ones ego and playing instead, for the gods. They gave me a purpose in my life which has never wavered – uplift and serve ones’ fellow human beings through the power and magic of poetry."

Lesley is the chairperson of I am made 4 God's Glory, while the other two are chaired by people who work for Lesley's law firm Ramulifho Inc.

Attorney, Lesley Ramulifh, allegedly received a total of R27.5 million rand from the NLC to refurbish an existing NPO and drug rehabilitation centre in Pretoria. But soon after construction started, the owner of the rehab, Ado Krige, started questioning Lesley on construction delays etc, as well as the fact that contrary to their agreement Lesley wanted Ado to sell the rehab to him. Since then construction (according to an independent report the value of work done only totals R4 million) has stopped. Ado has taken his case to the NLC who seem unwilling to do anything about the situation. Lesley received the R27.5 million by calling himself a director of an NPO called Denzhe Primary Care. We can prove that at least some of the money Denzhe received, about half a million rand, went towards purchasing two Ocean Basket franchises. We can also prove that the construction company Lesley appointed to do the R15 million refurbishment of the rehab, Upbrand Properties was registered in January 2016 with Johannes Kgomotso Letwaba, the older brother of the NLC’s COO, Phillemon Letwaba, as the sole director.

title: Amputee Xolani Luvuno
oneLiner: From heroin-addicted street beggar to Comrades Marathon runner & iron-man competitor, this is the inspirational story of amputee athlete Xolani Luvano
summary:
We tell the amazing story of Xolani Luvano. Hailing from the Eastern Cape, he spent his youth as a common criminal, stealing on the streets of Port Elizabeth. Then he discovered that he had bone cancer which resulted in his right leg having to be amputated. He ended up begging, spending the next 10 years homeless in PE, Durban and finally Centurion. Life on the streets is hard. He's had to beg and prostitute himself to feed his habit. 3 Years ago he was rescued by good samaritan Hein Venter who gave him shelter and a job at his perfume factory in Midrand. As part of his rehabilitation, Xolani began running with his work colleagues. This hobby fired Xolani's passion. Last year he took part and completed the Comrades Marathon, "running" the 98km race on crutches and one leg. Now he's turned attention to the gruelling Iron Man and is training to take part in the race on 7 April. We tell Xolani's inspirational story

Xolani Luvano has a truly inspirational story. He's an amputee who spent 10 years homeless and addicted to heroin. 3 years ago he was rescued from life on the streets by good samaritan Hein Venter. Since his rehabilitation, he's got a full-time job and gone onto run the Comrades Marathon and is training to compete in the grueling Iron Man on 7 April in Port Elizabeth.

title: Pure Inbred
oneLiner: When you buy a pedigree and purebred pup you believe you are buying the best and healthiest dogs - but our investigation shows that is not the case.
summary:
Riddled with genetic disease Dog breeds aren’t even a real thing – like nature created them that way, and that every mutt is a mix of pure breeds. Like: 1,5 retriever, sheepdog, 1/6 poodle, chow? German shepherd, 1/12 border collie So they are selectively bred for their traits – 90% of all dog breeds were created the past 100 years. In 19th century Victorian era, competitive dog breeding became all the rage…then they declared it a pure breed. Inbred – never allowed to mate outside of species. One study found that 10,000 pugs have the same genetic diversity as 50 individuals – making them highly inbred. This leads to them being often sick. 60% of golden retrievers die of cancer, 1/3 of spaniel’s have skulls too small for their brains. Great Danes are so huge now that their hearts can’t support their bodies. Bulldog – so cute – total genetic failure. A century of inbreeding has ruined them, noses are so squashed they can barely breathe, their heads are so big they can only give birth by caesarean section, their tails have become ingrown, they basically all have hip dysplasia and their average life expectancy is 6 years – these dogs shouldn’t be alive. But they win things like “best in show.” Kennel clubs could fix their problems if they cross breed, but they won’t because then they won’t be as cute. It’s our existence that is letting them live up to our arbitrary existence. Easy solution – go to shelter.

We are going to be looking the entire industry - from breeding and how it began in Victorian England times, to the dog shows which award breeders with best in show awards for certain bred attributes - which are unhealthy for the dog, to the breeders - both unethical and ethical, and then to the regulator of the industry KUSA. We will interview numerous case studies and go undercover to show the real way this industry works. Based on the UK documentary's which exposed this industry on the UK kennel club, who established these breeds. This is going to rock our audience's socks off - because what you thought was healthy and wonderful - will turn your perception of this world on its head.

oneLiner: As the UK continues an ambitious project to map the genomes of 100 thousand people with cancer and rare diseases, we discover that Africa is planning to follow suit.
summary:
The 100 000 Genomes Project in the UK aims to capture - through an incredibly complex but increasingly practical process - the information contained in the genes of people with rare diseases and cancers. That involves sequencing the 3 billion letters of each persons genome, and examining where the likely "genetic malfunction" that led to a particular disease is taking place. Once that information is collated and cross-checked - and the complexities of how that data is stored and protected overcome - it'll be far easier to detect and therefore treat those diseases in other people. This is the future of medicine: Targeted diagnosis and treatment at a genetic level based on information about your unique "biological architecture" which will be deciphered and eventually stored on a massive data base. It's a process already underway in many parts of the world, and one being grappled with by our own Medical Research Council. In spite of the enormous logistical and resource challenges, there's a plan to do in Africa what is being done in the UK.

While genetic medicine is in its relative infancy in South Africa, Carte Blanche will gain insight into its potential to shape future medicine by visiting the acclaimed 100 000 Genomes Project run bu the NHS in the U.K. This will provide our viewers with a practical guide on the ambitions of our own medical research council as it captures the unique genetic "fingerprints" of a broad section of the population and uses that information to refine what is becoming known as "precision medicine".

title: Turtle Rescue
oneLiner: Every year dozens of baby turtles wash out on the beaches of the cape. If not rescued they will die. Carte Blanche investigates.
summary:
Turtles are cold blooded and cannot warm themselves. They thrive in the warm waters of KwaZulu-Natal and Mozambique where they breed during the summer months. They lay their eggs onshore in the the sand and after 60 days these tiny animals fight their way into the sea heading into the warm current where they drift and float whilst feeding. But some get lost in stormy seas and cross currents drifting kilometres south into the icy waters of the cape. From Plettenberg Bay on the east coast to Witsand on the west coast it is believed that hundreds of turtles wash ashore every year but only a few are the lucky ones found by passers by and picked up. Human intervention is needed to rescue the stranded animals; some with injuries and damaged flippers they are in urgent need of medical attention. But it is not only the babies that need rescuing; adult turtles are often found by fisherman or divers out in the open seas where they are entangled in fishing lines. Plastic bags that float in the ocean looks like jellyfish, a staple diet of loggerhead turtles who are often found with plastic in their gut. Even baby turtles poop minute plastic pellets called nurdles that have become one of the biggest polluters of our oceans. From Loggerheads to Leatherbacks, all seven species of turtles found in South Africa has been treated by a team of experts at the Two Oceans rehabilitation centre since its inception in 2009. They have seen the damage first hand that man causes: from treating infected and gashed carapice caused by boat propellers to removing plastic bags from the gut of a Loggerhead, they have managed to turn the statistics around.

From March till September is a busy time for the Two Oceans Aquarium when sea turtles are being brought in to their rehabilitation centre. These tiny sea creatures are found frozen on the beaches of the Cape coast lifeless and still. They are cold and starving, suffering from dehydration and hypothermia and in a permanent state of shock. Referred to as ‘cold stunning’ their heart rate have decreased to a point that they will die if not rescued.

title: Big Brother Vumacam
oneLiner: The Johannesburg CBD and its surrounding suburbs have now been turned into a surveillance hub. What price are South Africans willing to pay in return for greater security?
summary:
The Johannesburg CBD and its surrounding suburbs have now been turned into a surveillance hub. On many street corners poles designed to house security cameras are being erected, in readiness to watch over you… it’s for your “security”. But as a resident of the city do you know how much the cameras can see, have you been consulted and are you willing to compromise your privacy by having this big brother's eyes on you?

What is the price that South Africans are willing to pay for security and does this come at the expense of our individual privacy? There has never been such a massive roll-out of security cameras in South Africa as those Vumacam are installing across Johannesburg, in a major plan to link security surveillance across the whole city. The plan is to extend the system to the rest of the country. We get an inside look at how the system works.

experts: Ms. Ashleigh Parry Prof. Jane Duncan Mr. Murray Hunter Ms. Ahmore Burger-Smidt Mr. Michael Sun

title: End of Life Doula
oneLiner: As it becomes a growing trend in South Africa we ask what is an End of Life Doula?
summary: An end of Life/Death Doula is not a medical professional, their primary role is to emotionally support the dying and their family. The Doula explains it as, “Helping the patient to live while dying”. Practically they help with legacy projects, closing lose ends with loved ones, confronting the fear of dying and what happens next. Often when someone are passing their main concern is the well being of those they are leaving behind, the job of an end of life Doula is to allow them the space to speak about their own fears and unfinished business.
experts: Ms. Samala Ms. Denny Dearlove Ms. Stasha Ms. Nicci

title: THE JRA IS FALLING DOWN
oneLiner: With only 6 % of the City of Johannesburg’s bridges in a good condition – who’s to blame? Carte Blanche investigates.
summary:
94% of Johannesburg’s bridges are in a fair to extremely poor condition. City Mayor Herman Mashaba would like you to believe he inherited the problem and that it’s the ANC’s fault. We beg to differ. There is proof that Mayor Mashaba is not free from blame – he is in part responsible for the current situation. We speak to insiders and experts to get to the bottom of the bridge fiasco, putting Mayor Mashaba on the spot.

- STORY CURRENTLY IN THE NEWS - BUT OTHER JOURNOS ARE REPORTING ON THE TRAFFIC DRAMA... - WE UNCOVER THE CORRUPTION AND MISMANAGEMENT BEHIND THE CURRENT STATE OF JHB's BRIDGES - VISUALS WILL BE SHOCKING - WE HAVE ACCESS TO A RECORDING PROVING KICKBACKS AND IMPLICATING A VERY SENIOR OFFICIAL AT THE JRA - GREAT OPPORTUNITY FOR CONFRONT WITH MAYOR HERMAN MASHABA AND A CHANCE TO DEMAND THAT REPORT HE PROMISED ALMOST A YEAR AGO - HE IS SO SET ON ROOTING OUT CORRUPTION BUT APPARENTLY NOT SO MUCH WHEN IT INVOLVES COALITION PARTNERS.....

title: IBOGAINE KILLER
oneLiner: A controversial rehab drug administered by a dentist claimed the life of a Canadian citizen in Durban – we investigate.
summary:
Ibogaine is a highly controversial drug only available in 7 countries – South Africa is one of them. Intended to treat opiod addiction, but not recommended for benzodiazepines. A Canadian citizen came to SA to get off his anti-depressant addiction. He arrived and died two days later at a rehab centre run by not a doctor but a dentist. The family fears that the South African legal system will fail serve justice for what they say is the murder of Milos Martinovic. We get exclusive interviews with his wife and father – both broken by his loss, angry at charlatan dentist and deeply concerned about the rule of law in the country.

title: Illegal street racers
oneLiner: We take a look into the fast and furious world of illegal street racing
summary:
The story will immerse the audience into the secretive illegal racing scene. This will be a no holds barred approach to the subject, we will have details how racings routes are determined, we will get a glimpse into the painstaking and expensive exercise of modifying a car for a street race and the incredibly obsessive 'relationships' these street racers have with their cars. We will also look at the history of street racing in Joburg and South Africa as a whole. We will speak to the organizer of the illegal street race Dielo or Uncle 'D' who has been racing since he was a teenager. We will also be speaking to JP who claims his crew is the fastest in the country, he runs a more organized form of street racing, he says he doesn't consider himself "illegal" and blames MotorsportSA for not making enough facilities available to racers. We will be interviewing Jess, a female racer who will be speaking about being an extreme minority in the world of racing. She has taken on experienced racers both on the street and the tracks and more often than not she has come up on top. In esssence, the story will be mainly on the subculture

We will take the audience into a world very few people have access to - the world of illegal street racing. We will be taking an unusual approach to the subject -meaning the story will focus less on the legality of this extreme pass time. The story will have a no holds barred feel to it and will be gritty and visually interesting. The story will not be an all-boys affair ; We have female racers who are well respected in the underground racing world and are just as passionate about cars.
caseStudies: Jason Chabose Charne Lee Jones Ahdel Victor Ambrose Peterse

title: Forgiven Ways BEE Easy
oneLiner: According to former employees, self styled prophet Ernest van Antwerpen is using his Forgiven Ways Group to circumvent BBBEE legislation and pocket the earnings for himself and his ministry.
summary:
BEE-Easy targets South African corporates through existing BEE legislation which allows for benefits such as increased BEE ratings and tax exemptions. For example, a corporate can sponsor a BEE candidate for a learnership for 1 year. IT will cost the corporate between R30 000 - R40 000 per learner, and a monthly stipend for the learner of between R1500 - R3000 p/m. The corporate pays the amount, in many cases upfront, to BEE Easy to facilitate the process. But according to former employees and learners, the money is channeled by Ernest to his church and pastors. In 2018 BEE Easy took in 400 learnerships. But students say that from day one they were treated badly. At the BEE Easy offices they had one toilet to share between all the students, with no refreshments offered during the day. They did not receive monthly stipends on time or at all. And some of them have now not received the certificates promised despite completing the courses. Former BEE Easy staff members were forced to attend monday morning prayer sessions at the offices. Ernest's teaching in Yahushua-culture was offensive to many of them. In June 2017 BEE-Easy stopped paying their salaries, and if they complained they were told they were going against God. Many left after three months of no payment and BEE EAsy still owes them the money. But they have simply hired new staff, taken in new corporate customers, and carried on with the business. While doing so, they have offered many existing NGO's the opportunity to become fully black owned by partnering with Forgiven Ways, which is supposedly black owned. But they have hijacked the existing NGO's and NPO's projects, under the promises of huge growth potentials and capital investments that never happened. So Forgiven Ways ends up with controlling shareholding in the projects, but runs them into the ground and don't pay what they promised.

Ernest van Antwerpen is a self proclaimed prophet and messenger of God. His teachings fall under what he calls a Yahushua-Culture and are in themselves quite controversial, amongst others he has published "Prayers against homosexual sins" and claims the African continent is poor because "Africa is poor due to the idolatry and the occult behaviour of African people." But Ernest has also created an extremely complex company structure under a trust called the Forgiven Ways Group. And he is using the trust and specifically one of the entities under the group called BEE-Easy in a BEE fronting scam that rakes in millions and does very little in the sense of actual Black Economic Empowerment.

title: Western Cape Anti-Gang Unit
oneLiner: can the new gang squad make a dent?
summary:
The program will start with the gang squad forming for an evening's work and various sub plots will take place throughout the insert as we see the unit in action.

The cape flats is a war zone. Gang-related murders in the Western Cape significantly exceed the trend countrywide, Major-General Norman Sekhukhune, head of police crime research and statistics, announced on Tuesday. The statistics cover the period 1 April, 2017 to 31 March, 2018. Out of the 973 gang-related crimes committed countrywide, 808 occurred in the Western Cape, with the Eastern Cape markedly lower in second place at 87. They are followed by the Free State with 46 and Gauteng with 14. In the last two weeks, there have been 18 gang related murders. Adults and children who live is the Cape Flats are traumatised. One report released a couple of years by the cape Town trauma centre stated that – Sixty percent of children said they were “jumpy or easily startled”, 55% felt “irritable” and had “fits of anger” and over half said they were not able to concentrate, which “adversely affects school performance”. The authors note that “traumatised children [are] vulnerable to school failure and drop outs” and those who “drop out of school are at greater risk of gang involvement, criminal activity”, exposure to violence and becoming perpetrators of violence themselves. We spend an evening with the gang unit and interview Major General Andre Lincoln, who head it up, and our questions will surround: the squads success’s – its challenges, what their goals are, the intelligence work that need to go into operations – what are the solutions besides police activity? Hopefully we will identify a force member who lives on the Cape Flats and who can give his perspective. We are awaiting confirmation to interview a gangster with a balaclava who can shed light on the rising numbers of gang related deaths. To help describe the anguish, we speak to acclaimed singer James Bhemgee, who two years ago, survived a gang shooting, and who lost his son and sister recently. James said that gangsters broke into his sister’s home and shot her, and he said that his son was shot en route to a peace meeting. In response to the violence, a program called Peace Ambassadors was established. It was set up by Professor Brian Williams (UWC) who mediates in war torn countries. He also has a PHD in economics and has a good grasp and gangs and their economies’ (drugs, sex workers etc). The program has been piloted in Cape Town. Teenagers have choices besides being lured into the glamour of gangs. It starts from within - Peace, a state of harmony, is likened to a light that is a gift. This gift must be shared with others for its power to warm the hearts of everyone and to act as a divine compass. The methodologies applied during the peace training demonstrated that it was possible for anyone to become a messenger of peace. Peace has spiritual, philosophical and practical value at personal and collective levels. we speak to a reformed feared ex gang leader who was 25 years in prison and who now peace ambassador. His name is Magadien Wentzel. We speak to one 18 year old Riedwaan Samuls who was shot by gangsters while playing soccer. He survived 4 bullets. He is a peace ambassador and instead becoming bitter, he continues to preach peace. If there is time we speak to the parents of another peace ambassador whose son was killed in cross fire. As part of a group of peace ambassadors in Hanover Park, Keagan de Silver, 17, was involved in educating his community about the benefits of peace. On Wednesday, the Grade 11 pupil from Mount View High School was shot five times in a spaza shop close to home. His mother, Natasha Williams, said emergency services took their time in taking him to hospital. He took his last breath while she was holding him. The cape flats is a war zone. title: Lukhanyiso, Broken Field of Dreams.
oneLiner: Carte Blanche goes into the Free state to investigate farming projects and finds a horrifying picture
summary:
In February 2013 The Lukhanyiso farming project was launched by the Department of Rural Development and land reform in the Free state. The idea was to create 90 small scale BEE farms, creating 370 jobs with a gross yearly profit of R37.5 million rand. The project was conducted over a period of five years from Feb 2013 to January 2017 In a progress report the projections were as follows: The gross yearly turnover for each of the 90 pig and chicken farms is around R640,000, while the central farms annual turnover escalates to R21,4 mill in year 3 onwards. The income and expense analysis provide for a profitable gross margin profit business case with a total of R135,9 mill profit over the 5-year period. The operational budget for the Lukhanyiso Farm will be R23 mill annually where 90 BEE farms will be managing 9,000 pigs and 112,500 chickens, or an annual production of 30,938 pigs and 843,750 chickens. The capital budget for the development of the 90 individual farms and the centre farm is around R57 mill.

Great case studies and all the documentation to tell our story properly and full access
caseStudies: Zolile Manquthu

title: Why Should South Africans Care about Brexit?
oneLiner: The United Kingdom, within Europe, is a major importer of South African goods, but after Brexit, what will become of our trade agreements with the British?
summary:
The deadline for the UKs exit from Europe is fast approaching - 29th March 2019. The UK was split down the middle in the referendum, the British government is now battling to get a deal agreed to by its members of parliament. The country has woken up to the myriad of consequences that simple vote in 2016 has invoked. Europe has long been aware of the far reaching ramifications of the UK's exit plan, but now as the moment of truth gets closer the rest of the world is paying much more attention to what it means for them. With almost a fifth of South African exports going to the UK and our historical links with the country, it's about time South Africa got to grips with what Brexit means... for us.

For those South African companies with European headquarters in the UK, how much harm will Brexit do to their business, when it blocks their convenient gateway to the continent?
experts: Mr. Peter Haine Brexit Expert Mr. Douglas Gibson Mr. Rob Davies Mr. Goolam Ballim Economist

title: Eskom Unbundling -- what the future holds
oneLiner: Eskom, the country's largest power utility is technically insolvent and struggling to keep the lights on. Are we speeding towards Day Zero?
summary:
It will be a long haul to sort out Eskom's rot. Dealing with the financial, operational and structural crises is urgent. It is an emergency says Public Enterprises Minister Pravin Gordin. Lack of maintenance triggered Stage Four loadshedding, plunging the country into darkness with devastating effect on the country's people and the economy. A probe into factors leading to the collapse of the entity is underway.There are those who say that Eskom is a metaphor for South Africa. It's a vast megalith entirely bankrupted by people who have treated it as their personal ATM's and has become a political playing field.This is a disaster threatening to destroy the country's economy. A large part of the rot set in when the government decided to go ahead with building Medupi and Kusile. the world's two largest and most expensive coal-fired plants. Mismanagement and rampant corruption has led to serious delays and an billions of rand overspent. The culture of non-payment and rampant theft of electricity has added to the utilities woes. Municipalities are in arrears of more than R17-Billion. Stage 4 load shedding was implemented . This means that around 40% of generating capacity was not available. Lack of maintenance was one of the contributing factors. Splitting Eskom into three entities has Unions up in arms, already smelling job cuts and privatisation. The bottom line is,the lights are out for two reasons: Corruption and Mismanagement. On Wednesday Tito Mboweni, Minister of Finance will inform the nation about the way forward.

President Cyril Ramaphosa has announced a decision to unbundle Eskom into three separate state-owned entities, Generation, Transmission and Distribution. The announcement was in all likelihood discussed with the IMF and the World Bank as well as other major investors. But days later, the country was plunged into darkness when the troubled utility announced nationwide Stage 4 load shedding with devastating effect on the country's people and the economy. To sort out Eskom's rot will be a long haul but intervention is urgently needed. Public Enterprises Minister Pravin Gordan has described the crisis as one of the biggest risks to the South African economy. The question we are asking is: How did we get here, how will we fix it? And is unbundling a solution?
