title: Knysna Elephant -- the last lonely elephant
oneLiner: Just how many Knysna elephants are there left?
summary:
SANParks, who are the controlling authority of not just the forests, but also the Garden Route lakes system, says that their camera traps and evidence collected by rangers indicates that only one cow still survives, a 45-year-old matriarch who is reaching the end of her reproductive years. But naturalist and conservationist, Gareth Patterson, disputes this, saying his research indicates there are five or six surviving elephants. Patterson’s work in the Knysna forests has been documented in “The Search for the Knysna Elephants”, a documentary screened internationally by Animal Planet. His elephant research is ongoing, alongside research into another mysterious denizen of the southern Cape, the relatively unknown coastal leopards.Unfortunately Patterson claims set back attempts to remedy the lonely elephants situation, his study created the impression there was a family of both male and females that could survive for hundreds of years.

This week SANparks confirmed something they have suspected for the last 20 years -there is only one Knysna elephant and is now the last free-roaming and most isolated elephant in the world. She is the last survivor from herds that once roamed the forests, the rest have been hunted out. Elephants are social creatures, especially female elephants, they move in family groups, but this poor female has spent the last 20 lonely years hiding in the deep impenetrable indigenous forests above Knysna and Sedgefield. The elusive Knysna elephants have become figures of folk law, forests creatures that appear and disappear. For years the numbers have been debated, and can they save themselves? Are there both male and females and with protection like the Addo elephant will their numbers recover? In 1920 when they establish Addo Elephant Park there were 16 elephants now there are 480. This week SANParks confirmed, that their camera traps, set up along ancient elephant paths, recording her movements for the last 15 months, only capture one female. The forest is so dense there are only certain routes and they have mapped them extensively, and not once over 4 years has another elephant ever been captured. It comes on the back of the Landmark Foundations study, done two years done prior to this study, which also recorded only one female. These elephants evolved within this forest terrain and this is our last opportunity to re-establish a population with the resident genetics. But why keep searching for the elephants? So much time and money have been spent to the existence of the elephant because they are the most southern free ranging elephants and have a specific genetic adaptation to existing in the forest despite being Savannah elephants and they play a critical role is this lush eco-system. Time is running out and Patterson "find" of 5 elephants and possibly one male has only set back the efforts to intervene. Extensive consultation is taking place with all the stake holders around the forest about how they can reintroduce more elephants. The Addo to Eden corridor is a conservation project that hopes to open the passage but that is a long way off. Conservationist are asking how much more evidence do we need before we do something to rescue the last remaining forest elephant from a extinction? What now that they have confirmed their suspicion? What urgent action? What is the update in the stakeholder involvement? The camera traps has also documented other threatened species like the coastal leopard, ratels, blue duiker giving conservationists far more information about the habitat than they had before and now they have footage to prove it.

title: PurrPaws For LIfe
oneLiner: Two weeks ago, an animals shelter South of Joburg burnt down - animals died, and donated began flowing in. But now allegations of years of serious abuse and,now, arson are swirling around the centre.
summary:
The SPCA has given us access to their files on her - years of abuse from 2012 - January 2019 - the warnings range from serious abuse - animals that are sick not getting veterinary care, hundreds of animals being put down etc continual sickness amongst animals - especially cats (snuffles, oozing eyes etc), dogs fighting and malnourished - she often has numerous dogs in different cages who fight and are then mortally injured. There are warnings (all acknowledged and signed by her) that show the issues brought up after the fire have been going on for years. Shortly after the fire Kitten and Cat rescue gave evidence of serious abuse of the cats - those photo's were posted by the SPCA in response to the public asking why they had not stepped in. Turns out they were intending to shut her down before the mysterious fire. About the fire - Lindie says it was caused in the upstairs linen room by rats chewing cables, but arson investigators were called to the scene. We will ask the police for an update on that investigation. Turns out, it wasn't the rescue centre that was on fire, but her personal house.

Carte Blanche investigates whether PurrPaws for life owner - Lindi van Rooyen - made hundreds of animals suffer years of abuse from willful neglect (2012-2019) - and then decided to end it all by setting her house on fire. We all know her story - on Jan 30 2019, it was reported that the shelter at PurrPaws burnt down killing roughly 30 animals, call for the public to come save the animals and make donations came in. Roughly a million is account for with online postings, but since then she has gotten rid of almost 800 animals. Allegations then began by various shelters who received these animals - that there were not neutered, were pregnant, were badly injured, were very diseased, malnourished. The questions began - how did the fire start, why did lindie have so much time to remove her personal animals from the house, her furniture, her TV etc, First responders said the workers said she was seen where the fire started shortly before it went up in flames, and that they had been sent to fix a fence at the bottom of the garden. Neighbours said she often wasn't there, and neglected the animals - often hiding injured/sick ones from the SPCA when they came for inspections. Turns out the SPCA have been investigating her for years responding to numerous complaints.

experts: Mr. Jaco Pieterse NSPCA

title: Wild Animals in Cages - Inside SA Zoos
oneLiner: Do our municipalities have the resources to manage our zoos effectively?
summary:
For weeks the debate has raged around Lammie the elephant cow at the Johannesburg Zoo. Her partner died last year and animal welfare organisations are calling for her to be moved to a sanctuary where she can be with other elephants and rewilded to some extent. But the City of Johannesburg is adamant that Lammie will stay at the zoo. But the issue around whether or not we should have zoos is not clear cut. Some people hail their educational value whilst others see them as cruel and dated. The fact is we still have zoos all over South Africa and our municipalities have a duty to look after the animals in their care. Last year Bloemfontein Zoo was in the news because of filth and lack of food for the animals. This sparked a campaign against the zoo and municipality, but although the noise has died down, we take a look to see if the animals are truly taken care of. In Gauteng, both the Joburg and Pretoria zoos are commended for their more modern approach to keeping animals. Cages and pit enclosures have been exchanged for habitat-simulating enclosures and for the most part the animals are given "toys" for stimulation. The enclosures are generally kept clean and there doesn't seem to be issues with providing food. The worst transgressing zoo at the moment seems to be the East London Zoo. Residents, activists and animal welfare organisations have been calling for the zoo's closure for quite some time. Middle last year one of the zoo's brown bears was first spotted with paralysed hind legs - Jenny had been at the zoo, living in a cement pit enclosure for more than 35 years. She was euthanised and now her daughter, Gina is the only remaining bear at the zoo. Witnesses and video footage shows the bear in poor condition, with almost nothing to stimulate her. The water in the moat within her enclosure is filthy.

Zoos across the country have come under the spotlight as more and more people see them as inhumane and cruel. But although there is an argument for their educational value, the very least they can do is make sure the animals are kept in as comfortable surroundings as possible, and well cared for. While some zoos are managing to provide habitat-simulating enclosures and adequate stimulation, others are housing their menageries in small cages and the condition of the animals says it all. But who is responsible for the welfare of the animals in our zoos as well as enforcing the law, and how can it be allowed that a brown bear lives in a cement pit for more than three decades?

title: Flamingo Rescue
oneLiner: People from all walks of life stand together to save hundreds of lessor flamingo chicks.
summary:
The Kamfers Dam outside Kimberley is drying up fast. It is home to approximately 60,000 lesser flamingoes and they have been breeding at the dam for about 30 years. The dam is one of only four breeding sites for the lesser flamingo in the world. But disaster has struck. A vast area where the flamingoes have nested has dried out completely, leaving nests exposed. During the hot days the flamingoes leave their nests to move to the the small area that still has water leaving the chicks and eggs exposed. Eggs are breeding out and the chicks are vulnerable. In some instances the chicks are so dehydrated from the heat that they are unable to hatch themselves. Now the community of Kimberley have come together and have collected about 3,000 chicks so far. They are being cared for at the Kimberley SPCA, and flown to various rehab centres across the country. So far, about 1,400 chicks are at Mike Bolhuis' farm just north of pretoria, where he has hired experts to help look after the chicks.

Community organisations, the SPCA in Kimberley, conservationists and private individuals are standing together to rescue more then 1000 lesser flamingo chicks are dying in the scorching heat just outside Kimberley. Volunteers from the community of Kimberley have been collecting newly hatched chicks from their abandoned nests and taking them to the local SPCA where they are hydrated, fed and looked after a local vet. Some 900 chicks were flown to Wonderboom Airport where they are being taken care of by Mike Bolhuis on his private property. The rest of the chicks are said to go to various wildlife rehabilitation centres across the country. Experts say if the rain stays away the pan could be completely dry within 2 to 4 weeks, forcing the adult flamingoes to move away.

title: Brainternet
oneLiner: The future of human integrated technology is here - In a world exclusive Carte Blanche shows local wits students together with singularity university use a brain to communicate with the internet.
summary:
By the 2030s we will be able to connect our brains to the internet via nanobots that will “provide full-immersion virtual reality from within the nervous system, provide direct brain-to-brain communication over the internet, and otherwise greatly expand human intelligence.” What is consciousness? We might be one step closer to understanding the brain and therefore understanding our conscious minds. Two years ago, Prof. Adam Pantanowitz and two 4th year students at Wits were able to start bridging the gap between having our brains communicate with computers. They were able to …explain The "Brainternet" project streams brainwaves onto the internet. Essentially, it turns the brain into an Internet of Things (IoT) node on the World Wide Web. IoT refers to connecting any device with an on and off switch to the internet. This technology has Global applications – medical diagnostics with epilepsy, hospitals had to induce seizures, but now they can diagnose remotely with a wearable device and live stream to early warn a patient, and even intervene at their location. Social applications – to be able to communicate remotely – we have been working through smartphones but we not it would just be wirelessly connected to your brain through an implant.

Now in a world first and Carte Blanche exclusive we’ll show how Adam Pantanowitz and team have taken this one step further – in a soon to published paper that has been submitted to a journal, they can show a brain transmitting information between two computers. This is called the brain network - The footage is exclusive! This project uses two computers which were disconnected (no network connection, no wifi, no cables), the students encoded into flashing light information like the word hello/goodby (flashing light is similar to morse code and the signal is picked up by the cortex in the back of the brain), that word was then transmitted via the flashing light through the eye by looking at the light, to the back of the brain, called the visual cortex, now the technique is not new, but the transmission of the word from computer 1 to computer 2 through the human brain is a world first and entirely unique. It effectively turned the human brain into a non-cognitive passive network, and we were able to connect the two distinct computers without using traditional means, passing on information. Brainternet works by converting electroencephalogram (EEG) signals (brain waves) in an open source brain live stream. A person wears a powered, mobile, internet accessible Emotiv EEG device for an extended period. During this time, the Emotiv transmits the EEG signals to a Raspberry Pi – a credit card sized little computer - live streams the signals to an application programming interface (code that allows software programmes to communicate), and displays data on a website that acts as a portal. This is currently an open website where the public can observe the individual’s brain activity. Brainternet seeks to simplify a person’s understanding of their own brain and the brains of others. It does this through continuous monitoring of brain activity as well as enabling some interactivity. Brainternet can be further improved to classify recordings through a smart phone app that will provide data for a machine-learning algorithm. In future, there could be information transferred in both directions – inputs and outputs to the brain. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X3-jRdZEA_Y https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LSdN--axYbA Brainternet makes the uploading of your brain similar to an iot.

title: Art Theft
oneLiner: South africa is a mecca for art thieves, Carte Blanche delves into the art theft world - how they do it, where they sell it, and ask why art is one of the best illicit currency's in the world.
summary:
Art theft is not a common crime, but when the thieves hit, they hit big – often amounting to millions of irreplaceable stolen art or artifacts. According to Robert Pearson, of Pearson and associates, the expert investigators of art thefts (specific) there are various kinds of thieves – 1. opportunists who see it as an easy buck, but are often caught because they don’t know where to sell it, and often end up getting caught by auction houses or pawn shops, these paintings are sometimes destroyed/abandoned to void being caught with the artwork and sometimes end up in private homes for display purposes And 2. Selective targeting of specific pieces, artists, museums and collectors. This can take place at museums, galleries, and private residences. All thefts are limited due to security, often theft by a trust employee who forms a close relationship with the target is a common trend. Pearson has a good network of contacts to circulate the details of a piece with reward money often, often resulting in recoveries. There are some preventative measures: security, good CCTV camera surveillance, motion detected surveillance. Exhibitions, auctions and private viewings that are advertised tend to lure in the criminal element – we need to be careful without program. International criminals are known to frequent SA, and through local crime syndicates, identify and target arts and private collections – either well-known or up and coming artists, as well as specific collections.

we have the footage of an art heist at Davielle Ballie gallery when it was still in Norwood. It has since moved to Jeppe and is in an up-and-coming artistic area – we will be filming the interviews there in a beautiful backdrop of artwork and creativity. We can interview Darren (owner)/Matthew (curator) from the gallery about the theft that will be shown on the TV. They are happy to accommodate all our interviews there, as we can film links there as well. They are seeing if we can speak to the artist whose works were specifically targeted – the footage shows men entering the premises pretending to be security guards, once inside, they take out guns and go for the art work they specifically wanted. John Pearson (art investigator) will break down the theft and speak about what happened after – he says they then went to a nearby house, and couldn’t find a buyer. They then contacted a local artist who sells his art at Killarney Mall, he took the paintings, not knowing they were stolen, and was sitting with them to sell. He recognized that one of them had a number of the back, and it was the gallery – they then sent Pearson to go and see – all 5 paintings worth R500,000 were recovered. There are lots of other cases in South Africa regarding art theft – one of the most perplexing was the one where Ace Magashule gave a Pierneef work R2.5 million to a bodyguard when he was moving office. The bodyguard gave it to an auction house, that recognized it and returned the painting.

title: Pat Lambie - the babyfaced assassin retires
summary:
Lambie, who is currently contracted to French club, Racing 92, said on Saturday he was retiring on medical advice, telling French news outlet Le Equipe that he had already contemplated retirement before arriving in France after three concussions in South Africa, "two of them serious." After the last, in May 2017, he didn’t play for six months. He suffered a further concussion in December 2017. The symptoms lasted 40 days. He said that the repeat concussions had caused “trembling legs, headaches, migraines and eye irritations. I have not been able to do any weight sessions in the last two and a half months because I had a terrible headache. “I followed the advice of two neurologists. They advised me to stop rugby.” The 28-year-old spent several months out of the game after taking a horrible knock to his head in a collision with South African-born Ireland flank CJ Stander in a Test at Newlands in June 2016. He struggled with concussion-related symptoms since that incident and again suffered a heavy head knock when he collided with Sharks team-mate Rhyno Smith during a Super Rugby clash against the Southern Kings in May 2017. Lambie is widely regarded as one of South Africa’s most talented backline players in recent history because despite his relatively small stature – 86kg, and 1.77m – he is able to play at just about any backline position, switching easily from flyhalf to fullback, and is a deadly kicker.

The decision by charismatic Sharks and Springbok flyhalf and fullback Pat Lambie to retire from professional rugby at the age of 28 has focused attention sharply on the problem of concussion in professional contact sport – especially rugby. He played 56 matches for South Africa.

title: Drugs Lessons from Lisbon
oneLiner: After exposing the growing drug problem in Durban's famed Marine Parade, we travel to Lisbon to see the startling impact of one of the world's most progressive drug policies.
summary:
Portugal's success in overcoming a significant drug - mostly heroin - problem stems from a change in attitude. Initially, resources were poured into policing the problem as the country followed the global trend in criminalising drug use. But, after little to no success, it was decided to treat drug addiction as a medical rather than a criminal issue. Drug use (not sale) was de-criminalised, and resources diverted to assisting users into overcoming their addictions. The result - while not perfect - has been miraculous. Small wonder then that other countries are looking to Portugal as a blueprint in trying to bring their own drug problems under control. In a recent Carte Blanche expose on the drug use and criminality currently taking place in the streets behind the famous hotels along the Marine Parade, a city official suggested the drug problem would solve itself once development of the Point area got underway. It appeared a short-sighted approach. Far from solving the issue it would, at best, move it to a different part of the city. In this insert, we'll ask whether the experience of a country like Portugal might provide a more pragmatic and lasting solution.

In the 70's and 80's Portugal was overrun by drug peddlers. Astonishingly, as many as one in 100 Portuguese was addicted to heroin and the scourge became a drain on the country's limited resources. But, thanks to forward-thinking policy makers, the situation has been turned around and the country is respected globally for its rational and humane approach to drug addiction. We'll see first-hand whether the Portuguese approach might provide a blueprint for turning the tide in the drug-trade in places like Durban.

title: Greener On The Other Side
oneLiner: We travel to Europe's greenest city and ask: What's stopping South Africa's towns from cleaning up their act?
summary:
This is a story about the type of green future that is possible with a little foresight, planning and political will. Vaxjo is a shining light in a country that has made clear its intention to unburden itself of fossil fuels within the next few years. So precise has its vision become, that it even takes steps to mitigate the environmental impact of modern construction methods. We will be taken on a tour of the city and shown the initiatives and technologies that have made it Europe's greenest. But, this is also a story about a country that is being left behind in the race for carbon neutrality. South Africa is still largely reliant on fossil fuels and one of its provinces holds the inglorious title as the world's most polluted. Recent satellite imagery highlighted alarming levels of Nitrogen Di Oxide in the atmosphere - a direct consequence of the province's positioning at the centre of coal-fired energy provision. It is the antithesis of Vaxjo. Vested interests, misunderstanding, misdirection and fear have all contributed to a widespread distrust of clean energy and its independent producers. So, can South Africa produce its own Vaxjo? And, if not, what will the consequence be of a failure to convince Eskom, the mines and the unions that this is the only way forward?

Sweden's Vaxjo claims to be Europe's greenest city. It is carbon neutral, runs its transport network on recycled waste and uses the latest construction techniques to limit the environmental impact of its own expansion. This will be a first-hand view of the type of future all cities should aspire to, and provides the prefect yardstick against which to measure South Africa's cities and towns.

title: Kuils River Pollution.
oneLiner: The impact of the pollution and the experiences of people living alongside Cape Town's Kuils River is described as "Apocalyptic" by experts.
summary:
The City of Cape Town is undertaking a health survey to investigate the concerns of the community. A step long overdue. How long it will take the council to act is not known. The City denies that its handling of sewage is negligent. The pollution has impacted on marine life in False Bay. Ibuprofen has been found in huge levels in snoek. Pharmaceutical products aren't the only substances which can't be adequately processed by plants such as Zandvliet. There are findings of traces of caffeine in sea urchins. The City of Cape Town claims the problem is caused by informal settlements and unplanned development by residents of the catchment area which extends northwards from Khayelitsha towards Kuils River. The human waste from these "illegal settlements" and Cape Town's rapid population growth is also contributing to the contamination of the river.

For years, scientists and the communities living next to the Kuils River near Macassar CT, have expressed concern that the sewage flowing into the river from a nearby waste water treatment plant is both an environmental and a health hazard. The people of Sandvlei below the discharge point from the Zandvliet facility, are suffering from numerous medical complaints so severe that they have even resulted in surgical intervention due to E.coli poisoning. The City of Cape Town claimed for many years that the facility only discharges treated effluent. However recently the council conceded that "sub-standard" treated effluent is leaving the plant. Nothing has been done about it. Chemicals and the effluent have also had a detrimental effect of marine life in False Bay.

title: Will Endley
summary:
William Endley is a 56 year old retired SANDF colonel. He was sentenced to death in February 2018 and suddenly set free in November 2018 as part of a peace deal between warring factions in South Sudan. After his retirement from the SANDF he was involved with mine clearing operations in Iraq. Endley was employed as an advisor in South Sudan in 2015. Because of his experience in integrating non statutory forces in the post 1994 South African National Defence Force, Endley was an ideal advisor to then deputy president, Dr Riek Machar. South Sudan has been mired in conflict for decades, Machar is a leader of the SPLM (Sudan Peoples Liberation Movement) he was appointed deputy president after the Compromise Peace Deal. It was at this time that Endley started working in South Sudan. The peace agreement did not last and it didn’t take long for hostilities to flare up again. President Salva Kiir accused Machar of plotting to overthrow his government. Machar fled to South Africa where he is still under “house arrest”, Will Endley and others were arrested and detained. For two years Endley was kept in horrific conditions. He was basically left to die. Endley’s sister Charmaine initiated a campaign to free her brother. It took two years for Endley to get his day in court. He was found guilty. A charge of attempting to overthrow the government, led to a sentence of death by hanging. Shocked family and friends resorted to petitioning government. Then, unexpectedly a peace agreement was signed by the warring factions in South Sudan and president Kiir ordered that Will Endley should be released, within days he was back in South Africa. Will Endley is a father, grandfather and sees himself as a peacekeeper, it just happened that he found himself on the wrong side. He’s presently in Cape Town where he is contemplating the future that he did not have two weeks ago.

the first television interview with Col Will Endley after he's released from death row in South Sudan. Will is well spoken, has an unfortunate moustache and should work well on camera. The idea is to get his sister Charmaine to expound on the anxiety, fear and hopeless sense of loss that Endley’s incarceration brought upon her. Her own career and family suffered immensely during the last few years. The story will be filmed in Cape Town Will Endley wrote some poetry during his incarceration. During my tenure at the NSS and later at the JCP, my future and prospects were very bleak. I composed a poem and left it with a friend for safekeeping and, if need be, to send it to my sister.

In November 2016 Carte Blanche investigated claims that the city of Johannesburg’s valuation department had been defrauded by half a billion rand when an employee had decreased the values of 22 buildings – so that the owners would pay less rates and taxes. title: BODY CORPORATE NIGHTMARES
oneLiner: Buying sectional title have several pro's and con's and you should properly weigh up the options before making a decision.
summary:
BODY CORPORATE RULES: The Sectional Titles Act states that a scheme's rules are binding on the body corporate, the owner of the property and the persons who are occupying the property, that is the tenants. The rules and regulations of any particular complex may change, and even though all sectional title investors or owners may not necessarily agree with the changes, they would not have the power to change them individually. Owners of sectional title units also do not have the freedom to alter, renovate or expand their sections without the approval of the body corporate. In addition, all the owners are jointly and separately liable for the debt of the body corporate, which means that if an owner does not pay his/her share, it may become the other owners' problem as well. There are several advantages as well as disadvantages of buying sectional title homes and prospective buyers need to do their homework in order to make an informed choice. Once you're in, you are in and you have to abide by the body corporate's management and conduct rules and this of often where war starts to rage...

Buying sectional title have several pro's and con's and you should properly weigh up the options before making a decision. Sectional title describes the separate ownership of a unit within a group-owned complex or development. The owner of the unit automatically becomes part of the body corporate, which is the legal entity that owns and controls the common property in the sectional-title scheme. The body corporate lays down the rules that have to be adhered to by all the owners in the development. In addition, owners are obliged to pay levies according to the size of their units (those with smaller units pay lower levies). These levies are calculated in accordance with a budget, which is prepared annually by the trustees or agent. WHAT LEVIES ARE NORMALLY FOR: The levy usually includes the insurance premiums, maintenance of the common property, wages and salaries of cleaners, security and other staff involved in maintaining the common property, as well as any water and electricity required for the common property. Owners of sectional schemes usually only need to pay for their rates and taxes, insurance for the contents of their home, their own private gardens and for their monthly electricity and water consumption. The specifics may differ slightly from complex to complex. Bodies Corporate have to abide by certain legislation - especially if the body corporate wants to enact rules and regulations not stipulated by the Acts that govern them. But they often don't follow these procedures, and with most sectional title owners not knowing what their rights are or what the legislation stipulates, they could easily be abused. title: Comeback Noni
oneLiner: In the new year, South Africa’s own World Boxing Champion Noni Tenge is scheduled to defend her WBF title in Las Vegas. But Noni’s comeback trail has been a long trek in the wilderness.
summary:
South African Noni Tenge is World Boxing Champion - "She Be Stinging”. Her alias is in homage to Muhammed Ali - he who "floats like a butterfly, stings like a bee". In contrast to Ali, Noni, winner of no less than 5 different World Titles, as a South African female boxer is battling in the wilderness. She struggles to fund trips to her fights, which has cost her two of her titles. Noni has even had her government-funded educational diploma withheld because government has not paid the final installment. Despite women’s boxing only gaining broad acceptance in the 21st century, in other sports or in other countries, Noni Tenge would be a superstar sports woman and would not be living in her current flat-sharing accommodation. The winner of eight world title fights and with only one loss to her name, Noni is from the Eastern Cape. In 2011, Noni became the first female fighter to win the IBF Welterweight crown. Born in East London, known to the world as South Africa’s boxing capital, Noni Tenge debuted professionally in 2007 and has an outstanding record of eighteen wins, one defeat and a single draw from twenty outings (11 of her wins being by Knock Out). She is truly world class. Noni was one of five women boxers who put on an exhibition for parliament, at the invitation of President Mbeki, which inspired government to legalize female boxing in 2001. However, seventeen years on, women boxers are struggling to have sustainable careers, with a lack of government support for even a champion like Noni, South Africa’s undisputed number one woman fighter. As she prepares for her next World Title fight, we interview Noni and witness her current training and living conditions. And as Noni continues to wait for the certificate confirming her successfully completed sports management diploma, we ask the Minister of Sport, Thokozile Xasa, why her department has withheld the final payments for Noni’s education.

Noni Tenge is one of the country's World Champion Sports Stars. But not only is she a World Boxing Champion, Noni is the holder of a Sports Management Diploma. Well, she would have the Diploma if the Minister of Sport would pay the last grant installments promised to her. Why is Noni so undervalued by South Africa?

After our story aired, most of the houses forcefully evicted by members of the EFF were reoccupied by the same tenants. Even landlords in upmarket areas face similar battles. Michelle Dickens from the TPN Credit Bureau monitors tenant behaviour in SA. She says 10% of tenants in SA are more than 3 months in arrears in South Africa. According to their data, problem tenants are in two categories - low end tenants who pay rental of R3000 per month and less, and high end tenants, who pay rental of more than R12 000. She has provided us with a landlord, Caroline, who is willing to be interviewed on the battles she has faced in getting tenants evicted in Up market Johannesburg suburbs. I am just waiting for her to contact me back, but Michelle has confirmed she will do interview.

Two oceans marathon winner Thulani Sibisi bought a house in Orlando in the same street where Walter Sisulu once lived. It was his dream to live out his last days next to where the famous SA icon once lived. But since buying his property four years ago, Thulani has never been able to occupy the home. A family member of the previous owner has occupied the house and refused to move. Despite four court ordered evictions, police have failed to keep the illegal tenants out. We accompanied Thulani, the Sherrif and Public order policing units to serve the fourth eviction. But the tenant gathered support from the local community, and was able to break back into the house the very same day, chasing away Thulani's private security firm and reoccupying the home. Police stood by and did nothing despite our camera's presence.

title: Citizens Fight Back

The insert will reflect, through interviews and a re-enactment, on the moments four case studies were faced with this danger and bravely fought back. From the case studies we'll reflect on the following: - Have you ever been a victim of a hijacking before - In the moment that you realized something was wrong what did you and what did you think - Would you do things differently I suggest a re-enactment of the most daring cases study, Tiaan Coetzer and his wife, who upon realising that they were being followed hatched a plan to cunningly escape the hijackers. They reversed onto the hijackers before they pulling, leaving the hijackers bewildered and thawing their plan. The National Hijacking Prevention Academy provides demonstrative workshops on how motorist should respond during a hijacking situation. We'll film a demonstration, which will be conducted by representative Richard Brussow, get one on one interaction with Richard and the presenter in a car about the dos and donts. The academy's philosophy is that as a motorists you should not fight back but rather follow to calmly follow the instructions by the hijackers, without aggravating them. Richard Brussow is an insurance expert, who will comment on the consequences of a fight-back response during a hijacking. I expect him to speak to these few points: - What does an insurance company expect you to do during a hijacking situation - Are you penalized for fighting back (i.e no payout is made) any damages made to the car will be paid for by the driver - Do you risk increasing you premiums following a fight-back incident because you are now considered a high risk client - Can you present CCTV footage to support your claim The insert will include the CCTV footage of each case study.

Interviews with motorists who have been caught on CCTV camera daringly fighting back would be hijackers and escaping these dangerous situation. These videos have gone viral on social media, with users divided on whether this is a brave or an irresponsible move.

title: AI for Eyes
oneLiner: How 21st century tech is assisting the blind and visually impaired
summary:
Apps and smart devices have begun to dominate the way we interact with the world around us - and it's no different for people living with a visual impairment. From brand new (and pricey) wearable VR devices to smart refreshable braille (replacing 50s style braille typewriters) and even free apps, the world of assistive tech is expanding at a rapid pace - and perhaps even helping the blind to achieve a greater level of independence than ever before. We will look first at wearable devices, which have leveraged off the VR and MR technology released by Google and Microsoft in recent years. Although wearable VR did not take off as much as anticipated in the mainstream, it's had a big impact on assistive tech. We'll speak to two or three people who use different wearable devices about the impact they have had on their lives. We will also meet Mukthar Khan, who works for assistive tech company Sensory Solutions. He is blind himself and can talk about the challenges of being blind especially in SA, as well as the various devices developed to help. He will show us the refreshable braille device which allows import of text documents, note taking and interface with a phone - on one deceptively simple, small black box. He will also talk to us about the various apps that are available, often free of charge.

Low tech solutions like white canes, guide dogs and Braille have been around for decades or even centuries to help make life a little easier for those who cannot see. But a new wave of smart technology, machine learning and virtual reality devices is changing the way the visually impaired are accessing the world around them.

"Look, I go to work and at the end of the month tax comes off my salary. Then I go to the petrol station and I pay more tax. Then I buy groceries and I pay tax yet again. Why must I now pay more tax!" he asks. Since 2013, almost 70% of Gauteng's three million highway users have refused to pay their e-toll bills, which has left SANRAL the road agency with a headache. They are facing downgrades, they cant raise money on the bond markets, and they are deeply in debt. So much so the new finance minister Tito Mboweni has just announced a R5 billion rand bailout in his MTBPS. Ironically all this could have been avoided if government had taken OUTA'S advice in 2013 and added 10cents to the fuel levy to pay off the roads. Had they done so, by now the entire debt will have been paid off. Instead the GFIP has become the ANC's Gauteng failure - and they are now sitting with a R67 billion rand debt.

title: ERMELO PONZI SCHEME
oneLiner: When someone you trust offers you the opportunity to invest money and receive an extraordinary monthly return on your investment, why would you let the opportunity slip?
summary:
-An application to liquidate - or wind-up - Love and Let's Live Pty (Ltd), the company belonging to A'riel Willem Theron - a 30-year old resident from Ermelo who operated a so-called "Ponzi scheme" with 1 356 investors' money - was brought by creditors as an urgent application in the Pretoria High Court on 6 December 2017 -A provisional liquidation order was issued by the Pretoria High Court on 30 January 2018 -A Final liquidation order was issued on 16 March 2018 -The effective date of the liquidation of LLL was on 6 December 2017 - the date on which the urgent application was heard by the Pretoria High Court -On 6 February 2018, Hannes Muller and Lariska Arends from the Tshwane Trust in Pretoria were appointed as the provisional liquidators of LLL -Muller and Arends immediately started to act according to the insolvency legislation - seizing assets and financial records of LLL. They also approached the High Court to ask for permission to start formal and official questioning of related individuals -The liquidators don't know what the current whereabouts of Theron are - he earlier informed them via email that he is "now living a wanderer's lifestyle in South America", and he refused to provide the liquidators with any information to assist them with their investigation -The financial records were investigated and forensic report was written containing information about how money flowed in the company -1 357 Investors paid over a total amount of R290 390 780 to LLL -According to a written agreement between investors and LLL, a return in investment of between 72 and 96% would have been derived from trade in foreign currency -From the financial records, it seems that only 5,12% of investors' money LLL received was in fact used to trade in foreign currency AND these investments were traded against a loss

When someone you trust offers you the opportunity to invest money and receive an extraordinary monthly return on your investment, why would you let the opportunity slip? More than 1300 investors countrywide, with almost half of them based in the small Mpumalanga town of Ermelo, invested a total of R282 million in two years in a company called "Love and Let's Live" belonging to Ermelo resident, Andre Willem Theron, who renamed himself A'ri'El Willem Theron. Theron promised an 8% monthly return on investment - and as a ponzi scheme works, delivered that to earlier investors promptly. The deal was to trade the money in foreign currencies. It was a scheme of epic proportions. Theron - in letters to investors and the attorney working with the liquidators - denied ever running a ponzi scheme, ever planning a scheme, but "innocently" wrote several letters to investors when the bomb burst apologising for the loss of their money, said he was "very sorry", "would give his life to them, but unfortunately had to leave the country to start a new life and was now making a nomadic existence in South America". Investors have opened five separate criminal cases with the SAPS, but nothing has come of it... Love and Let's Live has finally been liquidated in July 2018 and Theron has been sequestrated. R15 million has flowed to his close family members. R6 million salaries were paid out in two years. Theron falsified a Forex Trading account statement which he showed to investors in December 2017, that stated there was USD110 million in the account, when in fact there was only USD353 in the account. The forensic audit states that only 1,5% of the total amount invested was in fact traded on foreign currencies and this was done at a loss. So what happened to all the money?

title: Borer Beetles
oneLiner: A tiny alien beetle is threatening to change our urban landscapes forever....
summary:
OPENING LINK - trees - Thhis is the most beautiful time of the year in Johannesburg, but imagine this view without the trees. A tiny alien is infecting our trees, a potential catastrophy for urban and natural forests. Seq - Tree pests are nothing new - the price we pay for globalisation… Dedicated team at Pretoria University - FABI Some of FABI Successes…. but now they have a new enemy... Trudy Paap discovered the beetle. Wilhelm de Beer and his team are tracking the process. - we look at the beetle, how to identify, how it reproduces, the symbiotic fungus and damage caused. We also look at the people and the work they put in - the hours of dedication it takes to fight such a tiny enemy - they will also show us a process of innoculating trees which they are currently testing. They will show the beetle under the microscope, DNA sequencing, symbiotic fungus. Spread of the beetle - KNP, Northern Cape, KZN, Western Cape, Limpopo… How it spreads Food security? We chat to FABI about the possible infestation of fruit tree crops. (maize and wheat are fine, but many fruit trees are suseptable) Joburg, threat to the Urban forest - speak to City Parks — what people must do if they have infested trees. How to minimise the threat. WHAT NOT TO DO. Introduction of dedicated sites where people can take felled trees. Hylton Fryar - App developed for reporting possible infestation - more than 300 users of the app - key to identifying the spread of the beetle. Neil Hill - Joburg Urban Forest Alliance - shows infected trees. Felling Back to FABI, what they do when people report the infestation. The future - how the beetle can be stopped - possible biocontrol — Biologists think that minute parasitic wasps, which are known to attack ambrosia beetles in their native range, could be introduced to South Africa, but these first need to be thoroughly studied to make sure they won’t also attack indigenous South African beetles. Threat to indigenous forests.

The Polyphagous Shothole Borer (PSHB), is a sesame seed-sized beetle that infests more than 200 tree species from 58 families. The beetle bores into the tree and lays its eggs. But it is not this damage that kills the tree. The beetle travels with a range of symbiotic fungi and it is one strain of the fungus, which the larvae feeds on once they hatch that causes harm to the tree. A dedicated team of scientists - under the leadership of Prof Wilhelm de Beer from FABI is working to find a way to evict the PSHB from Urban forests, our fruit trees and natural forests.

title: Nugent Commission - SARS
oneLiner: SARS has been marred by allegations of corruption and staff exodus recently. Failing to meet its tax collection targets for 3 consecutive years, how will a crippled tax institution impact the taxpayer
summary:
When a government institution fails to achieve its core mandate as such with SARS it is a cause for concern. SARS’ main objective is to collect tax revenue for the state, which they have failed to do efficiently for the past three years. The troubles at SARS began with the appointment of Mr Tom Moyane who became SARS commissioner on the 27th of September 2014. Under Mr Moyane’s stewardship the institution has regressed with allegations of corruption, procurement irregularities and staff intimidation from the commissioner himself and his enforcers. This prompted President Cyril Ramaphosa to initiate a commission looking into SARS led by former Judge, Robert Nugent, dubbed the Nugent Commission.

The South African Revenue service is a pivotal institution to the stability of the country. In the past few years as with many other state institutions, SARS has been in the media for all the wrong reasons. From allegations of rogue units to the failure to meet its tax collection targets three years in a row with some of its staff members testifying at the Nugent commission that SARS’ shortfalls are also key to the increase of VAT. How did an institution that is so integral to the welfare of the country get so crippled?

title: Drought Aid
oneLiner: They are called the ‘fodder boys.’ A group of youngsters from the Cape flats giving hope to farmers who are facing the worst drought in 200 years and are unable to feed their animals.
summary:
Imtiaz Sooliman is the founder Gift of the Givers, a nonprofit organisation that move into areas where disaster has struck and people have lost everything. Instead of despair, they bring relief. From victims of fire to areas where drought has claimed its toll, they work tirelessly to help those in need. In January this year Sooliman looked at the youngsters in Hannover who live in fear of gangsters and drug lords and tasked Ali Sablay from the organization to select a group of youngsters from Hanover Park to join the organisation as volunteers. The Western Cape has been called the murder capital of South Africa. Ten of the 30 police stations with the highest incidence of murder are found in this province and 808 gang related murders alone last year. For the community of Hannover there is little hope of leading a peaceful life and the prospect of work. It is against this landscape that Sablay took the 10 youngsters under his wing. None of them had any prospect of work but already the burden of responsibility were weighing heavily on their shoulders; parents and younger siblings were looking at them to put bread on the table. Set against this backdrop the fodder boys were formed and started working for Gift of the Givers.

Farmers are on their knees praying for rain. Drought has taken its toll in large parts of the country. Sutherland has seen the worst: farmers have sold their prize animals for as little as R30 to avoid starvation. Hope came in the form of the fodder boys: A group of young men rescued from Hannover on the Cape Flats by an NGO who are now delivering feed to desperate farmers in drought crisis. In Sutherland alone sheep stock have dropped from 400 000 to 104 000. Some farmers have sold up their last belongings and moved to start a new life, but for most of them there is no alternative. Farming is in their blood and survive they will. The fodder boys have changed their lives and made it bearable as they receive feed to keep their animals alive until the rain comes back again.

title: THE TWO-BOOK BANK
oneLiner: The men who gave a new meaning to bank robbery. In what is described as one of the most daring heists SA has ever seen, how exactly was almost R2 billion looted?
summary:
In 1982, VBS was established as the Venda Building Society - as a mutual fund in which one could deposit savings or buy shares. VBS came to prominence in 2016 when it granted a R7.8 million loan to former president Jacob Zuma to settle debt relating to the upgrades to his Nkandla home. Despite the Municipal Finance Management Act (MFMA) forbidding municipalities to invest with mutual banks, many did. In early 2017, Treasury issued an instruction to municipalities to stop investing with the institution. As a result, a number of councils withdrew more than R1 billion from the bank. The Reserve Bank in March this year and put the bank under curatorship amid a liquidity crisis. In April this year, the Reserve Bank of SA launched an investigation under the leadership of adv Terry Motau SC en the firm Werksmans. A provisional report into fraud, probable money laundering and reckless business practices found that around 53 individuals unjustifiably and illegally received R1,89 billion between 2015 and 2018 and calls for them to be criminally charged, the money be recovered and VBS be closed. “It is corrupt and rotten to the core. Indeed, there is hardly a person in its employ in any position of authority who is not, in some way or other, complicit,” adv Motau said. The report states that “the overwhelming evidence that has been gathered, from numerous sources, reveals (VBS chairperson Tshifhiwa) Matodzi be the kingpin in the fraudulent and theftuous conduct of VBS’ business. He, his companies, and his associates have been positively identified as the main beneficiaries of the massive fraud”. According to the Curator’s application to liquidate Vele Investments, “the bank has been the victim of a large scale fraud that has caused the bank a losss in excess of at least R1,5 billion and Vele has participated in and benefitted from the aforesaid fraud”. (p12)

The men who gave a new meaning to bank robbery. In what is described as one of the most daring heists SA has ever seen, how exactly was almost R2 billion looted, fictitious accounts and overdrafts created and how was the majority of shares in the bank bought with non-existing money? It takes a masterplan for a heist to succeed. Meticulous and detailed planning. The right move at the exact right time. Roleplayers have to come together to successfully execute the plan -- each one playing their own part. Putting together the pieces in what ultimately lead to the collapse of VBS reads like a movie script – the masterplan for a successful heist. We will do a story on who the kingpin and roleplayers are, how they planned the heist, how they executed it, how it worked, how much money was stolen, in which manner it was stolen, from whom it was stolen. We will compare the lavish lifestyles of the perpetrators against those from whom were stolen - now left in the dark and destitute. What are those on the ground who have lost everything saying and is there any recourse for them? What happens now - will there be prosecution?

title: OLX Gang
oneLiner: We expose a dangerous syndicate who hold innocent victims who advertised vehicles for sale online, hostage at gunpoint and force them to empty out their bank accounts.
summary:
He asks them to remove the ads online. He tells them to meet him at a shopping center in Van der Bijl Park where they can sign a sales contract and he will pay the money over to their accounts. Once they meet him at the shopping centre the story changes. He shows them a large amount of cash, and says he will pay them cash, but that they have to go fetch the rest of the money at a friend's house. They then drive him to a house (that we have identified) in Evaton. Once inside they show the victims another bag which supposedly contains rough diamonds and asks them if they will be interested in taking the diamonds as payment. At this point two men, dressed in full police uniforms appear, and accuse the victims of being involved in diamond smuggling. They separate the victims into two rooms, where they are told they will be taken to police station and repeatedly raped if they do not cooperate. They are physically assaulted and have guns pointed at them. They are then forced to transfer money from their bank accounts into the syndicates bank accounts. The syndicate also takes their bank cards to atms and withdraws cash. If the limits are reached, the syndicate will hold one victim hostage while another is driven to a bank where they are forced to withdraw any remaining funds under threat of having the remaining victim at the house shot. Once the victims have been robbed, they are let go, and warned that if they go to police they will be killed. The syndicate has their registration nr on their vehicle checked, and obtain personal info like street address and such about the victims. They are then told the usual "we know where you live"...

We have been approached by two case studies who have fallen victim to a syndicate using the exact same modus operandi to rob them. The syndicate approaches people who have advertised vehicles for sale online via sites like OLX and Gumtree. They employ the exact same tactics every time. A coloured man who speaks fluent afrikaans phones the victim, and he claims to be in South Africa from Namibia. He offers to buy the vehicle at the advertised price, but tells the victims they have to meet him in Van der Bijl Park as he is only in the country for a short time and does not have transport. He assures them he does not need to see the vehicle, and that he is a truck driver, and will come pick up the vehicle with the truck on the next visit to SA.

title: The ImPossible Tour
oneLiner: Grant Lottering has faced impossible odds on the bicycle - but he continues to push the boundaries of endurance.
summary:
Grant Lottering was a professional cyclist who in July 2013 was training for the world champs in a 140km preparation race in Trento, Italy. Rounding a corner in the rain at 60km/h he crashed into a rock embankment, collapsing his lungs and thorax, crushing his shoulder, fracturing 12 ribs, his spine, femur, scapula, clavicle, and sternum, rupturing arteries…His heart had stopped beating by the time the medical team arrived. He was told he was lucky to be alive and would never ride a bike again. But even while he was still in hospital, he swore he would return the next year to complete the race in which he had crashed and one year later, after six surgeries and 83 rehabilitation sessions, he completed the ride 170km La Marmotte through the Alps, then the Charly Gaul – the race in which he almost died. Over the following four years he has tackled one endurance feat after another, riding hundreds of kilometres through the Alps under conditions that have ranged from tricky to treacherous. He has not always succeeded - in 2017 he was forced to give up due to freezing temperatures and howling wind - but he has proved the ability of the human spirit to triumph over impossible odds.

IN 2013 former professional cyclist Grant Lottering almost died on the side of the road in Italy after a dramatic crash during preparation for the world champs. He was told he would never get on a bike again but he swore from his hospital bed to complete the race in which he had crashed - the next year, he did. Since then, he has completed one solo ultra-endurance feat after another and proved the strength of the human spirit.

title: Fuel Price Hikes 2018
oneLiner: October has heralded a record breaking fuel price of over R17 per litre, for South Africans. Experts say it's going to hit just about every aspect of our economy.
summary:
Since January this year South Africans have experienced 5 fuel hikes that have put our downward-spiraling economy into further perilous territory. In September, it looked like there was going to be some relief as a 35 cents/l fuel increase was abated, and at the last minute we saw an increase of only 4,90 c/l. But the Euphoria didn't last, October is seeing the fuel costs for ordinary consumers increase at around R1.00 /litre, pushing the cost of fuel to over R17,00 per litre. What has driven South African fuel prices out of control, and are there more hikes to come? Who is responsible and can something be done to halt the drain on our pockets? Is the fuel levy responsible for some of the high cost of our fuel? Carte Blanche takes a journey with ordinary consumers who have been hard hit and it seems have no other choice, but to bite the bullet.

The fuel levy is currently the fourth-biggest source of income for government after income tax, company tax and VAT. It contributes 5% to national tax revenue. It’s easy to collect and difficult to evade. It is a large contributor to South Africa's high cost in fuel and looks like it is here to stay, generating over R 70 billion in government revenue per year.

title: Bio Farming
summary: Science Fiction meets reality, we have done those stories internationally, and been amazed at the world of innovation being used in the medical arena. But right on our doorstep in Cape Town is a genuinely disruptive technology that is changing the way we make, store and distribute pharmaceuticals. In 2014 Belinda Shaw went to a TED talk in Cape Town, Prof Ed Rybicki from UCT took the floor, with two questions: What if there was a way to make complex pharmaceuticals inexpensive? What if we could do them right here in Cape Town, South Africa; the continent? Prof Ed Rybicki and his team at BRU (Biopharming Research Unit) had developed a world class way of developing vaccines and anti- bodies in tobacco plants (actually a weedy relative of the tobacco plant Nicotiana Benthamiana). BRU in fact held an incredible patent portfolio for their research which was being sold off shore for commercial production. FOR EXAMPLE: their key patent for developing flu vaccines in plants went overseas. There was very little local interest to develop their research from lab scale to commercial mainly due to the costs involved. Another case of incredible South African inventions, research and innovations that end up being made internationally. Belinda felt a critical need to retain valuable IP (Intellectual Property) where it belonged – in South Africa. She set about investigating, - the potential of commercialising Ed’s research…looking for funding, for partners, for clients. There was/and is no question that the technology developed by Ed and his team at BRU is disruptive technology in that plant made proteins (used to make vaccines and antibodies) can be made cheaper faster and safer and often better than the traditional way which needs vast funds to set up vast sterile laboratories with enormous steel containers/ fermenters.

title: Eating Insects
oneLiner: Could insects be a viable source of nutrition for the world's growing human population?
summary:
The insert will start with Presenter in the kitchen with Gourmet Entomophagist, Zayaan Khan in her kitchen, cooking a delicious meal. But the ingredients are not ordinary. Instead of a beef fillet the viewer is presented with a variety of edible insects. Zayaan will speak about her love for insects, why it makes sense to eat insects and the different flavours and uses. Then we move on, saying it's not just isolated cases... more and more people are turning to insect eating as a healthy protein alternative. Endoki is a urban cricket farm in Johannesburg that breeds crickets for human consumption. Samantha Jack will speak about the nutritional value of insects, especially crickets. (She is a food scientist) and they will show us the process of breeding crickets all the way to getting the crickets ready for consumption. They will also speak to the environmental impacts of eating insects. Instead of 13 kg of vegetation to produce 1kg of beef protein, it now takes just over 1kg of vegetation to produce a kilogram of cricket protein. They also need much less water and do not emit methane or ammonia - pollutants associated with the beef industry. Then we move to the FoodNext Africa Expo in Cape Town (28 & 29 Sept) where Gourmet Grub will be exhibiting their ice cream to the general public. They use larvae juice (entomilk) to make ice cream. So insects are not only for nutrition, but can also be enjoyed for their deliciousness. We speak to some of the general public at the Expo about their thoughts on Entomophagy and specifically the ice cream. We will also have an opportunity to interview Leah Bessa, the Head of Product Development who will explain how they "milk" black soldier fly larvae and where the idea came from. We will also film sections of the ice-cream making process. The insert ends back in Zayaan's Kitchen. The meal is prepared and the presenter is ready to taste - Yummy!

It is estimated that the world's population will reach 9 billion by the year 2050, and we will have to more than double food production by then in order to feed everyone on earth. The UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has been actively promoting the eating of insects - Entomophagy - since 2003. In Africa many people are already eating insects, but not as a regular intake of protein, and of course in the West this is only now starting to become a reality. In America and Europe there are now some companies breeding crickets and other insects to produce protein powder as a meal supplement and even protein bars. Here in South Africa the times are also changing. Gourmet Grub is a company in Cape Town that produces ice cream from entomilk - cricket juice. Cape Town also has it's very own Insect Chef, who serves a variety of dishes made from one of the 1000+ edible insects available. In Johannesburg is our country's first cricket farm, where crickets are bred for consumption whole and as a protein powder nutritional supplement.

title: SA Crime Statistics 2018
oneLiner: Crime statistics for 2018 have been released and paint a disquieting picture for South Africans' sense of safety. But could they be used to improve the way we fight crime?
summary:
Not only do the latest crime statistics paint a distressing picture for South Africans' security, but for some communities the murder rates even rival those of war torn countries. Limpopo on the other hand is the province with the lowest murder rate, only 15 per 100 000, as compared to the overall figure of 35.8 per 100 000 people murdered. From even these broad observations it is clear that the crime statistics can help target attention on certain communities. In other words the latest crime statistics are shocking and some of the highest we've seen in South Africa, but they could help in the way we fight crime says Dr Chris de Kock. However, the biggest problem especially when it comes to murder, aggravated robbery and rape, is there aren't enough sub categories within the statistics to formulate effective strategies for crime fighting and crime prevention. Even so the South African Police could be utilising the data more effectively. For example 2.6 percent of the country's police stations recorded 21% of the murders throughout the country, 13% of police stations recorded 50% of all murders, if the police were to target resources on these specific precincts with more vigour, they might be able to bring the overall crime rate down by a significant amount. What factors have driven up the numbers in serious crimes? Minister of Police Bheki Cele says, the police have dropped the ball. Carte Blanche takes a harder look at what it would really take to change the country's overall safety.

Even though the latest crime statistics are shocking and some of the highest we've seen in South Africa, can they help in the way we fight crime?

title: LAND REALITY
oneLiner: The issue of expropriation without compensation has inflamed emotions causing a worldwide debate. But we are going to look at the first farm that is CONFIRMED to be up for expropriation and the realit
summary:
According to Ernst Roets of AfriForum, minister of land development and reform Maite Nkoana-Mashabane said they put together a list of 139 farms earmarked for land expropriation without compensation. This has become a hotly contested debate. In Limpopo nine farms are earmarked for expropriation - Akkerland Broerdery’s farm is on the Afriforum list, but AgriSA are questioning the legitimacy of the list, adding that making the list public was irresponsible. According to AgriSA, a snap survey of the list exposed its inaccuracy, which could have been legitimized before it was made public. Investigations conducted by AfriSA’s affiliations show that some farms on the list are those belonging to black farmers with joint procurement. We would also speak to AFASA in Midrand - who are the African Farmers Association of South Africa – who will say how this will also affect black farmers as well – not just white farmers, and there are black farmers on the list.

Johan Steenkamp’s farm is being expropriated. He’s a well-known avocado farmer and founder of Peppadew in South Africa. He is a co-owner of Akkerland Boerdery, which farms on two properties, Lukin and Salaita, near Njeledam behind Soutpansberg. His business partner is his brother-in-law, Arnold Cloete. He says they are happy to sell the land for fair market value, but they are currently involved in two court battles – one against the expropriation of land involving the Musekwa community, and another to fight the expropriation without compensation of our land. Akkerland Boerdery was originally offered an allegedly ridiculous amount of money as compensation, after the land was initially expropriated in favour of the Musekwa community. According to Steenkamp, the offer was neither reasonable nor accurate in terms of the market value of the property, and they started a process to ascertain the legality of the offer in court. Even before this expropriation process began, the new minister of rural development and land reform, Maite Nkoana-Mashabane, let Akkerland know their farms would be expropriated. The court documents were delivered a day before Easter weekend, and they were given just seven days to hand over the keys to their farms. After an emergency interdict against the minister, a process is now under way to set aside the entire expropriation process involving the two farms. The Musekwa community do not have a title deed to the Lukin and Salaita farms. The Kuvule community, by contrast, produced allegedly legitimate title deeds to the land long before the expropriation took place. Their lawyers, Denga Incorporated, have confirmed the view that it is in fact their clients who have actual rights to the land. But there are also allegations that the mining corporation Coal of Africa may in fact be behind the expropriation action, and that this has nothing to do with historical land reform, and everything to do with mining. It is common knowledge that the Lukin and Salaita farms form part of the valuable coal belt in the region. This is the where the land expropriate fight is currently taking place – it’s not theoretical. Please also see below that Steenkamps neighbour’s property was part of a land claim and it’s now in ruins – that community will also speak.

title: Prescribed minimum benefits
oneLiner: Prescribed Minimum Benefits are intended to help those who are at their sickest and most vulnerable - but is the legislation doing what it's intended?
summary:
Anyone who can afford to, pays ever-increasing medical aid premiums as a safety net for the day that the worst happens and you are diagnosed with cancer or a chronic condition. 16% of the South African population is covered by private medical aid care. In 1998 legislation was gazetted to implement Prescribed Minimum Benefits: a list of chronic, emergency and acute conditions which must be covered in full for any patient who is on a medical aid. This was supposed to be just the beginning of a series of policies to regulate the medical aid industry, but 20 years later the list has never been updated and neither have the treatment protocols. To make matters worse, most medical aid companies fail to inform their members that their conditions should be covered as PMBs. The result is patients paying extortionate medical expenses out of pocket, often when they are already incapacitated by illness. And for the rest of us, rising premiums making medical aid care ever less affordable and less comprehensive.

You are an ordinary middle class South African with a full time job and two kids. Every month, when your salary comes in, and those debit orders go out, medical aid premiums are a large chunk of the monthly expenses you bear. It might be barely affordable but many people will continue to pay just in case - for that day when the dread diagnosis of cancer comes, or you are admitted to hospital. When that day comes, you'll be relying on your medical aid to cover you - and the legislation is on your side. By law, emergencies, 25 chronic conditions and a list of 270 other conditions are covered as Prescribed Minimum Benefits for anyone who is a medical aid scheme member. But will you really reap those benefits when the time comes? Thanks to inadequately enforced regulations and medical aids failing to inform their members of their rights, many South Africans are paying out of pocket...which can mean losing your job, your car and ending up in debt review for hundreds of thousands. A new Competition Commission inquiry backs up what many doctors and patients have been saying for years. Carte Blanche takes a dive into the world of medical care to find out what's going wrong.

title: Daveyton Turmoil
oneLiner: The community of Daveyton is under siege by Nyaope gangs. Fed up with the lack of policing in their township they took the law into their hands with dire consequences.
summary:
For some time now residents in Daveyton have been terrorized by thieves breaking into their homes. People are being killed in the streets by the gangs with little or no police intervention. In the past few weeks, violence escalated as the gangs went on a rampage. According Nonkululeko, a Daveyton resident, the gangs try and recruit young girls and boys and if they refuse they get necklaced. In the space of seven weeks 11 people have been killed. On the 15th of August things got out of control, following the murder of two teenage girls by the gangs. The community turned vigilante and went in search of gang members. They say that some of the gang members attend the local school, Unity Secondary school and it was there that they took justice into their own hands by necklacing alleged gang members in front of children and staff. These gruesome visuals have been shared on social media. Crime has always been an issue for the people of Daveyton, but with the emergence of gangs such as the “Freaks” and the “Avanzas” within the township the residents are afraid for their lives and those of their children and angry about a distinct lack of police protection. Finally, when they took matters into their own hands, the police reacted, patrolling the township trying to stop more bloodshed. This was only after the mob of residents necklaced the high school student suspected to be part of a gang. But the police themselves became perpetrators in the violence.

A lack of police response to violence perpetrated in the Daveyton community, in the east rand of Johannesburg, has prompted residents to take revenge against the gang members by using vigilante township justice, with tyres and matchsticks in defense of their own peace and safety. The feeling is that the police have failed them.

title: Lowveld Tourism Under Threat
oneLiner: Tourism in our iconic Mpumalanga Lowveld is under threat!
summary:
It is labelled as one of South Africa's most scenic areas. The Lowveld & Panorama Route of Mpumalanga showcases the natural awe inspiring areas of the district including God’s Window, Mac Mac Falls, Bourke’s Luck potholes, Kruger National Park and others. The area falls under the Ehlanzeni district municipality which encompasses four local municipalities -- Thaba Chweu, Bushbuckridge, City of Mbombela & Nkomazi. The entire area is affected by what started as locals protesting poor service delivery, and which has now escalated in to a more organised form of disruption with the aim of... no one knows for sure. Whilst National Government sees the area's tourism potential, the breakdown seems to be with local municipalities not coming to the party. But poor service delivery in the area has left local residents frustrated and they have now taken to daily protests, blockading the major scenic routes in the area, cutting off access to some of the tourist attractions. Although tourism is not the sole focus, many local tourism establishments that cater especially for international visitors are feeling the pressure as they have reported a decline in bookings (30 to 45%) over the past year. At least 2 international tourism operators are considering halting trips to the area for fear of safety, and because of the daily struggle to get tourists to and from Kruger National Park and airports, and other tourist destinations. Even roads to airports are affected. We speak to local accommodation owners and tourism operators about their daily frustrations and the disappointment of tourists when they are unable to visit the area's jewels. The roads affected seem to be the ones that lead to the major tourist destinations, eg entry to Kruger National Park, Burke's Luck, Graskop and even the Adventura Resort. Locals burn tyres, and barricade the roads with branches and rocks.

The issue has largely been kept out of the media but there are daily service delivery protests in the Ehlanzeni District Municipality area (basically the entire Lowveld region), threatening the livelihood of tourism in this area. Specifically, the Thaba Chweu Local Municipality has a bad reputation when it comes to service delivery (according to locals). So locals are barricading the scenic routes and access roads to major tourist attractions which means that tourism operators have to make last-minute changes to their itineraries and self-drive tourists are affected on a daily basis. Locals are protesting poor (or non-existent) service delivery. Outside Mbombela a community was hard hit by a hail storm and the repairs have not been done completely. Resident are angry and keep barricading the N4 and other major routes outside the city. Near Hazyview, communities are protesting lack of water and electricity. Some people were given RDP housing, but there has been no water or electricity connections and the community is fed-up. It's been 3 years now. So, hence the frustrations. Similarly Graskop communities are also desperate for water and sanitation services and they are barricading roads leading to the iconic God's Window. The whole area is plaqued by protests, but it is not one specific issue... The problem lies, it seems with the local and district municipalities and their total lack of service delivery. Schools are falling apart, hospitals are substandard, roads have massive potholes. Tourism is not the target per se, but it is one sector of business that is suffering greatly at the moment. Another opinion comes from the African National Chamber of Commerce & Industry Mpumalanga -- saying that politicians with ambitions have seen the opportunity and are instigating the protests. He says the protests are well organised and are as a result of the in-fighting between various factions within the ANC that want control over the province.

title: Hangberg on a knife's edge
oneLiner: When a fisher goes missing at sea during a police raid the locals of Hangberg take to the streets in protest. Carte Blanche investigate.
summary: It is cold winter’s morning in Hangberg, a fishing village on the outskirts of Hout Bay. From inside the church the last notes of “what a friend we have in Jesus” filters through the somber air. The Pastor prays for the return of a ‘missing son’ and lay hands on the family as they ask for a miracle to happen. It has been five days since Deurick van Blerk went missing at sea. In the icy winter waters of the Cape there is little hope now for a safe return. “Please bring back our son,” ask the father, Edward van Blerk. “We still have hope that we will see our son alive,” he says. 26-Year-old Deurick van Blerk went missing on Friday night when he was out at sea catching crayfish with two fellow fishers. On the same night SAPS Water wing was out in full swing on an anti-poaching operation. They came across the boat, confiscated the crayfish and arrested two of the three fishers. In a statement issued by SAPS they were not clear if Van Blerk fell overboard or jumped. People are now speculating that perhaps he was shot at by the police and fell into the icy Cape waters.
