title: Microchipped humans
oneLiner: What is the future of humans being microchipped to perform every day functions, normally done with external devices?
summary: The first microchip was implanted into a human in the UK in 1998. Since then there have been a few advances in the technology, but it has not become a mainstream practice. In South Africa there are two engineers who are working on ways to use implanted intelligent microchips in everyday life and to solve some of South Africa's issues with access to good health care. Daniel De Kock and Jarryd Becker have implanted microchips into their skin. These microchips are the size of grains of rice and have the potential to start cars using program codes, send signals of biographical information (barcodes) to computers and phones within close proximity and also posses the power to provide geographical location information of the host. It is expected that in the future, the chips will have medical uses such as monitoring blood sugar or sounding an alarm if a heart attack is imminent. South African Law enables tests for the implanted chips – which are not allowed the same way under US regulation. Professor Basie Von Solms is a professor at UJ and a specialists in cyber security, he can give us a broader perspective on how these intelligent microchips are being used internationally and what the security risks are if this becomes more common practice. That is the basic overview. It is insane though when you listen to them talk about using implants to go beyond correcting a medical fault in the human body to actually turning humans into wireless super humans. To make us able to pay for things, start our cars, gain security access and provide our medical history by swiping our hand or arm near the device.

title: AB de Villiers
oneLiner: We sit down for an insight into how AB de Villiers became one of South Africa's most loved sportsmen and best batsmen in the world
summary: AB DE VILLIERS AB de Villiers is one of the finest batsmen ever to play cricket, and yet his achievement extends beyond his outrageous armoury of drives, pulls, paddles, scoops and flicks. Whether he is delighting home crowds at the Wanderers or Newlands or setting new records in Bengaluru or Sydney, he plays the game in a whole-hearted manner that projects a positive image of his country around the world and also makes millions of South Africans feel good about themselves. This is AB’s story, in his own words … the story of the youngest of three talented, sports-mad brothers growing up in Warmbaths, of a boy who excelled at tennis, rugby and cricket, of a youngster who made his international debut at the age of 20 and was then selected in every single Test played by South Africa for the next 11 seasons, of a batsman who has started to redefine the art, being ranked among the world’s very best in Test, ODI and T20. Through all the pyrotechnics and consistency, AB has remained a true sportsman – quick to deflect praise, swift to praise opponents, eager to work hard, to embrace the team’s next challenge and to relish what he still regards as the huge privilege of representing his country. This is the story of a modern sporting phenomenon. The statistics tell barely half the story but, so far, AB DE VILLIERS has scored 14 000 runs in 98 Tests for South Africa, 8 000 runs in 190 one-day internationals and more than 40 000 runs in his professional career. He is mainly distinguished by the style in which he bats and his humble, determined captaincy of the South African national team in one-day international cricket.
caseStudies: ABE DE VILLIERS

title: Brucellosis: Ondersterpport Biological Services and the impact on animal health in SA
oneLiner: Despite getting a R500 million cash injection from Treasury the OBS is not manufacturing crucial vaccines necessary for food security in SA
summary: Brucellosis a highly contagious bacterial infection in cattle, goats, sheep, wild animals and humans is a nasty, debilitating illness that’s rapidly spreading through animal populations across South Africa. The most common way people contract it is by drinking unpasteurised milk, but farmers, vets and farm workers are most at risk and many rural vets and farm workers are infected. Brucellosis is extremely difficult to treat in humans and infected animals have to be culled. In humans, unless it’s diagnosed in the first few months it’s almost impossible to treat as it’s an inter-cellular bacteria. It very painful, leaving the victim with chronic fatigue, and severe depression as it attacks the amino acids in the body, wiping out dopamine and serotonin. The collapse of the State Veterinary services along with the decline of the production of vital medication by the Onderstepoort veterinary services is threatening food security in South Africa. The national herd is extremely unproductive, badly managed and under resourced.

title: Olifants: Cry Me A River
oneLiner: Carte Blanche goes to Burgersfort where the Olifants river is rotten - filled with diapers and dead animals. We travel the river's path and investigate the reasons it's so polluted.
summary:
We will chat to several experts along the river - Paul Oberholster from the CSIR who worked on the project of cleaning the river with the Olifants River Forum. They obtained a report that has never been published and they have given to Carte Blanche. They tried to fix the upper river and can explain why the lower parts are so polluted. We will be flying over the Kruger National Park and seeing how dry it is, but also to get visuals - this will be with the bataleurs. We will also speak to ecologist -and vetinarian Dr. David Huchzermeyer about the animals in the river - he is a fish expert and studied why the fish and crocodiles were being diagnozed with a rare disorder called Pansteatitis. He will explain how the river has had it's problems and with the drought it may get worse next year. We have obtained several reports from Dr. Koos Pretorius on the acid mine drainage - where he says 30% of the river's ecology has been killed off. We also have other reports from a professor at University of Limpopo to back up the fish are dying throughout the system.

Diapers, diapers everywhere. The community of Burgersfort are superstitious and are throwing away diapers into the nearby Olifants river, so much so, that Peter Mashile who was raised in the community has decided enough is enough. He has employed several people to clean the diapers and give them back to the community's ready to reuse. Farmers in the area have lost cattle who have drunk the water and we speak to the mothers and ask why they do this. We will also speak to Peter who has fought to keep the river clean. Award - are an NGO based in Hoedspruit they are studying the river and are finding a unique management system to help with the pollution. We will go with them and test the water in burgersfort, we will also interview their CEO about the project and the problems that the river is experiencing.

title: Karoo Uranium
oneLiner: Despite a flatlining world uranium price, Australian miner Peninsula, backed by Russian capital, angles to mine uranium in the Karoo, threatening precious water sources.
summary: Very nearly too late, experts and affected parties -- like the vulnerable farmers of the Karoo, heard that Peninsula Energy and its local partners have been planning to mine 750,000ha of the water-scarce, ecologically sensitive region. But by mid-year, Karoo-based Dr Stefan Cramer, science advisor to the Southern African Faith Communities' Environment Initiative (SAFCEI is taking government to court for its secretive handling of the new nuclear build programme) had rallied massive support of communities in the region to make their voices heard against the company's plans to use up and pollute major water sources in its quest for uranium profits. Now the company has pulled back on its original plan, reducing their application to only 70,000ha. What made them do this? Was the the rising tide of activism against their now slowing dawning plans? Was the the astute analysis of their ostensibly self-serving environmental impact assessments by provincial environmental departments and organised agriculture? Does the reduction in the territory make any difference to the amount of water that will be lost now and in the generations to come -- as uranium and its toxic decay products linger in the environment for geological ages to come.

title: Jozi Cats - Africa's first gay rugby club
oneLiner: Paragons or pariahs? Are South Africans ready to embrace homosexual role models in sport? Africa's first gay and inclusive ruby club, Jozi Cats, is setting the trend for change.
summary: Jozi Cats, Africa’s first gay and inclusive rugby club, in May this year launched a provocative recruitment campaign that made headlines across the world, turning typical homosexual slurs on their head like, "fairy, "pansy", "pillow biter" and "fudge packer". The campaign created a stir beyond our borders, breaking the silence and taboo around homosexuality in sport. They are unashamedly embracing their their gayness and love of rugby at the same time, as well as raising the question of why there should even be a need for such a club in this day and age? “The truth of the matter is that many of our players don’t feel like they can be openly gay and be a rugby player in South Africa,” says Kuni. “So we started Jozi Cats as a space where they could be both. The club is somewhere that players can play social and competitive rugby in a safe and non-judgmental environment. ”The poignant campaign also helps to smash perceptions that gay men fit a certain stereotype which has been formed by society, which is why it was so crucial to use players from the club in the poster campaign. Carte Blanche meets some of these brave young men and goes behind the scenes in what is not your typical day at the rugby, as we explore the underlying stereotype of the "macho" sportsman and we meet some of the men behind the posters.

title: CancerDojo
summary: This is a story of anger survivor who beat the odds, having recovered from life threatening cancer - and he puts it down to using creativity and humour. Conns Berths is one of SA’s top creative thinkers and has run many ad agencies. he was struck down with cancer but decided to fight it through creative thinking. When he was diagnosed with a severe and extremely rare form of brain cancer in 2006, Bertish immediately set in motion the biggest creative project of his life. He began the process of using his imagination to immerse himself in his bout with cancer. He went straight to the first things he always relied on – his pen, paper and playful, problem-solving attitude. He began toying with cancer, studying the ill people around him, creating visual representations of what he was going through and documenting his experiences through conceptual thinking and storytelling. He used his imagination to create a drawn series of pen-on-paper metaphors that helped him to visualise his tumour and treatments with intent. Bertish was able to imagine the effects that different treatments would have on the tumour cells. He was also able to concentrate energy where his body needed it most - augmenting the effects of his chemotherapy, radiation and multiple surgeries by linking his mind to his body in a playful targeted way. Now he is taking his story to the world and already he has even invited at attend overseas companions. he is building a fascinating app, called the Dogo app to encourage cancer sufferers and to provide them with the tools he used. To be interviewed: Him and a doctor who will talk on neural imaging which combines positivism and illness.

title: HPV/ Oral Cancer
summary: It's not in the South African media but surgeons here are increasingly operating on patients with throat cancer caused by the HPV virus and not smoking, alcohol or bad diet. International literature is suggesting that HPV will overtake smoking as a leading cause of oropharyngeal cancers. The reason it seems that oral sex is the cause and more men are prone to it because of their sexual practice of cunninglingus. In fact these increases are seen more in developed countries than undeveloped countries. A controversial aspect of this story is the following - whether a patient has throat cancer from HPV or not does not affect treatment which is either surgery or radiation. This is why national labs are not testing for the virus and so we have no idea the extent to which HPV throat cancers are prevalent in South Africa. However we will be honing in on a medical practice and a particular doctor who regularly performs surgery on patients with throat cancer caused by the HPV virus. This private practice unlike other private practices always request private labs to test for HPV. Those with HPV are informed because the prognosis is better than cancers non-HPV related. The program will address the need for safety precautions. We will cover the fact that school children a re being vaccinated and we will get a doctor to talk about the need for safer sex. He admits this is a pipe dream because many practice risky sex. He will advocate that all sexually active men and woman should be vaccinated which can delay the onset of HPV. In this program John Webb can hold up a "dam" which is a piece of cloth which needs to be placed over the vagina to effect safer cunninglingus. The point is that it is doubtful that people will go to this lengths but we need to put it out there. The take home message is that HPV related throat cancers are on the rise and there are even some reports that say that it could overtake cervical cancer in the years ahead in terms of deaths. That is scary.

title: Fossils discovered on N2
summary: A huge treasure trove of fossils, including of some species that have not been documented by scientists before, has been discovered during construction work on the N2 highway near Grahamstown. Dr Robert Gess a palaeontologist who does consulting for Sanral said the discovery was significant because "many species have not yet been documented by palaeontologists". The fossils are from the the Devonian era which lasted from about 416 million years ago to 354 million years ago, and is often referred to as the "Age of Fishes". The earth at that stage was made up of only two large continents. South Africa was part of one of those called Gondwana, nearly 360 million years ago. He said between 20 and 30 types of fossil land plants, waterweeds and seaweeds have been collected from the rocks retrieved from roadworks at Waterloo Farm, and are being described by scientists. Some of the remains from Waterloo Farm include fragments of scorpions which represent the earliest known remains of land living creatures from the ancient supercontinent of Gondwana. Sanral is now planning to turn the area into a stop and rest area for motorists. We plan to film Dr Gess on site and driving to the site. Perhaps speak to one of the construction workers and also SANRAL environmental manager Mpati Makoa who will talk about how they are going to turn this area into a stop and go tourist site to preserve the fossils. We can get access to the film that SANRAL made and the insert can be complimented hopefully by magnificent graphics showing the continents moving. I do think we can make this quite an exciting piece.

title: Selfiecide
oneLiner: BUT FIRST, let me take a selfie. The last words often said before a selfie goes wrong. Diagnosed as a disease and banned in India - what is selfiecide and how are we dealing with it in SA?
summary: Selfiecide An accidental death that has been caused whilst trying to take a dangerous Selfie pic. The term selfie was word of the year in the Oxford dictionary in 2013. "A photograph that one has taken of oneself, typically one taken with a smartphone or webcam and shared via social media." But the "selfie craze" has since grown and has since been classed as a mental disorder - by the American psychiatric Association in 2014. APA said there are three levels of the disorder: Borderline selfitis : taking photos of one’s self at least three times a day but not posting them on social media Acute selfitis: taking photos of one’s self at least three times a day and posting each of the photos on social media Chronic selfitis: Uncontrollable urge to take photos of one’s self round the clock and posting the photos on social media more than six times a day. Although these are international examples (see below) - we do have some local examples - and we are going to spend the morning with the labstore ladies - a group of young woman between 19-23 whose job it is to take selfies in the social media company -Lab store. The are self proclaimed addicts and talk about the dangerous behaviour extreme selfie taking leads to, but also about the culture of selfie taking; in which, young impressionable ladies are "allogroomed" to include selfies in their daily lives. Nadia Scheepers and Abigail Ferns will talk about the stresses of selfie culture and how sometimes they take 50 selfies just to get the perfect one to post on social media - they will talk about the self editing process. Our teens are serious about taking selfies, so serious that it has become, for some, more important than living - and if the selfie response is less than expected or there is negative backlash or a photo is trolled - suicide is often considered as a final resort. Nadia is called the "Selfie queen."

title: Waste kings
oneLiner: from picking through rubbish bins and scavenging on landfills, waste pickers are saving municipalities millions of rands every year.
summary: South Africa has between 60 000 to 90 000 waste pickers who work tirelessly on the streets, picking recyclable waste material from rubbish bins in suburbs and scavenging on landfills to find paper, cupboards, steel and plastic and in a recent surprise finding, these invisible workers, are saving our municipalities up to R750-million a year. According to a report by the Centre for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR),waste pickers divert recyclables away from the landfills at no, or little cost, by recovering around 80 to 90% of waste. It is estimated that each waste picker diverts up to 24 tons of packaging waste every year and they do this while pulling their heavy trolleys around 40 kilometres per day from the suburbs to the landfills and back again. But the waste and recycling sector is on the brink of change thanks to mandatory extended producer responsibility, which means producers (of end waste material) will now be responsible for the waste they generate, cutting informal waste pickers out, and without any real means to earn a living from these recyclables. The CSIR has done research to see if waste pickers can be incorporated into the formal economy, and Professor Linda Godfrey, who led the study, said: "The most surprising finding for me was when we started to attach financial values to the savings by municipalities as a result of informal waste pickers."

title: Pelindaba
oneLiner: After working on apartheid SA's secret atomic weapons programme, hundreds of workers who were injured at Pelindaba are pinning their last hope of getting compensated on the Public Protector.
summary: Decades after being employed by the apartheid government at Pelindaba, hundreds of workers have been struggling together for the last 16 years to get compensation for debilitating illnesses that were probably caused by exposure to radiation or harmful chemicals. Over the years, workers at Pelindaba's test plants had been exposed to chemically toxic and radio-active materials that would react with their skin and organs and now, 20 or 30 years later, cause them to become very ill. No process for assessing occupational injury and disease was put in place -- the workers had nowhere to go in the company, or in the rest of government, to get their medical records, get independent medical advice and ensure fair compensation for job-related injury. In most cases, workers who were injured on the job, were summarily retrenched or let go without due process. It is not known how many workers died on the job, but we have stories of workers who died due to chemical exposure, even before they reached hospitals, and their families were none the wiser. We also have stories of workers' families now coming to the fore with questions about whether their parents' ill health now could have been caused at Pelindaba all those years ago. Under pressure to build Apartheid's nuclear bombs, a culture of cutting corners and working without proper oversight and protective gear took root. Now the chickens are coming home to roost, but in the context of Eskom and the government's stated commitment to nuclear power expansion, the workers have been ignored, intimidated, sent from pillar to post and dumped. Their last hope is that Public Protector Thuli Madonsela will take them seriously before she leaves office in October.

title: White River Water Issues
oneLiner: White River relies on tourism and farming for export, so when the town's water supply was cut off, it was like cutting off its blood supply.
summary: WHITE RIVER WATER ISSUES The water issues in White River are huge, fueled by corruption, illegal connections and the lack of action by the Municipality of Mbombela to address these problems. The residents of this leavy town now want answers that they are not getting from the people in charge of the town's water. Piet Badenhorst, a concerned citizen of the town initiated a petition to get Carte Blanche to investigate the water issues that have plagued this town for far too long. At a meeting that was held on the 21st of April in White River to discuss the water issues, Carol Zulu, the General Manager - Water and Sanitation of the Mbombela Municipality, as reported in the White River Post newspaper, said the main problem was the illegal tapping of power from the transformers and the clamping of valves on the pipeline that supplied water to the town. The Mhluluzi illegal informal settlement seemed to be the culprit. Zulu explained that on paper the water supply to White River was enough but due to the tapping into the power supply was a problem that could not be solved overnight. The challenge that they have is to stop the leaks of the illegal clamping of the valves. The illegal tapping of electricity had on several occasions been taken care of and resolved but reappeared. This crime happened at night and therefore the Municipality could not prevent it and had no control over it. Zulu said that on previous occasions the residents of the settlement had become violent and protested. With bigger houses being built there, the need for more power will increase and more residents will tap electricity from the transformers resulting in worse problems. Zulu said a new reservoir would be the answer to the problem and law-enforcement officers should be deployed to arrest the perpetrators. According to Piet Badenhorst the water issues won’t go away unless the pump stations are moved to safer premises

oneLiner: Premature babies born before 25 weeks are called micro prems and have almost no chance of survival outside the womb. Find out how doctors are working to save these tiny babies.
summary: Premature babies born sub 25 weeks – are known as micro prems – and some neonatal units in South Africa have developed such advanced bio mimicry incubators – in other words an extra uterine womb as close to nature as possible – that these minute babies are given more than a fighting chance. Dr. Ricky Dipenaar is a neonatologist and he heads up units at Cape Towns Blouberg and N1 City Netcare hospitals where he specialises in the care of these tiny babies. All babies born before the 40-week gestation period are considered premature, but these sub 25-weekers are far more high risk because their organs and systems are not fully developed. Dr Dipenaar and his team create extra uterine incubators to help these babies survive. From using ziplock bags or velcro bags, an artificial womb is created for these tiny babies. Micro-prems are so small that they can fit in the palm of your hand and they have very translucent skin. Their arms and veins are too small for an intravenous line so their feeding line is connected to their umbilicus and that's how they get their nutrition. A humidifier is then used to correct the temperature in the artificial womb and that's where the babies spend the first few weeks until they're "full term" babies and ready to go home.

Nicola Terblanche/Jameson was driving home from a night at friends, her husband was in the passenger seat and her son - Scott,3, was in the back in a baby car seat. Out of know where a car hits her car. Her foot is broken, she's dazed. Her husband managers to unbuckle his seat belt and get to their son in the back. Unfortunately, Scott died on impact. They go to the hospital and there they find out that the other female driver - Sharborne Lance - and one of the two kids in her car died as well. It's then that Nicola found out that the accident was not caused by this women. In fact, her boyfriend had intentionally hit her and caused her car to his theirs. He fled the scene according to a witness - Mr. Werner du Toit (Mapogo Security). The man accused of this crime is called Elliston "Trompie" Fortuin - he has a murder rap sheet as long as my arms. He's been in and out of jail thrice - serving 18 months, 3 years, 3 years, and 15 years (of which he only served 8) and is currently out on parole from the 15 year sentence. Trompies was arrested at a chop shop trying to get his car fixed after the accident. He was denied bail, however, the charges were provisionally withdrawn (for further investigation) and will be re-instituted soon as the police have escalated the matter to the DPP's office (High Court) because "off the record" there are worries as to the state prosecutor's conduct. It's a year since the accident and what is taking so long for this to go to court? He's on parole, how can this dangerous man be roaming the streets?

title: Unpacking the CA report on the Huey accidents
summary: Last year a Working on Fire huey helicopter crashed whilst fighting fires. A week later, another one went down, also killing the pilot. Recently the CA released their findings on the cause for the first accident which is resulting in the deceased pilot's wife contemplating legal action. It found that working on fire maintenance was not up to scratch and that the pilot erred in not doing preflight checks and acting quickly when a light came on in the cockpit warning of gearbox failure. The CA report is being challenged by Working on Fire. We unpack the report using other experts such as a veteran helicopter pilot who has fought fires often himself. He will use his own huey helicopter as an example when chatting about the accidents and the report. For example the report says that the pilot should have noticed frayed cables but these are actually hidden underneath panels. Our case study Mr Jannie Smit will demonstrate this. He will also take us for a spin in his huey helicopter where some of the interviews will be done. This investigation will be set within a narrative about the huey helicopter and why they are so popular in South Africa. But they are controversial which we will touch upon. Our pilot will tell us that there is little doubt that in massive fires like the Cape has witnessed, it is little wonder that these huey helicopters experience extreme stress and that maintenance has to be a priority. The pilot continues to say that more fire fighting helicopter pilots will die because a lot of them lack the experience in firefighting. Right after the accident, the working on fire huey helicopters were grounded and all had to be checked, now maintenance is spread over several other companies, but the question remains: Working on Fire has massive contracts from thr govt. How is it possible that they only had 2 registered engineers whose job was to cover and inspect all 20 huey Helicopters? Was this cost saving?

title: Abandoned Babies
oneLiner: The growing crisis abandoned babies, a woman's drive to address this human tragedy
summary: How to tell the story of babies who are abandoned at birth. The Child Protection Activist The plight of abandoned babies in South Africa is an issue that the government does not want to deal and are pushing under the carpet…says Dee Blackie, child protection activist. It all started for Dee when she saw picture in a newspaper of a little girl who had been abandoned and died on the outskirts of Soweto. Dee knew she had to do something. Approaching the government she was told:  “don’t understand” the problem ..I went back to university to do my masters in Anthropology looking child abandonment and adoption in the context of African ancestral beliefs. ….the abandoned Sindisiwe, whose name means ‘saved’ was abandoned by her mother in a hospital toilet, she was found by a nurse who thought she was dead, until miraculously Sindisiwe coughed and took her first breath. The nurse rushed her to the neonatal unit in the hospital and that is where she stayed for several months. Sindisiwe was eventually raised by her grandparents until they died when Sindisiwe was 12, and later by aunts. Sindisiwe never knew who her mother was until years later when she was an adult but on confronting her was “ I wish you had died then” Sindi, now in her 30’s, works as a charismatic minister ministering to people around the country. She is in the process of being ordained and setting up her own ministry. In Dee’s word’s “In her quiet unassuming way is an inspiration to many.” ….the saviours Nicole and Johan Olivier are a family of five, their youngest Noah was abandoned at birth, he was left under a tree in a field outside a township wrapped in a plastic bag inside his mother jacket. Nicole Olivier who had just miscarried twins got a call about Noah, for her it was meant to be. Love at first sight and three weeks later she adopted him, He is now the happiest and bubbliest 4 year old and the Olivier’s could not imagine their family without him.

title: Home Repo
oneLiner: In South Africa you are 20 times more likely to have your house repossessed than anywhere else in the world.
summary: In South Africa more than 150 000 homes were repossessed by banks over the last 20 years. It is 10x to 20x higher than anywhere else in the world. The reason for this is unscrupulous behaviour by banks and also inadequate consumer protection. Elsewhere in the world this does not happen because banks are forced to try and help the consumers before repossessing. In South Africa they are allowed to act immediately upon non-payment and they do so in a big way. Properties are then sold at a fraction of the market price and former home owners are forced to keep on paying. It has ruined tens of thousands of lives and families.

title: Meanwhile, somewhere in rural northern Malawi...
oneLiner: About 30% of Malawi's population are living in South Africa - but what effect is this having on the villages where they came from?
summary: For more than a century migrant workers from Malawi have been streaming to South Africa, with devastating effects on the villages where they came from. Typically the men come to look for work. Those who go home over holiday periods take some money back, but they've also taken HIV/Aids to these vulnerable communities, where health care is virtually non-existent. Even worse -most of the men lose contact with their families back home, prompting the women to also come to SA, to try and find their husbands.But, because these women don't have official papers or money for the bus fare, many of them unknowingly fall prey to ruthless human traffickers. If they survive the journey, with illegal border crossings (walking through Kruger etc) they end up in Diepsloot as illegal immigrants, and the people who brought them claim ownership of these women, as they can't pay the money for the bus trip. These women are then forced into prostitution, or simply sold off to willing men for a few hundred rand.

title: Phillipi Horticultural Area under seige
oneLiner: Food or housing- the centuries old bread basket of Cape Town is under threat by developers
summary: The Philippi Horticultural area – PHA- is a unique farming community of over 3000 hectares producing 200 000 tonnes of vegetables and flowers per year situated in the heart of the Cape Flats, a mere 20km from the centre of Cape Town. Most Capetonians have no idea how abundant and productive it is as they rush down the main roads that surround the area. They also have no idea that many of the vegetables they buy in the supermarkets have come from just a few kilometres down the road. Established by German immigrant farmers in the 1800s, it has been the bread basket of the city for nearly two centuries. It is situated on top of one of the largest underground aquifers in the world and so has an abundance of water. The temperature is ideal for vegetables, as the cool sea breezes keep soaring summer temperatures at bay. As the drought hits food production around South Africa, Philippi has been left unscathed. People are travelling in from further and further out of town to come and buy vegetables from the PHA. But the area is under threat from growing pressure from the City to provide houses. Two major sections of the Southern part of the PHA, which is the most productive vegetable growing area, have been rezoned. The future of food security in Cape Town is severely threatened

title: Handicapped Scuba Divers
oneLiner: Scuba diving, exchanging a wheelchair for a wetsuit, the Handicapped Scuba Association trains the severely disabled to enjoy the freedom of an underwater environment.
summary: A dive-a-thon, organised by the Handicapped Scuba Association, focuses the attention on a very special group of free spirits, confined in severely disabled bodies. Melissa Leonard has been confined to a wheelcahir since the age of six. For years she had a dream of being able to scuba dive but she had no idea where or how to go about it. Five years ago she was introduced to an instructor who specialises in teaching handicapped scuba divers. This turned out to be a life changing event for Melissa, learning to be safe in the potentially hazardous underwater environment took a lot of hard work and many hours in the pool. Divers have to be able to retrieve a regulator and clear a mask, amongst other skills. These actions require free movement of the hands and arms, even a simple movement like holding one's nose to equalize pressure in the ears, is impossible for some disabled divers. Scuba divers always dive in buddy pairs. Handicapped scuba divers require specially trained dive buddies to look after them throughout the dive, keeping them upright and constantly communicating with them. Braam Le Roux is a PADI diving instructor that specialises in training handicapped divers. We will look at his motivation for doing this very demanding type of training. Melisssa has found a whole new circle of friends through her diving activities and we will meet some of them and get to know their stories, Francois is a blind diver, he lost his sight 6 years ago in an accident, Cherise became a quadroplegic after a motor vehicle accident in 2014, at the age of 22, her scuba experience forms part of her re-hab. Vic Hugo suffered brain damage and use of his right hand side, he's the "official videographer" and a live wire in the handicapped scuba diving community, we will get to know him better. We will meet the dive buddies and instructors and film them under water with our characters.

title: Diabulimia nearly killed me
summary: Diabulimia is an eating disorder where Type 1 diabetes patients deliberately give themselves less insulin in order to lose weight Kyla was diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes when she was 16. At the time she already suffered from Bulimia and anorexia. She was as thin as could be and worked hard at keeping it that way. After being diagnosed with type 1 diabetes she started taking her prescribed dose of insulin and she started to put on weight. She soon figured out that If she withheld the insulin, her weight would come down. So her life spiralled into a very abusive relationship between her body and her mind. The side effects of withholding her insulin put her in hospital more times than she can count, she lost the vision in her right eye, had two toes amputated, but still she refused to take the insulin. She was diagnosed with Diabulimia, but refused to get help. Until this eating disorder threatened her ability to walk. She landed up in hospital and the doctors feared for days that Kyla’s foot would have to amputated. After she walked out of the hospital that week she agreed to being admitted for the treatment of her Diabulimia. Today Kyla is still battling and has to go to meetings every week to keep herself healthy. She has lost her job and her long term partner. From 16 – 32 years old she destroyed everything around her, because she was addicted to being thin.

title: Human Trafficking: For Sale
oneLiner: We take to the streets of Brooklyn where young girls walk the beat. Forced to sell their bodies, modern day slaves to be sold over and over again.
summary: It is Tuesday night close to 9h00 in Brooklyn. Slowly the streets take on a life of it's own. From dark alleyways and side streets, figures emerge in Koeberg road, the main artery that connects the veins of the northern suburb of Cape Town. Known as the hot spot that lures the seedier side of life, here you will find the action: illegals, pimps, prostitutes, drug lords, addicts and girls from all ages waiting to be picked up. Tonight is no different. We scout the streets with the Vice Squad, Cape Town's special Anti Trafficking Unit, on one of their regular raids. They plan to get more inside information from the girls walking the beat, their whereabouts and why they are here. We slow down the mini van and stop next to one of the girls standing alone, perhaps 17 or even younger, wearing heels and a short skirt. Officer Jacobs heading the 6-member Vice Squad team asks her name: "Lisa", she says in a soft voice. She is reluctant to answer any other questions beside her age being 23. "You know prostitution is illegal," says Jacobs in a warning tone to Lisa who is clearly lying about her name and age. Her slow speech and movements is an indication of being high on some form of drug. After a while Lisa admits to selling sex. The female officer in the unit speaks to her in a kind voice to try and coax more information from her that could lead us to her trafficker or pimp. We found out Lisa was recruited by a woman she became acquainted with back at her hometown in the Eastern Cape. The recruiter promised Lisa 'work' in Cape Town and offered her a lift and a place to stay. From here the story is almost identical to hundred's of women across South Africa who fall victim. They are mostly from small towns, poor family and not much hope for a better life or further education.

title: Nuclear Fallout
oneLiner: Hope for millions of people living in radioactive waste on the Witwatersrand gold fields - science steps in to bring their health plight to light
summary: Hair tells a story, just like the rings on a tree or the circles on a turtle’s shell. Hair keeps everything that is put into the body – medication, drugs…and in a new study commissioned by the International Agency for Research on Cancer, an agency of the World Health Organisation, the hope is that for the first time hair will confirm the story, backed by science, that anecdotes of mental retardation, cancer and kidney disease have hinted at – namely that the uraniferous mine residue in the Witwatersrand Gold Fields can kill. And that urgent intervention is needed to save lives. In eight mining areas of the West Rand, the WHO has, after decades of tireless campaigning and activism, contracted the Federation for a Sustainable Environment to conduct a ground-breaking study to determine the effects of exposure to radio-active uranium-rich mine waste in the area. The Witwatersrand has 20 times more uranium dumps than the United States and Canada combined. More than 600 abandoned mines surround Joburg, with much of their waste now piled up high next to an estimated 1,6-million people – most of whom are poor and black and up to now powerless to take the fight in any direction because of a lack of solid science and an abundance of denial both form organized mining and the state. Mariette Liefferink from the FSE will now collect hair samples form cooperating hair salons near the waste dumps and send it off to three laboratories in three different countries, together with hair samples from salons further away from dumps – like in Alexandra, Randburg, Laudium and Lenasia. The FSE is conducting this research under supervision of the Northern West University.

title: Meanwhile, back at the ranch...
oneLiner: The death bell may be tolling for the captive bred lion industry, but what will happen to the thousands of lions in captivity?
summary: The producers of Blood lions supplied us with extra footage of a lion hunt which took place in the kalahari on the botswana border. They also gave us an interview with the cameraman who filmed the hunt where he claims that especially three laws were broken on the hunt - 1) the lions were released only one day before the hunt started 2) the lions were drugged and 3) there was no nature conservation official present at the hunt We will check his claims and then take the footage to nature conservation, the lion breeders association and phasa - ask them to watch the footage with the presenter and give us their comments on what they see. The cameraman also reported the hunt to the green scorpions, and therefore we will also take it to them and ask why nothing has been done. Since the Cook report government has been trying to root out canned hunting, but got themselves tied up in knots with technicalities, distinguishing between canned and captive bred. But now, overseas legislation seems to be achieving what we couldnt do ourselves Australia and France banned the import of lion trophies from SA. And then in Jan this year, the US banned the import of all lion trophies from Africa, unless you can prove that the specific hunt had a real benefit for the conservation of wild lions. 85% of captive bred lion hunters come from the US, and this may very well mean the end of the industry. At hte same time PHASA, our own professional hunters body, also turned their back on the captive bred industry - stating that they will expell any of their members who take part in such hunt. So what will happen to the 6 - 8 000 lions currently on lion breeding farms? Will the breeders further develop the trade in lion bones with China, or will they be able to prove to the IUCN that captive bred lions do hold a conservation value?

title: PrEP in SA
oneLiner: South Africa has become the second country in the world to allow widespread access to groundbreaking HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis medication
summary: The Medicines Control Council of South Africa has have allowed a new, extremely easy to use and powerful weapon to stop HIV-negative South Africans from ever contracting the virus. The MCC has officially registered the use of a combination pill of two anti-retroviral drugs as a form of pre-exposure prophylaxis (or “PrEP”) medication; a pill taken once a day that massively reduces the chances of contracting the HIV. With South Africa’s high HIV burden, the deployment of this new intervention is profound. As of today, any general medical practitioner can prescribe PrEP. South Africans with private medical aid can motivate for PrEP to be covered by their medical plan. This vital new development in the fight against Aids it is now more crucial than ever that remaining barriers to accessing PrEP are removed. Fundamentally this means educating South Africans that PrEP exists and may help them personally and making sure that PrEP can be feasibly delivered in public healthcare settings. South Africa’s Anova Health Institute, in collaboration with the Desmond Tutu HIV Foundation, is currently implementing the largest state sector housed demonstration project for the use of PrEP. This project, taking place in Cape Town and Johannesburg, will gain the vital experience necessary to enable the department of health to take PrEP to scale. The rollout of PrEP on a national level could be viewed as the single biggest push towards combating HIV infection in Southern Africa. The drug however is not without it's detractors however with some calling it a "party drug" and a permission slip for rampant sexual behaviour.

title: El Nino
summary: El Niño 2015/16 is said to be the most extreme ever experienced in recorded history because it coincides with the highest temperatures ever recorded on earth. El Niño is a natural weather phenomenon occurring anything between two and seven years, which can last up to two years at a time. It’s a massive heat system that builds up in the ocean and is an oscillation between an El Niño and a La Niña. Scientists are divided as to what actually triggers the build-up. El Niño – literally ‘the Christ child’ as it usually hits around Christmas – is caused when the Pacific Ocean warms up over a prolonged period of time, and this leads to a reduction in the easterly trade winds, which in turn reduces the upwelling of cold nutrient-rich deep water. This has a direct impact on southern African weather systems, reducing the number of high pressure systems moving across the south of the continent, which in turn leads to far fewer rain storms in the summer rainfall areas. La Niña – literally the ‘girl child’ – often follows, and the results can be equally catastrophic for southern Africa. La Niña is the opposite of El Niño, and is caused by a drop in the Pacific Ocean temperatures of between 3 to 5°C. It causes far heavier than normal rainfall in the southern African summer rainfall season, which is normally not catastrophic, but following on a severe drought when there is little or no ground cover, this can lead to massive soil erosion, unchecked flooding, and loss of life and livestock. Such a massive reorganisation of atmospheric convection, which we define as an extreme El Niño, has severely disrupted global weather patterns, affecting ecosystems, agriculture, tropical cyclones, drought, bushfires, floods and other extreme weather events worldwide. . El Niño is a global weather system bringing extreme rain to some parts and extreme drought to others. For example Southern Africa is crippled by drought but parts of East Africa are drowning in torrential rains.

title: Infrastructure & the drought
oneLiner: Gripped by drought, it stands to reason that South Africa must treat every drop of water as sacred -- but we expose how water is wasted and lost due to dilapidated infrastructure
summary: In KwaZulu-Natal where the drought is pinching especially hard, more than half of water is lost due to burst pipes and leakages, thefts or other unauthorised use. In Gauteng, we are dangerously close to over-subscribing our available water...and yet we lose around a third through broken infrastructure and leaks. South Africa is the 30th driest country in the world, and yet we have invested little in expertise and maintenance -- rather settling for crony appointments in municipalities unable to fix the problems. According to the 2030 Water Resources Group, SA will face a shortfall of 17% between supply and demand by that year. In his 2010 State of the Nation address, President Jacob Zuma committed to halving leaks by 2014. Water leaks are also targeted by the national planning commission, which said fixing them is one of the cheapest and quickest ways of ensuring a water crunch does not happen. But losses have steadily increased -- the main reasons given by politicians are a lack of skilled staff, ageing infrastructure, a lack of information, and tariffs not reflecting the full costs of delivering water. The situation is the same across the country. A report by the Water Research Commission two years ago found that on average a third -- roughly 37% of water was lost in municipalities. This was either from leaks, or from people not paying for their water – both are included in "non-revenue water". So how has the situation changed in the last two years?

title: #Fees must Fall
summary: Across the country University Students are protesting the 10% increase in University Tuition fees. Wits University students were the first to come out preventing staff and students from attending lectures and eventually preventing staff from leaving the campus. On Monday UCT students joined the call of “Fees must fall” picking up on the slogan Rhodes must fall the student protest that brought Universities to a standstill earlier this year when students called for the transformation of Universities. On Monday Rhodes University, and Stellenbosch joined WITS and UCT. By the end of Tuesday campuses across the country had come out including Tuks, and CUPT. Today Universities across the country have come to a standstill. Students have been protesting the increase of fees for several years now but this is the first time they have all come out at the same time across the country. State and Private funding of Universities has been decreasing over the years and poor Students and their parents are taking the brunt of the financial stress. Many students are not poor enough to get state subsidies and their parents take out loans and bursaries to pay for their fees but there is little left for living cost, transport and food making the student’s lives extremely stressful. Students are graduating with massive loans to repay. Others who have qualified and got a degree don’t get their certificate because the university withholds the awarding of a degree until fees are paid up. This insert will focus on these students and their stories with the backdrop of the last weeks drama of students and University administrations coming head to head.

title: Limpopo Parks
oneLiner: Limpopo's provincial parks are struggling. Is it a lack of money, or could it be corruption?
summary: Blouberg Nature Reserve in Limpopo province is struggling to make ends meet like most provincial reserves. The proposed budget shows an expenditure of R7000 per month for this reserve for the next year. This is less than 10% of the minimum needed to manage the reserve. An organisation called The Friends of Blouberg have been helping to keep the reserve going for the past few years. However, the reserve is also under land claims, which hasn't been settled yet. For the past three years the limpopo government have allowed the land claimants to do hunting of 10 - 15 buffalo on this reserve annually to make some money. This is problematic because it is not a hunting reserve and you now have a situation where hunters and tourists are driving around the same park. When questioned about this, Limpopo government said the hunting allowance was part of the co-management agrement between the provincial government and the land claimants. However, a copy of this agreement obtained by the Friends of Blouberg shows that there is no mention of hunting at all. To make matters worse the hunting comes down to a huge financial loss for the province the reserve and the people of South Africa who ultimately own the buffalo.

title: Fish Hoek Crime: Cape Town’s CCTV ring of steel
summary: It is indeed the wild west. South africa has seen an increase in crime, up from last year. That includes Cape Town. But property crime has not increased in the mother city, and that's because, according to the City of Cape Town, of the introduction of communities buying their own special automatic number plate recognition cameras – which are then linked to the City's control room. Already Cape Town has 650 CCTV cameras. Neighborhoods have installed an extra 400 hundred and that number is increasing. The City pays for the electricity of these cameras and allows them on their light poles. The system is based on the UK system. London has only 15 000 CCTV cameras but the police have access to 2 million other private cameras. We highlight Fisheok which did not have one murder last year. We look at their model of how they have managed to get it right. One reason is that there is an enthusiastic band of people who volunteer for neighbourhood watch – and they use technology like laptops to keep abreast of movements of vehicles,tracked by these new cameras they have. They have close working associations with the local security company and the police. The main case study then will be Fishoek and we expand on the success of automatic number plate recognition which is spreading throughout the city.

title: Kimberley Psych Hospital
oneLiner: 12 years, a billion rand, many health MECs and contractors invested...and the largest psychiatric hospital in the Sourthen hemisphere remains at least another billion rands away from completion.
summary: Originally budgeted at R290-million, a massive state psychiatric hospital – the largest in the southern hemisphere – has stumbled from one construction crisis to another while mental patients in dire need of care rot in prison or face the stigma and threat of living in communities who don't understand them and have little compassion for their condition. The grandiose project outside Kimberley, meant to serve the entire northern region of the Cape and Free State, on which almost a billion rand has already been spent, ground to a halt in 2009 when contractual disputes erupted between the developers and the Northern Cape’s health and public works departments. In 2012 new congtractors were appointed, but progress remains halting as the new contractors INYATSI CONSTRUCTION went bankrupt and were bought out by multi-national construction firm MOTA-ENGIL. The real victims are the state patients who have been kept in prison for years – without having been found guilty of any crime – because the health department has nowhere else to place them. The department has been warned that it could face substantial legal claims from patients who have been deprived of care and freedom, some for as long as 15 years.

The plan is to take 130 buffalo, 50 white rhino, 50 sable and 32 nyala from the parks. That effectively means there will be no nyala left as last years census shows a mere 27 in the parks. Similarly when it comes to the buffalo there may be 1300 but 1000 of those are in Madikwe where they suffer from TB and another 50 in Mafikeng where they suffer from Bucellosis. So take 130 and you leave a population of only a 100 odd disease free buffalo, effrectively 50 breeding animals. And yet the project claims to be taking excess animals?

title: Antibiotic time bomb
oneLiner: Antibiotic resistance has been described as one of the biggest global threats - even more deadly than the threat of terrorism.
summary: Already 700 000 people die globally due to antibiotic resistance. In 10 or 20 years time, if nothing is done, we'll see people dying from simple infections. In South Africa the devastating effects are already being felt....there's been an increase in superbugs and antibiotic resistance. Helene van der Merwe was one of the first people to be impacted. She lost her 35 year old son when he contracted a superbug in hospital, antibiotics failed and sadly he passed away. Ian Samson was luckier, he also contracted a hospital infection and was on an IV drip for a week and then several courses of antibiotics before the infection finally cleared up. He says it was frightening, Antimicrobial resistance is a global threat. It happens when organisms are able to survive medicines aimed to destroy them. Bacteria can become resistant to antibiotics, viruses to antivirals and parasites to drugs like antimalarials. The World Health Organization says 150,000 deaths a year are caused by multi-drug resistant tuberculosis. If we don't take action, then we may all be back in an almost 19th Century environment where infections kill us as a result of routine operations. We won't be able to do a lot of our cancer treatments or organ transplants. Pharmaceutical companies need to be encouraged to develop new drugs, because the manufacture of antibiotics was not viewed as profitable. We haven't had a new class of antibiotics since the late 80s and there are very few antibiotics in the pipeline of the big pharmaceutical companies that develop and make drugs. We haven't as a society globally incentivised making antibiotics. It's quite simple - if they make something to treat high blood pressure or diabetes and it works, we will use it on our patients every day. Whereas antibiotics will only be used for a week or two when they're needed, and then they have a limited life span because of resistance developing anyway.

When Dube’s company, Vukani Aviation, was awarded the contract to lead the National Skills Fund's "New Growth Path" project to train 59 new pilots from disadvantaged backgrounds, it was a surprise. At that point he didn’t have an aviation school and had to buy one. In addition to the NSF allocation of R66 million, Dube also received R12 million from the Transport Education and Training Authority (Teta) to train another 12 pilots. There are allegations that this project, which charges R1.2 million per pilot (far more than other aviation schools charge) is nothing more than a get rich scheme for Dube. The first thing he did when awarded the project was buy himself a helicopter and a Porsche, which he hides in the Kruger Park Airfield when there are Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) checks, according to his students. The CAA has confirmed a probe into SAFTA (South African Flight Training Academy). The probe follows several complaints about management of the flight academy in Heidelberg, Gauteng, as well as questions about the "lucrative" R1.2-million-per-pilot programme. CAA spokesperson Sandy Motale said an audit of Dube's school last week had found operations to be "unacceptable". Despite the massive cash injection, only a third of the cadets have obtained their commercial pilot's licence almost two years after the first cadet intake. In addition not a single cadet has been employed at either of the two national carriers, South African Airways and SA Express - a key programme objective.

title: Blue-Green Algae: Troubled Waters
oneLiner: A looming water crisis is going to make Eskom and Acid mine drainage pale by comparison.
summary: The issue of Blue Greens has not received public attention as it should. These organisms are primitive, being neither plant nor animal but both. They are amongst the first living organisms that evolved on Earth, originally into a hostile environment where there was no oxygen and severe radiation from the sun because of the absence of an atmosphere. They are extremely resilient and are an indicator of severely distressed aquatic ecosystems. They produced our first oxygen and also evolved a number of complex molecules to protect themselves including sun block. They also produce a toxin known as microcystin, which they eject when in distress. Now here’s the issue – we have the highest known levels of contamination in the world. The Americans get concerned at 20 microgrammes per litre, but we have 10,000 spiking at 18,000 and nobody is concerned. We now know that about 2/3 o our national resource is contaminated from the attached paper. We also know that the toxin is released when the organism gets stressed. We know that blue-greens are found in large dams like Vaal and Midmar. We also know that the current bulk water treatment processes do not eliminate microcystin toxin once released. The only known treatment is with activated carbon and at present this is only available as an end-of-pipe solution, not yet as a bulk treatment solution.

title: North West Zama Wars
oneLiner: We bring you an exclusive look inside the Zama wars happening in the North West province, where hundreds of armed zamas enter mines at night and the police are powerless to stop it.
summary: The Klerksdorp/Stilfontein mining area is literally under attack by illegal miners. Security personnel are shot at on a weekly basis, Zamas scale the headgear of mine shafts from where they snipe at either security staff or rival zamas, and in an incident this week police in armored cars were told to withdraw from a mine at 3 in the morning because the situation was too dangerous. There is literally a fatal shooting in the area every other week. The zama syndicates operating in these areas are not only after illegally mined gold - they are also some of the main players in the copper theft arena. We have footage and video available of how zamas attack an Eskom substation at night, set it on fire and destroy all the equipment within. This means that they can come back the following night and strip the substation of any valuable metals - mostly copper cables etc. The mines are powerless to prevent the theft even though they know when and where it's going to happen because the zamas arrive in large armed groups. Police are usually asked to be at the scene but either fail to arrive or do not have the capacity to deal with the attacks themselves.

title: Graskoue Trappers
summary: Riel dancing is one of the oldest forms of dancing - thought to have evolved from the Koi, Nama and San who used to dance in sand in a circle around a fire. Farm workers in area have adapted it and it involves very intricate and fast dance steps. “Dans laat die stof so staan” seems like it may have found it’s origin here. But today there is a renewed interest in the cultural heritage of the decedents of the Khoi and San and the art form is alive and well again. Floris Smith who works as a chef in the Wupperthal area in the Cederberg area had a background in classical dancing and found this art form interesting.He started coaching a local group called the "Graskoue Trappers” and within a short time they won the ATKV Junior Riel Dance Champions. They were then invited to compete in the World Championships of Performing Arts in California this year. They have just arrived back in SA and a slew of medals including gold in the ethnic folk dance category. There is also a new form of dance genre that they have developed, which is a combination of tap and Riel and they also achieved gold in this category at the World Championships. We will speak to one of the tap dancers Zarion, who says he learnt tap from his grandmother who passed it onto his mother. Above the BUshman's kloof Lodge is San rock art and they depict dancers in a circle, we will film there and also go a bit into the history of the San. Rags to riches story, great visuals, lovely texture.

title: FPB Draft Online Regulation Bill
oneLiner: A new set of regulations threatens the very essence of our internet freedom
summary: A proposed policy to regulate online content in South Africa is poised to return the country to a worrisome state of severely curtailed free expression. The Draft Online Regulation Policy proposed by the Film and Publication Board (FPB) of South Africa is far-reaching and absolute in its censorship, potentially setting South Africa back by decades on issues of free expression, as well as putting the country on par with some of the world’s worst offenders—like Iran and China—in terms of restrictive legal environments for online speech. The Draft Online Regulation Policy, introduced by the FPB to regulate commercial content like films and games published online, is a purported attempt to protect children from offensive and illegal content, including child pornography, hate speech, racism, and extreme violence. But the online content covered by this policy would extend beyond that produced by commercial film and game publishers to include content created by individuals who publish game code, post YouTube videos, and ostensibly even those who post content on social media.

title: Oudtshoorn
oneLiner: Two years after losing their seats on the Oudtshoorn town council, members of the now minority ANC/NPP coalition flatly refuse to vacate their posts - the town hovers on the brink of bankruptcy
summary: Oudtshoorn is on a knife edge with politicians on all sides pleading for national governement and senior ANC intervention. We expect motion of no-confidence this coming week in municipal manager Ronnie Lottering. Speaker John Sotffels surprisingly resigned last week. We investigate allegations that Mayor Gordon April, Ronnie Lottering and publicity consultant Drewan Baird have been manipulating the system, holding on to power for personal gain - running the council like their personal fiefdom. The council stopped working two years ago after the ANC-coalition refused to hand over power to the DA-COPE coalition. Municipal budgets are not being passed - resulting in the non-payment of services - for instance, in less than a month, the town is due to be disconnected form the electicity grid by ESKOM to whom it owes around R25-million. The local river, a water source for the region, is being polluted by raw sewage, as service provision grinds to a halt. Money has been misallocated from the budget of the Cango Caves - an important regional, if not national, tourist attraction and significant income earner. The council has refused to hold meetings; suspended councillors for no reason; allegedly used public money in litigation as a delaying tactic; have allegedly offered inducements to other councillors in exchange for votes; and have ignored court orders. Protests flared in March when municipal workers heard the municipality had allegedly stolen their pension and medical aid contributions. It reached fever pitch this week when fisticuffs broke out in the council chamber after town councillors failed to approve the municipality’s budget for the third time in two months. The public gallery got involved in barricading councillors for two hours after the DA voted against the budget and the ANC abstained. Both the ANC and the DA-led provincial government put out statements pleading with Cooperative Governance Minister Pravin Gordhan to intervene.

title: Revenge Porn
oneLiner: Before you take that nude selfie to send to your partner or film yourself having sex.. think very carefully .. Your most private moment could end being used as revenge porn and posted online.
summary: The internet defies the law that what goes up must come down.. And many women are learning (the very hard way) that once explicit media of your most private moments goes up, it may never come down. Revenge porn is the unauthorized sharing of sexualized images, this happens most commonly across digital platforms. It is also largely categorized as digital sexual assault. It has become one of the most popular ways that disgruntled exes are taking out their anger on their former partners - by leaking their most private photos or videos online - naming and shaming the victims and sometimes even tagging the name of the company they work for and to their profiles on Facebook and Linked In etc. 95% of the victims are women. As with offline violence against women, the bulk of the abuse is at the hands not of strangers, but of people known to the women targeted. In the case of both of our case studies, their offenders were their former partners. There are 2000 sites dedicated to revenge porn. From myex.com (where men can post pics of their exes) to shesahomewrecker.com (where women name and shame their partners mistresses and it's run by a woman). The online world is being used as a weapon and the victims incur huge social, financial, psychological, emotional and professional costs. There are incidents of victims losing their jobs, receiving rape threats, having to move and even having to change their name. Revenge porn cases happen all around the world, to people across all ages and the topic has started to make international mainstream news and every day conversations. Putting pressure on judiciaries and social network platforms to change laws and regulations.

title: Facebook - Getting a 'like' or having a 'life'?
oneLiner: Getting a 'like' or having a 'life' - we delve behind the screen into the world of Facebook and expose a web of deceit.
summary: Facebook is one of the largest online social media platforms in the world, with over 1'.3 billion users worldwide. It's purpose is to make it easy for you to connect and share with your family and friends online. But for many subscribers it serves as an escape, providing a platforms where you can reconstruct your identity and be whoever or wherever you want to be.. Chances are, your Facebook persona will get more likes than the real life version of you and that kind of affirmation can be addictive. In this story we look into the different forms of lies that you may encounter on Facebook: IN 2014 Zilla van den Born, a Dutch student, pretended to be on holiday in Bali for 5 weeks - she created her entire trip on Facebook and had all her friends and family believe that she was on holiday, when she actually never left her apartment. We conduct a social experiment and expose how easy it is to fake a Facebook profile and connect with total strangers who are none the wiser.. Our profile is totally innocuous, but others are far more dangerous with greater consequences.. A catfish is someone who pretends to be someone they're not using Facebook or other social media to create false identities, particularly to pursue deceptive online romances or demand money.. Carina is a case study who fell victim to this.. We speak to her. (TBC) We should also speak to Facebook to understand how you can protect yourself from deception..

title: Concentrated Solar Power
summary: South Africa has 33 Renewable Energy power plants commissioned and by the end of next year there will be enough plants online to generate the same amount of power as Koeberg. By 2030 they will generate 17 800 MW of power. Globally there is a move towards renewable energy, the G7 announced this week that they intend to stop using all fossil fuels by the end of the century. title: Beware the copier
oneLiner: Have you copied any sensitive documents lately? There's every possibility that those documents still exist on the hard drive inside the copier you used.
summary: Have you copied any sensitive documents lately? There's every possibility that those documents still exist on the hard drive inside the copier you used. Remember when copiers were simple—just paper in, copies out? Once they began scanning and faxing, copiers evolved not just in capability, but as a serious security risk. Buried in your copier is a hard drive used to create an image of the original page that is then sent to a folder, attached to an e-mail, or sent by fax. Over 20,000 images can stay on the drive long after you have walked away. If the drive is not removed from the copier when your lease is up or if you replace it, or if a repair includes the replacement of the drive, your old drive can become an expensive data breach. It is relatively simple to retrieve the information stored on hard drives in copiers – and sensitive information about companies, individuals and government departments is there for the taking.

title: Canned Lion

summary: A tragic incident where an American tourist was mauled to death at Gautengs top tourist destination, the Lion Park has raised some serious concerns. The park which prides itself on close encounters with adult lion and cubs has long been an accident waiting to happen says experts in lion behaviour. You simply can't habituate young cubs to people and then allow people into their enclosures where they are bored and unafraid. It will at some point end badly. Another disturbing reality is - what could you do with an endless stream of cubs to keep visitors happy? And what do you do once they are too big and too dangerous to cuddle. Wildlife groups say that they end up dead - as trophies for canned lion hunters. Permits issues by Gauteng nature conservation show that at least 2 sets of lions were sent to lion hunting establishments in the last 2 years. We are currently trying to get more recent stats. Another area of concern is the lack of control over these hunts. Nature conservation officials are meant to be present to ensure that the hunt goes off humanely and the the hunters comply with the permit regulations and dont hunt more than what the permit allows. But authorities are short staffed and this rarely happens. Which of course may explain why the stats for lion hunts don't correlate. There are substantially more trophies listed by the Chinese government than what CITES and the SA govt reflect in their stats. There is also around 3 tonnes of lion bones exported last year, And it seems the numbers keep growing annually, Food for thought next time you cuddle a cub.

title: Honey Bee Crisis

Two thirds of the worlds crops rely on bees for fertilisation . Infected bee colonies can be treated with anti biotics but the South African bee industry is divided on this, with some worried about the dangers of the antibiotics and chemicals , and with the Chairman of the Northern Transvaal Beekeepers Jan Steenkamp saying that Cape beekeepers should "just kill all the bees in the Western Cape " .Mike Allsopp of the Agricultural Research Council disagrees says South Africa is now somewhere between a crisis and a catastrophe , and that bees are indispensable when it comes to South African food security and that a mixed approach to solving the problem MUST be used , using antibodies and working with the Department of Agriculture and developing disease resistant honey bees .So we ask what can be done to avert this crisis ? And what is being done? And why is there so much disagreement about what is the right way forward? The Department of Agriculture is only just starting to train bee inspectors unlike any other country facing this issue ...most of the big role players in the South African Bee industry will be at a conference in Pietermaritzburg this weekend , but will also be available in the Western Cape next week ...

title: Medicinal uses of Cannabis

summary: There is currently a raging debate around the medicinal used of cannabis in South Africa, sparked by a conference held in Benoni this week. It harks back to the campaign started by Mario Ambrosini that really went nowhere. The debate in South Africa can benefit by insights from the US where the conversation has been ongoing for many years and where it is slightly more sophisticated. In the US 23 states have allowed the medicinal use of cannabis and 3 states so far have approved the recreational use of cannabis. There is a story behind the story -- why was cannabis outlawed in the US? Could it have been for other than medical reasons? Dr David Bearman, one of the US's foremost practitioners prescribing cannabis to patients believes that this is the case. He is a passionate supporter of the medicinal use of cannabis and has recently also published a book "Drugs are NOT the Tools of the Devil: How Discrimination and Greed Created a Dysfunctional Drug Policy and How It Can Be Fixed". He considers cannabis a wonder drug that is non-toxic and has a plethora of medicinal uses, including fighting cancer. And he says it has no side effects. Dr Donald P. Tashkin is an American pulmonologist at UCLA who has studied the effects of cannabis Tashkin has spent 30 years studying cannabis. In 2006, he was in charge of a large case-control study on marijuana and the risk of cancer. Contrary to his group's expectations, the study found no increase in lung cancer risk even among heavy users of marijuana. We met him and it is surprising to find that he, as medical specialist, considers cannabis smoking beneficial for general lung health. We have interviews with both these specialists, and they have surprising medical insights and claims -- contrary to what is commonly believed about cannabis..

title: Children and past lives

summary: How could a two-year-old in Louisiana remember being a World War II pilot shot down over the Pacific? Or a boy in Oklahoma recall being a Hollywood extra? For more than a decade, Prof Jim Tucker has travelled the country meeting families, hearing stories like these, and trying to determine if the children’s memories are valid. Continuing a fifty-year research project at the University of Virginia involving children from all over the world, he decided to focus on cases in the United States, where parents would not expect their children to say such things. The children usually begin talking about a past life at the age of two or three and may talk about a previous family or the way they died in a previous life. Their statements have often been found to be accurate for one particular deceased individual, and some children have recognized members of the previous family. A number have also had birthmarks or defects that matched wounds on the body of the deceased person. We interview Prof Jim Tucker and try to find South African case studies by means of an open call to viewers who have children with stories about past lives.

title: Second Sight

A company in California has developed a device, a bionic eye that can restore sight to people with conditions that affect the retina. A small camera sends impulses to an implant in a patients eye and these impulses are transmitted to the optical nerve. The brain then interprets the impulses and the patient can see.

title: Richard to Amber

He is a charming man and one aspect of this story is that he has waited so long for this transgender operation. He seems to have now found peace. If one goes back into his life, his quite severe identity issues can explain a sometimes turbulent past - drugs, failed marriages, suicide attempts etc. Now that he has so called 'come out' and told his friends about his decision to become a woman, he has found acceptance and, in a way, some peace. We follow the story of this young man as he takes his hormonal treatments, the chiselling of his adams apple, a realignment of his jaw. We are present at his final operation to rearrange his genitals and we also interview him afterwards. We learn of the advances that are made. For example, using nerve endings, they are able to build clitorises. These men turned woman can actually achieve orgasm. We also learn that there are strict procedures to undergo these operations in the legal way. One requirement overseas is that before hormonal treatment, a man has to dress like a woman for three months. It is often quite archaic and humiliating. We also learn that new research has found female genetics in the brain but trapped in a male body. title: FREE STATE HEALTH CRISIS II
