summary: The Free State Department of Health is in a state of collapse. With the MEC of Health in the province boasting that patient care and the safety of patient are his number one priority, patients and doctors on the ground disagree. What they see and experience is not at all the view that the MEC has of what is going on his own department. When in an accident on the N3 or N5, you will be taken to the Thebe Hospital in Harrismith, medical aid or not. But how equipped is the ambulance that will take you there and the casualty unit at Thebe Hospital where you need to be stabilised or treated? It is the only hospital in a 80km radius, yet it is still only a district hospital - with no CT scanner. Our source says he prays that he never has to land up in that hospital. We also again turn our focus to the Free State Health Department's finances - how much wasteful expenditure was there in 2014/2015? And what does the MEC plan to do about the cash-strapped department that doesn't have enough money to provide medicine and basic consumables or cannot repair equipment or infrastructure at failing state hospitals in the province?
experts: Mr. Benny Malakoane FS MEC Health

title: Gilan Gork - Debunking Psychics
summary: Gilan Gork II – Debunking Psychics South African mentalist Gilan Gork has approached us to do a programme that looks at debunking psychics. How psychics use psychological tools of influence and persuasion but having a psychic ability is a myth. Our programme starts with the set up that Carte Blanche recruits a few volunteers who want to participate in a psychic experiment with Gilan. The experiment is loosely based on a famous psychology experiment called the Barnum or Forer effect. Here is an excerpt from Wiki that explains it. The Forer effect (also called the Barnum effect after P. T. Barnum's observation that "we've got something for everyone") is the observation that individuals will give high accuracy ratings to descriptions of their personality that supposedly are tailored specifically for them, but are in fact vague and general enough to apply to a wide range of people. This effect can provide a partial explanation for the widespread acceptance of some beliefs and practices, such as astrology, fortune telling, graphology, religion, aura reading and some types of personality tests.

title: Free State Health Crisis

summary: Doctors working in the Free State public Health Sector say the system has bene brought to collapse through a combination of ineptitude, corruption and neglect – despite repeated complaints, cries for help and going the extra mile. In an anonymous letter they write: “We are medical doctors working in government hospitals in the Free State who believe it is our duty to inform the public of the dire conditions in the Free State Department of Health. “Not many years ago the hospitals in the Free State were among the best in the country, known not only for the world class medical care that they provided, but also as excellent training institutions for medical students, interns and registrars. Doctors used to queue for employment in these hospitals. The decline of the Free State health system has accelerated since Ace Magashule became premier, and even more so with the appointment of Benny Malakoane as MEC for Health.”

To date they have been used during drug busts in Mitchell’s Plain at night and the Police have been able to monitor and track people escaping and hiding from officials. They are being flown over the Standfontein area, a notorious part of Cape Town where cable thieves burn the plastic off copper cable under the cover of darkness before they take it to scrap dealers. They've partnered with WESSA (WILDLIFE AND ENV SOC OF SA) and they're endorsed by numerous scientists and environmentalists. They use WESSA's methodology for testing their water samples. They call themselves "citizen scientists" and the aim of their trip is to measure the health of the Vaal which is so crucial to the survival of Gauteng and NorthWest and industry/mining/farmers along the way. title: Artificial pancreas for 4 year old boy in Australia
oneLiner: Break through technology in the treatment of Type 1 Diabetes
summary: Xavier Hames like many Type 1 Diabetes sufferers was diagnosed as a toddler; it is most prevalent in small children and young adults. His mother tells the story about trying to prick the finger of her small child 4/5 times a day to check his sugar levels and then having to give him regular injections. She talks about the fear of putting him to bed, the fear that her child will have a hypoglycemic attack at night and go into a coma. Dr. Jones/Official spokesperson for the new technology, explains what Type 1 diabetes is and what treatments have been available up until today. He introduces us to the insulin pump, which has been around since 2003. It required human intervention to monitor and release the insulin. Fast forward to 2015 and the old insulin pump has taken on a new form, this new pump can actually predict when glucose levels have become dangerously low and therefore stop the release of insulin. The pump is starting to behave like an artificially pancreas, allowing both mother and child a solid nights sleep. This ‘artificial pancreas’ also allows Xavier to live more like a normal 4-year-old boy, he can have a bowl of pasta or eat the food at a party. To bring it home we speak to pediatric diabetic specialists dr. Segal about this new technology, when it will make it to South Africa, if it will be affordable and whether or not this is a practical solution for Type 1 diabetes sufferers over here. Dr. Jones/Spokesperson explains how long this pump has been in development and what is next for type 1 diabetes patients. Xavier is the first patient, but when will this be available world and what does it cost.

title: Kaileigh Fryers bucket list

It was a one-car accident; the driver of the vehicle was drunk. Kaileigh’s friends try to piece together the night of the accident. Trying to move forward from losing their bestie. While Kaileighs family are struggling to keep going, her mom is battling to get out of bed. Losing a child and a best friend at 19, when they have their whole life ahead of them can destroy you; it will definitely change your life forever. But Kaileigh’s death has changed the world in a way no one expected. While packing up her things, Kaileigh’s parents found her diary and on one of the pages she had made a bucket list of 49 things she had to do before she died. But they weren’t normal 19-year-old things, like fall in love or bungee jump. Some of them were, but most of them were about making the world a better place. Things like volunteering overseas, talking to an old person about their life, donating blood, inspiring somebody, making a difference, starting an orphanage, adopting a child. They were things far beyond her years Kaileigh’s bucket list went Viral. The world has started ticking it off. The family set-up a FB group and people from Australia, Germany, Mongolia, Kenya, Texas, Utah all started ticking off things from Kaileigh’s bucket list and posting videos to her FB group. Videos of them dancing in the rain, giving blood, running marathons and volunteering over seas. Her life may have been cut short, but her spirit continues to change the world!

summary: Martin Pistorius was a twelve-year-old boy in South Africa when he was struck by a mysterious illness. He was slowly debilitated... until he could no longer move his body, or speak. Then he slipped into what doctors called a vegetative state. His parents were told he would soon be dead. But after four years, something happened inside Martin. His mind began to function again, but not his body. He was soon fully aware of everything around him, but had no way of sharing. He was trapped inside his own body, like a ghost boy. title: Eastern Cape Farm Abuse - Whipping
oneLiner: Where do addicts turn when they've burnt all their bridges? Anthony Tovy provides a home and work on his farm in the Eastern Cape. Little did the boys know they'd leave, literally, scarred for life.
summary: In the Eastern Cape near Uitenhage lies a farm where Anthony Dovey provides homes for young men that have strayed and are struggling with their addiction to drugs. Anthony offers them a roof over their heads and pays them minimum wage to work on his produce farm. Enter the young addicts: Michael, Adrian, Sam and Matthew. They all lived on the farm. Adrian Pizani has been in every rehab centre in JHB and CT. He has tried many times to get clean, losing his family, friends and young adult years to Herion, Dagga,and Cocaine. He realized his addiction would cost him his life. His best friend Michael Cusdin, who served in the Navy and got hooked on drugs there, told him about the Farm in the Eastern Cape. Little did they know what they were in for. Adrian and Michael spoke to Anthony first on the phone, he said that he has space for them and they decided to leave in early 2014. Anthony, at first, seemed quite normal. The man was in his 40's and the other young men seemed to like him. It wasn't until Adrian and Michael stole a bottle of Anthony's whisky that they found out how Anthony would "cure" them. Anthony tied Adrian to the barn ceiling - called the torture chamber. He handcuffed his hands so he was unable to move, pulled down his pants and made him stand there in his underwear - sometimes Anthony made him go naked. Anthony then took a sjambok and whip and beat Anthony until he would pass out. His scars and injuries were so severe-the photographs speak for themselves. While Anthony inflicted his "torture" on the young man, he got an erection, and screams "suffer, suffer!" All of the young men on the farm were given this same treatment, but Adrian was "special" to Anthony. One night Anthony climbed into bed with Adrian and sexually assaulted him. This caused Adrian to finally leave. Adrian, Michael and Sam are making police cases.

title: Unsecured Lending

summary: For the last three years Cambist has been offering investors the impossible – a 19.5% return guaranteed on their investment by buying up bad debt. It sounded like an offer that was too good to be true but for three years investors have been receiving their repayments on time and without any issues. So has Cambist achieved the impossible? Or is there more going on? Cambist is part of a spider’s web of partially-connected companies – Bridge, OneLaw, Flemix, Solvo, OneSys to name but a few. Bridge, a similar investment scheme, was placed under business rescue earlier this year and investors were told that if the company is liquidated they’ll only get 18c for every R1 of their original investment. But Cambist has been going to great lengths to stress that they are a separate company to Bridge and are not affected in any way. Then on Monday 1 December, around 300 employees of OneLaw, the company that owns and runs Cambist, got a nasty surprise – the company was being liquidated. There was no warning, there would be no severance packages and everyone had an hour to pack up their desks and leave. But Cambist insists things are still fine and investors will keep getting their money. To put it into perspective Cambist has received approximately R700-million in investments – even former Foreign Minister Pik Botha is an investor.

Werner’s wife, Hannelie, a doctor, was working at a hospital when the attack began. We speak to Riana du Plessis, Hannelie’s sister “It was their life mission, to train the Afghans, to support them, to help them.” She said the attack had apparently been carried out by three people dressed as policemen, including a suicide bomber. Du Plessis said: “The Taliban thought that they [the South Africans} were trying to convert Muslims to be Christians. They targeted my brother-in-law, Werner.” . He and his children had been taken aside and shot and they bled to death, she said. We look at the situation in Kabul, possible reasons why the family were killed. We talk to Dutch Reformed Church in Moreleta Park in Pretoria, where Groenewald had been a full-time pastor. The Dominee Willem Badenhorst said the family had been in Kabul to serve the community.

It is the city's most enduring cultural asset, constantly adapting to the needs of a changing society. We provide a brief history over the last 100 years of the orchestra and the stars it has produced. We discover how and why they have managed to survive when local government funding dried up many years ago. The orchestra manages to survive by outsourcing themselves to a variety of genres - musical productions, international acts etc. But one of the orchestras main functions is to develop skills transfers in the communities. They have training initiatives in townships around Cape Town which are benchmark projects. The aim of these projects are to provide employment for youngsters in the future. A gala concert and dinner is taking place at the beginning of November to commemorate, with the release of a new book, 100 years of existence.

title: Aqua Safety - preventing drowning
oneLiner: ...prevent your child form becoming another drowning statistic.
summary: Drowning remains one of the top causes of unnatural childhood death in South Africa. According to recent statistics released by private hospital group Netcare, nearly 72% of near-drownings occur around the home and only 1.22% at the beach. Three-year-old children seem particularly vulnerable and constitute 45.45% of the total. Furthermore, for every child that dies from drowning, five are left with permanent brain damage from the lack of oxygen that occurs in a near-drowning. With summer approaching, many more children are set to drown this year. There are many measures that can be introduced to make pools and bodies of water safe, but one of the best options is to teach children to survive when falling into water. We visit a swimming pool where babies and toddlers (from 6 months upwards) are taught to survive and float for at least 15 minutes after falling in a pool fully clothed with a winter jacket on. title: Ghetto Rainbow nation
oneLiner: A voyeuristic journey into PE's slums where Nigerian druglords like alongside Afrikaans tannies. Its South Africa like you have never seen it before.
summary: The focus of this story is Impala flats in PE's poor, formerly white suburb of Sydenham in North End. It's now PE's Hillbrow. Run by two drug lords - one Nigerian and one Afrikaans and white they control access to the flats. They control the drugs and they control the prostitutes who work from the building. It's their hub. Their dealers are a mxed bag - a true rainbow nation who we have on camera performing prison rituals in the passage ways. They aren't scared to flick a knife at an interloper, but they also treat the old Afrikaans tannies who live there with great respect, helping them with their groceries and even supplying the odd joint to help make life more bearable. The prostitute in the building is Elsabe. She's 17 and lives there with her 16 year old drug dealer boyfriend. She's pregnant now and wants out. What you see here is a microcosm of the macrocosm - the people are desperate, poor and will do anything to survive. They don't see colour anymore - only the colour of money. And for them they say this is the easiest way to make it.

title: Kyalami Retrospective
oneLiner: One of the great monuments of South African sport looks like its heading toward the checkered flag.
summary: The Kyalami Race Track is a major part of South Africa's sport's legacy. The venue hosted 21 Grand Prix races, and numerous A1 and World Superbike Series races. The track opened in 1961, hosted the world's top F1 drivers for 20 consecutive years, was shut down in the mid-80s because of political sanctions, and again hosted Formula One in 1993. With ownership having changed hands several times and the current owners being liquidated, the track is going on auction on the 24th of July. Depending on who buys it, Kyalami will either be rehabilitated as a race track, or be razed to the ground to make way for commercial and residential development.

title: THE BATTLE FOR UKRAINE
oneLiner: A dozen other countries were pulled into, what has been described as Putin's reckless war in Ukraine this week, when a passenger plane was shot out the skies killing all on board.
summary: The incident touched off immediate finger-pointing between pro-Russian separatists and the Ukrainian government. Kiev denied involvement and labelled the incident a "terrorist act." Russian President Vladimir Putin responded by blaming the Ukraine, saying “This tragedy would not have happened if there was peace on this land, if the military actions had not been renewed in southeast Ukraine." But many in Ukraine say it’s Putin who is fuelling the fires of war in the Ukraine. In February 100 Ukrainian protesters were gunned down in Kiev’s Maidan Square by suspected Pro-Russian separatists. And later that month Russian forces annexed Crimea. And if that wasn’t enough to set Russia and the west on a collision course, the downing of MH 17might is the tipping point... and ordinary Ukrainians are worried they’re going to end up stuck in the middle of an all out war between the worlds super powers.

title: Fly By Night Ambulances
oneLiner: Few state ambulances in KZN are fit to run; and a dangerous fly by night ambulance industry has sprung up. With no regulations in place to rein them in, these cowboy operators are getting away with it
summary: When an ambulance arrives at the scene of an emergency, you think help has arrived. There’s just one problem - ambulance services operating in KwaZulu-Natal’s private sector are not regulated. You could be transported in a vehicle that is not properly equipped to deal with your injury or treated by someone who is not properly qualified. Medical aids and the RAF will only pay ambulance companies that have been certified by their industry body, the Board of Healthcare Funders (BHF). However, once an ambulance provider has been issued a practice number there is no mechanism in place to monitor their operations. As a result, unscrupulous operators have rushed to the scene.

title: Finance Minister Nhlanhla Nene
oneLiner: How will newly appointed Finance Minister Nene steer the economy that is heading in the direction of another recession, how will he improve business relations and international investor confidence?
summary: How will newly appointed Finance Minister Nene steer the economy that is heading in the direction of another recession, how will he improve business relations and international investor confidence? South Africa is Africa's most advanced economy, but can we remain the prime investment destination? Minister Nhlanhla Nene said that an uneven demand from aborad and the protracted mining strike capped South Africa's economic growth at around 2% this year. That could stoke continued volatility in the value of the country's currency, the rand and interrupt plans to narrow the budget deficit and it would be a challenge to achieve the numbers government had penciled in. How will he guide through this and what other plans will he put in place? Who is he and why will he make a good Minister of Finance? What does the future hold for the South African economy in his view?

title: Classified Cons
oneLiner: From buying a rolls royce, to planning a beach holiday - be careful of the fraudsters on the other side of the keyboard.
summary: This is very much a process story, Carte Blanche extra style taking a look scamsters in the online classifieds world. We start by going out and buying a rica'ed sim card from a dodgy little shop in Randburg and film it on hidden camera. Armed with this we can operate....we've had numerous complaints of various types of scams so we are going to take a look for ourselves. First we place an ad for a Ipad we have for sale on several classifieds. What we are hoping for is that one of the crooks who has taken a consumer for a ride by providing fake proof of payment is scouring the net and takes the bait...just like he did in the case of Brandon Morton whose nephew lost his playstation after he handed it over to crooks who had actually never paid. We hope to set up our own sting and do the handover in a public place and confront the driver...we may even need to get the banks involved to verify the POP. Next we look at identity theft...a man posing to sell a Rolls Royce and claiming to be on an overseas mission - except when we track him down, he is indeed overseas but has no Rolls Royce for sale. His passport details are being used to give credence to the scamster...skype interview in the DRC and his wife is here. Then there is the Missing in Action variety of crook, he advertises cattle, sheep and even holidays on the web, get's you to pay the deposit and when you get there the promised stock or holiday house simply does not exist. The bottom line is Rica is meant to sort this out, meant to help track down conmen like this.... but it's not working. These guys are advertising every day and they just keep changing sims and its business as usual. Who is policing this? Why are there no raids and how do consumers protect themselves against these classified cons?

title: Vets Bills
oneLiner: Are vets bills exorbitant or justified? We look into the prices that vets in JHB area charge.
summary: Vets bills are a topic of much contention in South Africa. Routine procedures can end up costing a fortune, people who cannot afford to pay for procedures sometimes have to euthanize their pets and vets prices seem to vary depending on which practice you take your animals to. The SA veterinary council does not provide pricing tariffs or a pricing guideline. Vets say their fees are justified given the years they study, the long hours they work, state of the art equipment and because of the quality of care. On the other side of the spectrum, we have community vets who charge minimal rates, but they are only available to minimal income earners. So what happens to the modest income earners who are slapped with a R 10 000 vets bill?

title: Texting & Driving
oneLiner: Mobile device use while driving is becoming one of the leading causes of death in the world. In South Africa we are only just starting to scratch the surface of this global issue.
summary: According to recent studies, using your mobile device whilst driving is becoming one of the leading causes of death in the world. In the US, the statistics show that texting whilst driving results in more road fatalities than drinking and driving. South Africa has a relatively poor road safety record, with over 16 000 fatalities every year. Research shows that in over 90% of car accidents the driver causes the accident and distracted driving is becoming an increasing problem. For the first time in SA, we are starting to look at our drivers behaviour. Discovery has developed an app that monitors one’s mobile device usage. By recording people’s behavior they found that drivers who use their cellphones while on the road record an average of 52 seconds of distracted driving per trip – the equivalent of one kilometre driving blind at 60 km/h. We put these statistics to the test to determine just how dangerous driving whilst using your phone can be..

The Robben Island Museum is so frustrated by the lack of maintenance that it presented a report to the Arts and Culture portfolio committee requesting to take over maintenance of the island. title: PE Murderous Ganglands
oneLiner: It's been called the land of shattered dreams - there have been more than 140 gang related deaths in PE's northern suburbs in the last two years.
summary: n the ganglands of Port Elizabeth's northern suburbs violence and sudden death are almost daily events. Driven by drugs, drug trafficking and at other times seemingly senseless, motiveless causes, death stalks at will. Young men and boys find themselves drawn inexorably into this tangle of lawlessness that leaves so many dead and dying; stricken parents weeping over the lifeless bodies of their bullet-ridden children, crying out for the answers to the eternal question "Why . . .?" The names of the once peaceful suburbs of Schauderville, Gelvandale, Helenvale and Bethelsdorp now are now almost as synonymous with violent death as Passchendaele, Ypres, and the Somme, albeit on a smaller scale. Currently nine gangs roam the dark streets in search of prey: the Dustlifes, Paparazzi, Upstand Dogs, Blink Boemelaars, Sesteen Honde, Von Boeties, Untouchables, Boomshakaas and the Shootas. Murder and gun battles are the order of the day. Law enforcement is considered so dangerous that in August 2012, the police requested assistance from the army in a bid to combat this apparently unstoppable lawlessness. The SAPS tactical response team (TRT) works in groups. Its members are dressed in helmets, blue overalls and bulletproof gear and resemble American SWAT teams. But successes are limited. Some gang leaders have been arrested and recently, Dust Lives gang member, Gavin Minnie, was sentenced to 40 years in prison for the murder and robbery of Nelson Mandela Bay traffic officer Neal Domingo. But these amorphous groups seem to merely splinter into new gangs with new leaders who must fight one another to gain or retain dominance. Victims of fatal shootings have been as young as 13, as in the case of a boy caught in lethal crossfire. Other killings are performed execution-style in cold blood in front of the victim’s friends or family members.

title: GREYHOUND RACING
oneLiner: Dog racing has been put back on South Africa's gambling agenda just three years after government decided to abandon the idea. Who’s behind the push and should it be stopped in its tracks?
summary: SUMMARY Dog racing has been illegal in South Africa since 1949. Yet the government are considering legalising greyhound racing with their recent publication of the proposed Draft National gambling Norms standards in the Government Gazette no 37653 of 23 May 2014. The bill included dog racing as part of a proposed suite of gambling activities. Cora Baily, from IFAW wants to know “What can have possibly changed since 2011 when the department... backed down from the idea of greyhound racing?” In 2011 despite a massive lobby by the pro-racing fraternity, government responded positively to overwhelming evidence of the cruelty and welfare concerns related to dog fighting. In the rush to legalise the sport, hardly any thought has been given to how it will be regulated. IFAW believed legalising greyhound racing would only worsen an already out-of-control animal welfare crisis in South Africa. They fear the same syndicates involved in illegal dog fighting and hunting will jump on board and will open illegal racetracks – especially in remote areas of the EC and Mpumalanga, where it’s difficult to monitor them. The re-introduction of greyhound racing under the poor socio-economic conditions that affected much of South Africa would lead the dogs to be seen as expendable commodities. Greyhound puppy mills will spring up. The greyhound racing industry, internationally, is notorious for the high number of dogs put down each year because they aren’t champions.... tens of thousands of greyhounds are euthanized last year in Australia.

title: Free State Healthcare (Free State Health)
oneLiner: Stockouts, no money for elective surgeries - is the Free state health care system in need of resuscitation?
summary: STATEMENT: FREE STATE HEALTH SYSTEM IN COLLAPSE – LIVES ARE BEING LOST Free State Health System in Collapse – Lives are Being Lost Urgent & Immediate Intervention from Minister of Health needed JOHANNESBURG – The Free State health system is collapsing with stock outs of more than 200 essential drugs and supplies at the provincial depot, desperate health workers begging for help and stock outs of supplies needed for critical investigations such as electrocardiographies (ECGs). ECGs monitor heart activity for various medical procedures. Out of stock drugs at the depot include antiretrovirals, antibiotics, pain killers, meningitis treatment, anti-psychotic medication, anti-rabies drugs, high blood pressure medication and epilepsy medicine. Supplies include anti-TB masks for health workers and solution to sterilise theatre equipment. The depot also has no HIV tests. A doctor working at a hospital in Bloemfontein reported to SECTION27 that they are increasingly running out of essential devices which they need for lifesaving procedures. These devices include infusion sets (connects the infusion bag to the venous catheter), central venous lines (a catheter placed into a large vein in the neck, chest or groin to administer medication or fluids, especially in emergency situations and in critically ill patients) and spinal needles (used for spinal anaesthesia and lumbar punctures to test for among others meningitis). “

title: Cigarette Hijackings
oneLiner: Somedays 12 cigarette trucks a day are hijacked and in some cases blue lights and Hawks officials have been fingered. It's a lucrative trade but why the veil of silence?
summary: Every day in South Africa there are between 5 and 12 cigarette truck hijackings. Many those involve British American Tobacco vehicles, We have footage of one of these hijackings in a garage forecourt, it shows the driver being hijacked at gunpoint while unloading at the garage. The vehicle is driven off and we have footage of it at its resting place in a suburb nearby. We also have footage of several other hijacking scenes around Johannesburg. And then comes the story of a truck hijacked on the Heidelburg road on the East Rand by Hawks officials who it appears may have been in cahoots with the fidelity security vehicle escorting the truck. There are too many anomalies: the truck is hijacked yet the escort does not sound the alarm via radio or panic button. The driver is forced out of the vehicle at gunpoint after being stopped by police officers with blue lights. He is forced into their car and bundled on top of the two fidelity guards. The saps officials then fire into the fidelity vehicle to give credence to the hijacking claim. It all just seems too staged. The SAPS then take the truck and in a separate care take the three men from the transport and security company and dump them in Midrand. Several hours later the truck is recovered in Soweto without the 12 million rand cigarette cargo. A third of the cargo is later recovered and Hawks officials arrested. The driver takes part in a line-up at the police station and co-incidentally meats his death 4 days later in a "car accident." Did he know too much? And why has the cigarette trade become so lucrative and so dangerous? We ask could it flourish without dirty cops propping up organised crime?

title: A Step Forward
oneLiner: One in 500 children are born with this defect, meet a woman who has pioneered a method of correcting clubfoot
summary: South African, Karen Moss’s son Alex was born with a clubfoot. The common treatment for a child born with this defect is a series of very painful operations, something Karen dreaded her son going through. So she looked further and found a Dr Ponseti in Iowa, US, who had pioneered a new method of successfully treating children born with this, simply put through a series of casts that slowly adjust the foot until its normal. After Alex had been successfully treated by Dr Ponseti Karen delved into the situation in South Africa and saw the desperate need of 1 in 500 children born in South Africa with clubfoot. Clubfoot is the most common musculo-skeletal birth defect. Many people still have no idea what it is. She started by bringing Dr’s trained in this method to South Africa, raising awareness and to give parents the information she had found personally lacking. In her words “ Every child has a right to have the opportunity to walk and run and play sport normally” Over time it became a regional effort, more training, a clinic support programme and lots of family support. She works through a grant from the US and partner clinics in Western Cape, Gauteng, Free State, Mpumalanga and Northern Cape. Clinics which are extremely busy. They are expanding to KZN . Karen is an inspirational talker, and dedicated spreading the method outside South Africa. They have two families here that they have been filming, as case studies, a newborn still going through the process, in Khayalitsha, and a one year old, in Delft who has already had successful treatment. She has footage of Dr Ponseti in the US. Her persona story interwoven with South African case studies ( balck and white) and the method would be a very strong story with practical implications for so many.

summary: In November last year when Radovan Krejcir was arrested on kidnapping and assault charges, the Hawks and private investigators reacted with surprise. The arresting officers was Col Killer Ximba, a Mdluli man with a past. Murder charges, allegations of torture and yet one of the most trusted men by Number One. Hardly surprising then that he was named as a benefactor in a Goldfields BEE deal. Col Ximba is an Mdluli man, promoted from constable to colonel in a day by murder accused spy boss Richard Mdluli, his confidant and long time associate. They worked together at the Vosloorus police station when Mdluli was accused of murder in a suspected love triangle. Ximba was also linked to Krejcir. A source alleges that Ximba was on Krejcir's payroll and the arrest was the result of Krejcir not paying over a 10k fee for handing over the brother of Krejcir's associate Doctor who disappeared with 25kg's of Tik. Suspicious and in an alleged act of revenge Ximba arrested Krejcir and allegedly tortured him. Then to cover his tracks and strengthen the case he, its alleged, trumped up conspiracy to murder charges, used Paul O'Sullivan as a foil to give credence to his claims. An ingenious plan if its true. Then, its alleged he arrested members of his own unit to prevent them from ratting him out, people like Nandi Rose Nkosi. They weren't clean either and he its said had dirt on her and some of the other members of his unit. It's a story of police corruption to rival the Jackie Selebi trial.

title: XDR-TB the Airborne Plague
summary: Phumeza Tisile and Linda Schutte from the opposite side of Cape Town both contracted Pre-XDR TB. Phumeza was 18 when she was diagnosed with TB and spent the next two years at deaths door, for 8 months she was misdiagnosed as having normal TB when in fact she had contracted Multiple Resistant TB from the outset. The initial treatment for MDR has left her deaf. A new drug which is not prescribed for the treatment of TB called linezolid saved her life. But linezolid costs R750 a tablet and the Medical Control Council won’t allow the generic to be imported. 80% of patients with XDR-TB die. Phumeza is now campaigning to have this and other drugs made accessible. Linda Schutte a housewife from the opposite side of town was also misdiagnosed for 4 months by her GP and all the while she was spreading MDR-TB. Finally after an x-ray revealed she had TB she went to treatment at the local clinic, she had no idea of the horror that lay ahead. Each blood test returned with worse results- she had pre XDR-TB. She was told she had to be admitted to the only hospital for treating XDR- TB- Brooklyn Chest in the Western Cape. Her experience was so terrifying that having spent a day in the facility she discharged herself and said she would rather die at home than die in Brooklyn Chest. Once again due the treatment on linezolid she is recovering but she too has to overcome the horrific side effects of partial deafness, nausea, psychosis, delusions and 30 pills a day for the next two years. Linezolid treatment costs R22 000 a month and medical aid does not cover it.

title: Tony Leon: Opposite Mandela
oneLiner: Tony Leon post election talks about his time in parliament opposite Mandela and today's challenges
summary: ony Leon has written a book of unique insight into an unexplored aspect of the presidency and leadership of Nelson Mandela. Opposite Mandela relates the untold stories of how South Africa's first democratic president related to his political opponents. Leon served as leader of the Democratic Party during Mandela's presidency. Although they clashed, sometimes fiercely, on great issues of the day, Leon enjoyed an unusually warm relationship with Mandela and had direct access to the president's office. In this first-hand account, he relates some of the more consequential moments of those momentous times in South Africa's history-in-the- making through the lens of the opposition. Although this is a personal account, it also explores some of the major themes, from reconciliation to corruption, which not only marked that period but also laid the basis for the current challenges which confront South Africa today, nearly two decades after Mandela assumed the country’s highest office, the very moment when Leon's political leadership began. Insightful, and simultaneously serious and amusing, this highly readable, first-hand account considers in a balanced manner both the golden moments and the blind spots of one of the most consequential presidencies and leaders of the modern democratic age.

The hospital is seriously understaffed, 4 staff members for instance in a 100 bed hospital. The roof is falling apart and maintenance issues are ignored. A cat apparently fell through the roof onto a child in the paediatric ward. The roads are full of potholes, the municipal electricity infrastructure is ailing, with power sporadic and unreliable and although its flooding in parts - there is no water in the taps. The landfill sites aren't managed instead they simply burn the rubbish - engulfing the town in toxic smoke and raw sewerage flows through the streets. This all despite the fact that Co-operative governance MEC Skhosana has failed to successfully intervene in the financial and governance affairs that have been plaguing the town for months. The task team that was announced with great fanfare, to deliver a turnaround strategy and deliver quality services has failed dismally - in fact if the townsfolk are to be believed the situation is worse than ever. Hardly surprising when the municipality is in dire financial straits - with a budget shortfall in excess of !68 million. It's also alleged that funds meant for infrastructure development is used to pay debt and salaries. The sheriff is apparently writing up municipal assets for attachment over bad debt and Eskom arrears run into millions.

title: Crime Scene: Pretoria

summary: Forensic specialists Kimberely Guluzian and Walter Sawall are amongst the world’s leading CSI investigators, based in Los Angeles, California. They have decades of experience, helping to unravel some of the most perplexing crimes in the US and around the world. In addition to their Police work, Kimberely and Walter are sought out by many of Hollywood’s leading film and television producers, to ensure that the forensics seen on global hits such as Dexter and the CSI Series are accurate. In an exclusive partnership now with TRIAL TV, Kimberely and Walter introduce Trial TV presenter Subniv Babuta to the real, often unseen, world of forensic investigation. For them, the Oscar case is unique. Forensic evidence is usually used to assess whether an individual did, or did not commit a crime. Oscar admits to the killing of Reeva – there is no need to prove that he was responsible for her death. So, in this case, how exactly can the forensics help us? Giving Subniv unprecedented access to their work, Kimberely and Walter share surprising new insights into the forensic details which could unlock the Oscar investigation. title: Airshow accident investigation

summary: On 12 October 2013 world champion aerobatic pilot Glen Dell competed at an air show in Secunda. After a final spin, the aircraft plummeted to the ground, bounced on its undercarriage and was finally stopped by a wire mesh fence. An uninterrupted video reveals that Glen was still alive after the crash and moving in the cockpit. Within minutes the plane started to burn. Just 1 minute 18 seconds after the crash the first fire truck arrived, but was seemingly unprepared. Glen died at as a result 90% burn wounds to his entire body later that evening. Now specialist reports reveal that he survived the crash, but died later from burn wounds as fire officials could not manage to put out the flames in the required time. How could emergency personnel have been so unprepared at an event of this magnitude? And, who's to blame? The buck it seems, in this case, stops with the Civil Aviation Authority.

title: Will the Youth Go to the Polls (Youth Vote)
oneLiner: We ask the question: will South Africa’s youth vote in the upcoming election? What does it matter to South Africa’s future if they do – or do not?
summary: President Jacob Zuma is expected to announce the date of the general elections any day now. The end of April or early May are touted as likely dates. Arguably, this will be the most important election – our fifth – since 1994, 20 years of democracy later. It will certainly be the most closely contested, with the ANC possibly dipping below 60% of the vote, the DA consolidating its gains in past elections and newcomers like Julius Malema’s Economic Freedom Fighters and Mamphele Ramphele’s Agang still unknown quantities. On the weekend of February 8th and 9th the IEC is holding its final registration drive, to register new voters and re-register voters who have moved to a different part of the country and want their vote to count in the province where they now live. For them, the worrying fact is that barely a quarter of 18 and 19 year olds and just over half of 20 to 29 year olds are registered. Go to the 30-39 year old age group and the percentage rockets to 87%, and even higher – 96%, for people in their 50s and 60s. All the major political parties have launched web apps and beefed up their social media presence aimed at capturing the youth vote. The ANC recently launched MyANCApp, while Twitter, Facebook and Mixit are the main platforms the parties are targeting. The DA recorded the fastest-growing number of Likes on Facebook in the last quarter of 2013, with the EFF running a close second, though they currently outpace both the ANC and the DA in total Facebook Likes.

title: ANIMAL HOARDERS
oneLiner: Locked in cupboards, stashed in washing machines and crammed into drawers, animals are falling victim to one of society’s strangest obsessions - animal hoarding.
summary: During her years working as a senior inspector, Reinet Meyer says she has seen countless cases of animal cruelty but none as bizarre and as heart-wrenching as what her team found when they responded to a case of an apparent animal hoarder in October last year. Cast Study no 1 The house belonged to a 72-year-old lady, Petra Paulson. Six months earlier the SPCA in Bloemfontein has confiscated a number of animals and laid a charge against her. But when they did a follow-up inspection they found she had starting the cycle of hoarding animals once again. The smell was overwhelming, with excretion all over the floor. In the kitchen they found a number of dogs 'hidden' inside the cupboards. In the draw of a steel cupboard they found a Miniature Doberman, crouching between the cutlery, literally wedged between the knives and forks. In another cupboard two dogs were hiding behind a toaster and another sitting between pots and pans. All the cupboards were locked and the dogs were trapped inside. Shockingly, they were told that the dogs live in the cupboard all the time and are never allowed out. In the bathroom they found dogs inside washing machines. One dog had faeces stuck all over her tail. She was covered with worms, which were literally eating her alive. Two dogs pupils couldn't close because they'd stayed in absolute darkness for too long and their eyes could no longer focus. In addition to the dogs, the team also found 10 birds in cages. A blanket was thrown over the cages in the middle of the day, in the middle of a scorching summer. One had an eye hanging at the side of its face. Another bird's beak was so short and broken into two halves that there was no way possible that he could eat or drink. In total, 198 dogs, 10 budgies, one Lovebird, two cats, a dove, two rabbits and four cockatiels were confiscated. And it’s not the first case Reinet says she and the SPCA have come across.

title: "FREE TO GO" JUDGE (You be the Judge)
oneLiner: The man once tipped by President Jacob Zuma to become KZN’s top prosecutor has been accused of allowing dangerous criminals to walk free, despite strong cases against them.
summary: Pinetown magistrate Stanley Gumede, who last year had been earmarked to head the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA), despite a raft of misconduct charges levelled against him, has released two men charged with attempted murder after a bloody home invasion in Hillcrest in April 2013. CB aired a story about a surge in the number of home invasions in the affluent suburb. This particular case study involved the attack and robbery of the Sutherland family. The story included gruesome footage of the attack, which saw homeowner Ryan Sutherland stabbed repeatedly as men armed with knives and pangas rushed into his house. The story helped prompted the intervention of a special police task team to combat rampant crime in the Highway area. Despite high-quality CCTV footage that identified the attackers, witnesses that positively pointed them out, as well as their own confessions, Gumede released them on free bail because of an allegedly shaky case against them. Ian Prentis (PI) was hired by Ryan Sutherland to work closely with the police to make sure the case was solid. He says they did everything by the book. He said the case against the two suspects had been “watertight”.“The docket was handled impeccably and, considering all the damning evidence, it was an open and shut case”. “The state opposed the granting of bail vigorously because of the violent nature of this crime. The suspects also had no permanent employment or fixed address. Because the case against them was so strong, and conviction was likely, they might flee and, despite all of this, the magistrate released them on free bail. Now they are in the wind. It is unthinkable,” he said. Ryan says he and his family are now living in the fear that the criminals will come back to “get “rid” of the witnesses. “Try to catch those guys again – that’s never going to happen. They are never going to pitch for their trial,” Sutherland added.

The Allocation of Long Term Fishing Licences granted form anything between 8 to 15 years expired on the 31 December and the Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries took to the last possible day to make the announcement. Of the 3 490 applicants only 600 licences were granted in seven different sectors. The Traditional line fishing was the worse effected with only 215 licences granted out of the 1 556 applications. From the 400 established traditional line fishing licenses, only 105 previous right holders were awarded fishing rights while 100 new entrants were awarded rights. After a massive outcry which saw hawkers and Line Fishermen standing togther for the first time in history, DAFF finally backed down an issued a moratorium, fishermen who did not get their rights renewed can temporarily go back to sea while their applications are reviewed. Its a bureaucratic stall, there are only 18 permits that can be issue and 115 rights holders lost their permits. In the mean time fishermen in other sectors like shark demersal and tuna pole fishing are still sitting in the same situation.

title: Slumdog Mountaineer
oneLiner: A dog named Rupee and his trek to Base Camp Everest
summary: Joanne Lefson and her dog, Oscar made a name for themselves travelling around the world to promote the cause of homeless dogs. And we did a story or two on her travels with Oscar. Joanne is passionate about dogs and Oscar whom she rescued from a shelter was literally her true love, then tragedy struck Joanne while reversing her car ran into Oscar and killed him. Expedition Mutt Everest was to be Oscar's last voyage - a journey 'the top of the world' to ask the Gods above to bestow a loving home on the homeless friends below. When tragedy struck in January, the plans stopped. Joanne: Actually, life as I knew it, stopped. If Everest is the highest place you can be, the months that followed Oscar's death couldn't have been the lowest in my life. In August she returned to the remote Northern region of Leh She has a donkey sanctuary there that was set up 5 years ago and returns each year to help out and see how things are going. Then during a random visit to a dumpsite in India …. Joanne “ to document conditions for these animals as part of a documentary for a Mumbai network, a small dog ran to me and collapsed beneath my shadow. He was skin, bones and right on death's doorstep. How could I turn away. I took him in, and found a temporary home for him with the sanctuary caretaker. It was only when I returned to Cape Town that I began to wonder if there was some greater karmic connection to the events that had occurred. Dogs in those areas are so afraid of people- and this little pup had run to me as if we had met before. Did Oscar send him to me to stop the tears? Then, I wondered, perhaps Rupee could take the lead and complete the Expedition in Oscar's honor. After all, he was a Himalayan dog and who better to take the message straight to the top than a homeless dog; the epitomy of the underdog that Oscar spent his life trying to promote...”

summary: This week saw the preliminary start of the historic commission of enquiry into the causes of vigilante justice in the township of Khayelitsha. The main work of the enquiry is to take place in March next year but it will be a commission which will have relevance for the whole of South Africa because mob justice is on the increase. Three suspects burn to death because they are suspected of stealing. These scenes should horrify every single South African, however desensitised they are. Often the mob gets the wrong person in any event. The common narrative is that the communities are sick and tired of crime in their area and the lack of police response. But is it as simple as this? What other layers contribute to this phenomena and what are the short and long term impacts on the community? The enquiry was commissioned by Helen Zille after having her hand forced by the controversial Social Justice Coalition, an NGO situated in Khayelitsha. Already there has been controversy because the police refuse to participate in the commission after being forced to do so. They even took this matter to the constitutional court, but lost.

oneLiner: Dodgy dealers are still turning back the clocks on second hand cars – old AND new! Carte Blanche exposes an industry that’s gone hi-tech to dupe buyers.
summary: It’s not a new phenomenon – Carte Blanche has been reporting on it for 17 years! What is new, is that dodgy mechanics are using more sophisticated technology that makes it much harder to detect tampered odometers. BUT that doesn’t mean that it isn’t happening any more. CARTE BLANCHE GOES EXPOSES A NEW BREED OF CAR CLOCKERS.

title: Don't Blame Facebook
oneLiner: Social Media Faux Pas
summary: Don't Blame Facebook tracks down people who have made some of the most extraordinary faux-pas on Facebook and other social media in the past few years. The programme discovers how sharing too much information online can have disastrous consequences, and reveals how these people's lives have been affected in the aftermath of their online 'fails'. In the first special, we saw the friends arrested on terror charges at a US airport after a joke tweet, and the McDonald’s employee who went to jail after hacking an international superstar’s Facebook page. Then there was the model arrested in her pyjamas when police burst into her home investigating a suspicion that she was harassing a celebrity. In this all new second programme, we find out what happens when a troll goes too far, when private photos end up where they shouldn’t, and see one young boy land himself in a truck load of trouble.

title: Metro Corruption
oneLiner: Port Elizabeth residents are taking a stand against soaring rates that they believed is linked to rampant corruption in the Metro.
summary: More than 3000 businesses and individuals in the Nelson Mandela metro are planning to take a stand and withhold 50 million rand in rates over the next four months in an effort to break their stranglehold... People in PE have had enough of the corruption in the Metro. On the 15th of October they plan to start handing in over 3000 disputes with the metro - which will result in over 50 million rand a month being with held in rates. It's a proactive citizenry initiative in defiance of the high levels of corruption. Rates in the metro have increased by between 30 and 270% and its killing off businesses and destroying any future prospects of investment. A walmer based hairdresser is paying R12000 a month in rates and a bed and breakfast in the same suburb has to cough up R26000 pm. And while businesses suffer an ANC leader and his cronies seem to be raking in the cash and behave as if they are untouchable. Nceba Faku (the former mayor and now regional organiser of the ANC for the Eastern Cape Province) and his millionaire businessman friend Mr Jeeva owe the municipality 36 million in rates and electricity but there is no effort to recover the money. The metro also sold Mr Jeeva the Ponte building for 2.8 million and now rent it back for 10 million pa. And in a tender scandal the metro over paid by 100 million for an electronics system for the municipal buses and when the new municipal manager Dr Lindiwe questioned this she was threatened with her life and pushed out.

title: Lucas Sithole: Wheelchair tennis (Sithole vs Watts)
oneLiner: We meet the man who made history as the first man from Africa to win a US open tennis championship
summary: Lucas Sithole is a 27-year-old triple amputee, meaning he has no legs and only one arm. Despite his disability, Sithole is arguably one of South Africa’s newest superstars – on the sports field and the recording studio. Earlier this year, Sithole won the US Open Grand slam 2013, the 2013 British Open and defeated the World No 1 at the ACSA SA Open Super series. Sithole is now officially the second ranked wheelchair tennis player in the world and the first man from Africa to win a singles US Open title of any kind.
caseStudies: Lucas Sithole

title: TACKLING CRIME IN TOTI (Toti Wave)
oneLiner: Residents of the seaside town of Amanzimtoti, say they are being besieged by crime and that their local police don’t seems to care and are sometimes even involved.
summary: At a recent joint Sector 1 and 2 public meeting, a vote of No Confidence in the Amanzimtoti SAPS was tabled and carried. Many issues were raised, including but not limited to, the following: • Refusal to open cases and/or issue case numbers; • Slow or no Response to call-outs - No/or lack of Accountability; • Failure to adhere to basic police procedure and/or Police Officers in breach of their employment contract; • Failure to charge alleged, identified criminals; • Abuse/misuse of power and/or Government property; • Police officers involved in criminal activities.

title: High flying cigarette smugglers
oneLiner: Imagine getting a SARS bill for 45 Million that you know nothing about - one mans nightmare after high profile smugglers hijacked his import company.
summary: Like most of us Errol Mommsen wants to make a living and take care of his family. So with a partner he started an import business that focuses on cigarettes. He got all the paperwork in place and his operation was legit. Soon after bringing his first few containers in he was approached to help a company owned by Yusuf Deedat to bring in a few containers? They paid the duties and it all ran smoothly. He heard nothing further. Then several months later he started receiving bills that totalled 45 million rand in outstanding customs duties for cigarettes he never imported. On investigation he discovered that the cigarettes were imported by Deedat on his name, charging the duties to him. Strange though that the containers were released without the duties being paid? But then Deedat is linked to Ernest Zuma and Paul De Robbillard who together are also directors of Fastjet. Errol can't get help and has spent 2 million on legal fees already, neither the NPA nor SARS want to help him and no action is being taken against the perpetrators.

title: Wedded Wanderers
oneLiner: A new study reveals the secrets of female infidelity and looks at the rise in online sites for married people who are looking.
summary: Browse around on the internet and you will be shocked to discover how many new sites there are that cater strictly for married people who are looking for a little fun on the side. The biggest of these is AshleyMadison an international site that has country based sites around the world - including South Africa. The site claims to have more than 20 million members worldwide. It is run by Noel Bilderman based in Canada whose wife, Amanda, is South African. If we send a cameraman Noel is more than happy to talk to us about the "success" of his concept. His website and particularly his Cougarlife site has also become the subject of a research project and a book being written by Marlene Wasserman (Dr Eve) who has drawn on the South African membership for her research into cyber infidelity. She says the female infidelity figures are astonishing - it will make you look at women in whole different light. I have arranged talk time with her for this afternoon to get more information on this aspect. 3 potential case studies have already been identified but of course we need to find creative ways to shoot these interviews as they are still married and looking! And have children, colleagues etc...

summary: On the 12th of October the 9th in a series of murders of Krejcir associates was killed in a hit just around the corner from the Bedford Centre in Bedfordview. This time it was Sam Issa, a Lebanese national who has lived here in South Africa for 16 years. It's alleged that he paid Krejcir's million rand bail in Pretoria last year (and never repaid it) and that he was owed around 4 million rand for cocaine by Krejcir. Both men were also eyeing taking over the Teasers strip clubs and there seems to have been some rivalry over this. Sam aka "Scarface" was also allegedly bad mouthing Krejcir who owed him 5 million. The word on the street is that this is the motive for the hit. He has also previously paid bail for Agglioti. New evidence - we have affidavits from two different individuals who claim to have been asked to do hits for Radovan. We have the pictures sent to them by Radovan and we also have affidavits from one of the individuals in Prague who was meant to be killed. He also provides a threatening letter. In addition how is Radovan getting away with running a loan business if he is not registered with the FSB? And how is it possible that 18 months after arriving in SA on false passports with a husband who is on the interpol red list that Katherina Krejcir has a SA ID and permanent residence. We have a copy of her ID. All their businesses and properties are in her name. Also who is Colonel Samba from the Bedfordview police station and why has he been seen having meals with Krejcir in Bedfordview restaurants?

Tomorrow the family have to fly back to Malaysia to give evidence. They have been let down by the govt who promised 24 hour protection so there is an element of danger. And they are conflicted as well because they know that their evidence will probably result in the death sentence of the criminals. They are totally apposed to the death sentence but the family will make a stand and ask that the criminals are not sentenced to death. I have spent two hours with Sham Moodlier the father and he is an amazing person.

It is widely believed that the problems afflicting the NPA began with the suspension and subsequent dismissal of Pikoli in 2009.

title: MedRegs
oneLiner: Easy targets but no magic bullet
summary: The insert starts with beautiful images of San bushmen with a voice over describing how the San bushmen discovered that Hoodia, grown in the Kalahari, suppressed appetite and fuelled their energy to boost them for their hunting expeditions. In 1997 the CSIR isolated the ingredient in Hoodia known as P57 which is responsible for its appetite suppressant effect and obtained the patent. Hoodia products exploded around the world. It was seen as the silver bullet. Its virtues made famous by celebrities such as Nicole Richie. The CSIR released licenses to companies such as Pfizer and later Lever Brothers who spent hundreds of millions of rands on synthesising the product to be used as an appetite suppressant. The study was dropped for safety reasons. Despite no clinical trials to support Hoodia as the magic bullet appetite suppressant, around the world it is still being sold in huge quantities. In 2002 the CSIR officially recognised the San's rights over Hoodia, allowing them to take 3% of the profits. Some producers in South Africa have been granted a license to grow the plant. Controversially no money has passed hands to the San because the department of environmental affairs has still to get parliament to sign the benefit sharing agreement. It's been on the table for over two years now. So there are South African producers who are making a mint and yet paying no percentages over. This story could be potentially damaging to the government since after all we are in the run up to the elections. Who knows, perhaps after this insert (if commissioned) is aired, that agreement will be signed off. Against this backdrop we describe just how many fakesters there are out there - both overseas and here - who claim the amazing results from Hoodia and who often don't have any Hoodia ingredients in their products. Let it be said that Hoodia in large dosages does appear to work but there can be health dangers.

title: Beachwolf

The hyenas that were there were either killed while crossing the main road (have footage) to get to the seal colony or left to move further inland. Now Ingrid suspects that 2 of her study animals Tosca (Breeding Female) and Alaika have moved into the Atlas Bay area but she is not sure. Alaika has a collar and Ingrid tracks her to the atlas bay area, but is Tosca there as well. She finds evidence of cubs around the den but is not sure whose they are. Ingrid sets up camera traps to find out the truth, but it is destroyed by young Hyena (Caught on camera) and the den is vacated. (AS hyena are known to do) Ingrid thinks they have moved to Jungle Den, a popular den site within the same territory and on inspection finds it is indeed occupied. Once again she sets up her Camera Traps and while she waits Ingrid needs to check on Oblixa another Hyena who has moved into the old German Ghost town Elizabeth Bay. Ingrid returns to retrieve her traps and watches in amazement as the little cubs come out of den possibly for the first time ever, in the dead of night. She identifies Alaika and is very excited that this territory is being used.

title: Big Fish
oneLiner: From a background of poverty and gangs we meet the best marine guide in the country
summary: When marine guide Dalfrenzo Laing is giving you the intimate details of the sea barnacle’s astonishing sex life, you would have no clue that his back ground is one of poverty, drugs, and gangs….if it wasn’t for his scars and gold teeth. Growing up in Napier in the Western Cape, jobs were limited and working as a petrol pump attendant looked like as far as he would go. Then in a matter of an hour he received some of the worst news and got one of the best opportunities; Dalfrenzo was retrenched from the petrol station he worked at and as he was leaving a customer who worked as a tourism officer asked him if he wanted to attend the first marine guiding course in the country! Dalfrenzo said yes despite the fact he had not a clue what a marine nature reserve was…… That was a few years ago. Today he is the head guide on the De Hoop Nature Reserve on the south coast’s whale route, and he’s one of SA’s best marine guides, a breed even scarcer than the whales he points out. A feel good story for December that will take us from Dalfrenzo’s back ground in Napier/ Robertson, with his mother a singe parent, his struggles with epilepsy, and then later his heavy three years in drugs and gangs to the beautiful De Hoop nature reserve and the sex life of a sea barnacle.

title: An SA First - Earth's Blast from the Past
oneLiner: How a South African scientific team have solved the mystery of the Tutankamen scarab
summary: The craftsmen who carved the scarab forming the centerpiece of Tutankhamen’s burial pectoral knew they were handling something extraordinary. Being tuned into the universe beyond our solar system, they probably also knew what they were handling was extra-terrestrial, too. Now, a South African-led group of scientists has proved for the first time that this remarkable stone is, indeed, from outer space. It came to earth 28 millions years ago, a remnant of a comet that exploded over the desert in south west Egypt, spattering this and millions of other rock fragments that today are a treasure trove of another sort. For the scientists, these fragments give us an insight into the composition of the universe soon after it was formed billions of years ago. The stone, named Hypatia after the first well-known female mathematician and astronomer, will reveal the secrets of the pre-solar nebula, says an excited David Block, Professor of Applied Mathematics and Astronomy at the University of the Witwatersrand. The only other known case of a comet exploding onto a planet was in 1994 when comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 smashed into Jupiter, giving us spectacular footage viewed by millions worldwide. But it was impossible for scientists to get at the rocks, being so far away. A ten minute piece that brings cosmic science down to earth, linked to Egyptian archaeology and a first for South African scientists. Using footage I have of Egypt and interviews with Shoemaker re the comet named after him, and new interviews to be filmed of David Block and some of the other members of the South African team, this piece will portray a sense of wonder and a feel-good message of South Africans leading in the tough world of science.

title: Water Wars
oneLiner: 40 meter sinkholes, underground dolomitic explosions and a farmer ruined by municipal water extraction.
summary: For 4 decades Koot Geldenhuys' family has owned 4000 hectares in the Zeerust district in the North West Province. They sit on a rich water source and have farmed successfully. In 2005 the municipality which had serious water shortages approached them to extract water from the farm and registered a servitude. In exchange they had to stop farming and the municipality paid them R800k to register the servitude plus they agreed to help them set up an eco-tourism venture. The family kept their side of the agreement but the municipality squandered the money for the eco-tourism venture on a trip to Brazil before the world cup and now they are asking for their R800k back saying the contract was not approved. And top things off they can't farm due to the agreement, they have no real income and the municipality threatens them, tells the community they are to blame for the water shortages and as a result they have residents threatening them with guns and breaking into their property. And to top things off even further they have 40 metre sinkholes forming and underground dolomitic explosions due to the extensive extraction which is not sanctioned by DWAF. That's right - its not recorded and the government is doing nothing about it.

title: Spare The Rod
oneLiner: Should you spank your child if they are naughty? A new draft law is being proposed which would ban parents from spanking their children. Will you be in danger of breaking the law?
summary: Currently controversy is raging as the new draft law banning parents from spanking their children is being debated. It is a highly sensitive issue that immediately sparks emotion amongst parents and children alike. The way we are disciplined as children is intrinsic to the way we are brought up and to how we view rearing our own children. Was the experience positive or negative? Do we become our parents or are we trying to change the way things were. The anxiety to be the perfect parent is part of the 21st century preoccupation and discipline is key to 'getting it right'. What is the difference between a spanking and a beating and is a spanking more acceptable? The churches are up in arms, quoting Proverbs (13:24): “He who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him is careful to discipline him.” But, Childline South Africa has welcomed the new draft law, due to high levels of violence in the country. There are many who believe that such a law will not necessarily decrease high levels of child abuse. Opinions are divided on whether spanking is helpful or harmful to a child's behaviour. Since 1979, internationally, many countries have made parental corporal punishment illegal, but still.. Australia, Canada, South Africa, United Kingdom, United States allow this. On the other hand, many scientific researchers and child welfare organizations oppose child corporal punishment. Some studies have suggested that it does not benefit the child, and can encourage issues like anxiety, alcohol abuse, or dependence and externalizing problems. Various other repercussions have also been claimed. This story will be visualised through beautifully filmed evocative images of children and families across the social spectrum, creating another layer that highlights why this issue is so volatile and potentially explosive. The visuals of the children will be stylised, depicting their vulnerability and innocence to the world with which they they are expected to interact.
experts: Ms. Bathabile Dlamini Ms. Lumka Oliphant Ms. Carol Bower Ms. Shaheda Omar Mr. Errol Naidoo Mr. Khaye Nkwanyana Mr. Evangelistic minister Mr. Childline representative

title: BUILDER BLUES
oneLiner: Homeowners are left fixing up badly build new homes, while building subcontractors liquidate thanks to one construction company in Durban who finds excuses not to pay its bills.
summary: SUMMARY According to the National Home Builders Ass, the biggest hurdle to raising the standard in the construction of homes in South Africa is the non payment of building sub contractors. Here’s what they mean..... CONSUMER CASE STUDY: Brian Almanza and his wife took their life savings and bought their dream home in Hillcrest. Advertised as “A secure and safe family estate”, 101 Accuts Estate was the home the couple envisioned growing old in. They even got permission to establish an olive grove surrounding the dam which was supposed to be positioned in front of their lot. (His wife is Italian, He’s Sicilian). But just a few months into the building of their home it all went pear shaped. The building wasn’t straight, the floors uneven and things just went from bad to worse. Eventually Brian brought in his own engineer to try and fix up the place. But eventually even he “threw in the towel “saying he couldn’t work with the developer (Grid Construction) on sight manger and builder. Desperate, Brian had to let Grid do the finishing’s. NB John Payne, the engineer has kept a visual record of all the problems and is willing to talk us through it all. The home is 7 months old and is cracking, water pours in through the bedroom window, pain and plaster is falling off the walls. When the put in plug points they just smashed a hole in the poor guys marble tiles. BUT most importantly Brian is worried about security. There basically isn’t any. There is a chicken wire type fence which they have nailed on from the outside - where the robbers can unscrew them. There are big hole where thieves have dug holes under the fence. Brian has a business that takes him overseas often and he is terrified his wife and kids are going to be attacked. Shame the poor guy got all teary talking about his frustrations and fears – but in a manly way. You really feel for him. He will be great on camera.

summary: Cape Town, South Africa 2014 Becoming 2014 ‘s World Design Capital is a major achievement for the City of Cape Town….on the face of it a programme on this achievement could seem like another Top Billing light as a pancake insert…. it’s anything but that. This selection is recognition of the city of Cape Town’s effective and creative efforts to use design a tool for progress and the economic impact will be considerable. It can be compared to a year long World Cup Event …..creatives, entrepreneurs will be coming across the globe to learn and collaborate with local – but no less world class- talent. But this is not just an achievement for Cape Town but South Africa. Being World Design Capital in 2010 saw Seoul becoming a more considerate, more liveable city. Case in point - the Cheonggyecheon highway, instead of simply replacing an ugly 1970s-style highway with another highway, they restored the river over which the highway had paved, making the most beautiful urban park in the centre of the city – at the same time reducing pollution, temperatures and traffic. I would like to propose a one hour special on this Cape Town World Design Capital 2014 to be flighted either during December when Joburgers ( and a good portion of the rest of the country) camp out in the Cape or for the 5th January ( a pre record). title: Toxins for Tusks
oneLiner: With 41 elephants recently poisoned in Zimbabwe, and over 30 000 elephants reported poached last year throughout Africa - experts warn that the slaughter is heading our way.
summary: The 41 elephants died after drinking from a waterhole in Zimbabwe's Hwange game reserve (the consequent impact on predators and scavengers is huge). Between 30,000 to 40,000 elephant are being poached around Africa every year. While everyone's understandably watching rhino numbers deteriorate, the warning from elephant experts at the conservation / poaching coalface in East and Southern Africa is that the lifting of the ivory ban five years ago created this situation - and that South Africa's elephants could well be next in the cross-hairs (this news bodes ill for the government's recent decision to sell SA's rhino horn). In light of the claim by one of South Africa's most recognised elephant authorites that South Africa does not have an overpopulation - this could be devastating news - especially as we cannot protect our rhinos as it is. We tell the story of increasing and massive demand for ivory - with armed militia around the continent feeding that demand in order to pay for their weapons. With the help of undercover footage from China, and interviews with Africa's most knowledgable elephant watchers - we pull back the branches, explore the new trend in ivory poaching in 2013, and if the threat to SA's elephants is real.

title: One Man & a South African Parrot
oneLiner: His tireless work to save the only surviving South African parrot from extinction has led the Nat Geo Society to name Steve Boyes South Africa's only Emerging Explorer for 2013
summary: There are maybe 900 Cape Parrots left in South Africa - in a tiny patch of the Eastern Cape. It is for his efforts in working virtually single-handedly to save them from extinction - plus for his work in preserving wilderness, like with his Okavango delta conservation work as seen on CB - that local ornithologist Steve Boyes has been named by the National Geographic Society as the only South African on the global list of Emerging Explorers for 2013. He has photographed and nursed these birds - decimated by the destruction of their favourite landscape, and disease which that destruction has caused. So obsessed and passionate is Steve with - and about - these birds that he is moving his expectant wife from the city to a farm in Hogsback - the epicentre of the bird's dwindling range - just to be among them. When he's not treating them in his lab, he is working with locals, major corporations and global NGOs to rescue this parrot. His child will be born to the tune of parrot-song. This is a proudly south african story - in which our national parrot will be saved by the resurrection of our national tree - the yellowwood (the fruit of which it needed to thrive, and in which it nests). An initiative also driven by Steve. We will tell the story through stunning visuals of these beautiful birds in flight and close-up on the 'treatment table' - a story of rare passion that will leave a lump in the throat, as we get a glimpse of the beauty and character Steve sees in the critically endangered Cape Parrot, which we will show as a symbol of local resurrection. Plse note this story will not duplicate the okavango story at all...

title: FLYAWAY COSTS
oneLiner: Airline tickets keep going up as ACSA goes on an infrastructure spending binge while airlines and consumers have to fit the bill.
summary: ACSA is about to spend 40 billion rand on a terminal in the middle of OR Tambo as part of their 10 year plan that they don't want to share with airlines and despite airlines trying to get information on the plan and to weigh in on it they are forging ahead. It falls into a flawed funding model - the more they spend in terms of capex the more profit they make. But the more they spend the more money they need to recoup from us the consumer and that hits the bottom line of many airlines and every consumer who buys an air ticket. it's also being cited as one of the reasons low cost airlines have gone bust. Which begs the question - does ACSA have our best interests at heart? They are also spending 400 million on IT over the next 5 years and many insiders believe that at the very least the re cabling which makes up 15% of that budget its unnecessary and a waste of money. A whistleblower has come forward from XON, who have the tender for internal communications within ACSA. There are allegations of fraud within XON - nepotism, they are only fronting BEE, under pay their workers. Millions of ACSA’s public funds are unaccounted for with regards to their contract with XON and they are now redoing cabling which is unnecessary for the next few years. An upgrade may be necessary in the future but in this economic climate and given that there is existing cabling - why are we spending the money?

title: African Entrepreneurs
oneLiner: They are young, they are african and they are full of ideas these are our entrepreneurs of tomorrow
summary: The story of how William Kamkwamba, using junkyard scraps built a windmill and brought electricity to his rural Malawian village is iconic. In fact the book he wrote, “The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind’, was not only a best seller but named on Amazon.com’s top 10 books of 2009. Footage of William travelling to the USA and visiting different wind farms is too good to be true, this young boy telling these farmers what he did, their increduality. William is now at Dartmouth studying engineering, having progressed from testing as a 4th-grader (at the age of 20) to the Ivy League in just 3 years. William has his sights set on building utility-scale wind power projects to dramatically improve the electricity infrastructure in Malawi. A large part of William’s success today is because of the African Leadership Academy, a non- profit organisation dedicated to launching projects and transforming dreams that they believe will transform Africa. Their mission is to identify exceptional young entrepreneurs who are leading by example and underscore their ability to significantly shape the future of Africa. To this end they have an annual competition for Africa’s potential greatest young entrepreneurs between ages of 15 and 22. A story on these young entrepreneurs going for the big prize… ALA have lots of footage of them both scouting for applicants and finalists. title: Ostrich Onslaught
oneLiner: A once thriving export industry is collapsing under a EU export ban. More than 50 000 ostriches have been culled since avian flu was detected and it's spreading and has been described as a crisis.
summary: South Africa's beleaguered ostrich industry, already collapsing under a European Union export ban as it waits for at least three months for bird flu tests to prove negative, has suffered another blow after the virus was found in the Breede River to Great Brak River area last week. Since the H5N2 virus (avian flu) was first detected 50 000 ostriches have been slaughtered. The government has paid out R50 million in compensation to farmers and the provincial agriculture department initiated a retraining programme to save 20 000 jobs threatened by the crisis. We get up close and personal with a farming community on the verge of collapse - the ostrich farming has been part of South African culture for generations - it's colourful, the farmers full of character and so are their towns.

title: Michaeli Mycroft (Chaeli Mycroft)
oneLiner: Michaeli Mycroft is an inspiring story of a young woman who has just won the prestigious International Children's Peace Prize in Amsterdam for the work she has done in helping disabled children.
summary: We did a story on her in 2004, but the Chaeli Foundation has grown substantially in the past 8 years. They now see to the needs of over 3000 disabled children a year and they are a dynamic organization that is changing lives in a profound way. In November 2011 Michaeli was awarded the prestigious International Children’s Peace Prize in Amsterdam for her remarkable acts in assisting and defending and the rights of disabled children. At the end of April she will be attending the World Summit of Nobel Peace Laureates in Chicago where she will be the very first recipient of the Activism Award. (This is an award from the Laureates and not the Nobel Prize Organization) This would be a follow on a story but a chance to catch up with a remarkable individual in her fight to help disabled children in South Africa.
